        for v34 in 0..v8
            v45.push(v1[(v36 + v34) as usize])
        if v32 == 2
            return t2(v12: k1(v1: v45), v18: v36 + v8)
        let v46 = f21()
        var v22 = ""
        for v34 in 0..v8
            let v3 = v45[v34 as usize]
            if v3 == 10
                v22 = v22 + "\n"
            elif v3 == 13
                v22 = v22 + "\r"
            elif v3 == 9
                v22 = v22 + "\t"
            elif v3 >= 32 and v3 < 127
                v22 = v22 + copy(v46[(v3 - 32) as usize])
            else
                fail x2(v13: v36 + v34)
        return t2(v12: k2(v22: v22), v18: v36 + v8)
    if v32 == 4
        var v23: List[t1] = []
        for _v47 in 0..v8
            let v48 = try f22(v1, v36)
            v36 = v48.v18
            v23.push(v48.v12)
        return t2(v12: k3(v23: v23), v18: v36)
    if v32 == 5
        var v37: List[t1] = []
        var v38: List[t1] = []
        var v49: List[i64] = []
        for v34 in 0..v8
            let v50 = v36
            let v51 = try f22(v1, v36)
            var v52: List[i64] = []
            for v53 in v50..v51.v18
                v52.push(v1[v53 as usize])
            if v34 > 0 and f11(&v49, &v52) >= 0
                fail x2(v13: v50)
            v49 = v52
            let v54 = try f22(v1, v51.v18)
            let _v55 = v51.v18

            v38.push(v54.v12)

        let v48 = try f22(v1, v36)
        let v56 = v48.v18
        return t2(v12: k5(v26: v8, v27: Box(v48.v12)), v18: v56)
    let v42 = v1[v19 as usize] & 31
    if v42 > 24 or (v42 == 24 and v8 < 32)
        fail x2(v13: v19)
    return t2(v12: k6(v12: v8), v18: v36)

# Decode a whole buffer holding exactly one deterministic item.
pub fn f23(v1: &[i64]) -> t1 ! x2
    let v48 = try f22(v1, 0)
    if v48.v18 != (v1.len() as i64)
        fail x2(v13: v48.v18)
    return v48.v12

# ---------------- JCS (RFC 8785) ----------------
# Json values with integer numbers only: an integer is printed the way
# ECMAScript prints the equal double, which for |v| <= 2^53 is its decimal
# form; larger magnitudes trap (I-JSON range). Non-integer numbers need
# spec (no f64 bit access for the shortest round-trip form).
pub kind t3
    k7
    k8(v12: bool)
    k9(v12: i64)
    k10(v22: text)
    k11(v23: List[t3])
    k12(v24: List[text], v25: List[t3])

fn f24(v12: i64) -> text
    let v57 = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    return copy(v57[((v12 >> 12) & 15) as usize]) + copy(v57[((v12 >> 8) & 15) as usize]) + copy(v57[((v12 >> 4) & 15) as usize]) + copy(v57[(v12 & 15) as usize])

# JSON string per RFC 8785 3.2.2.2: escape " \ and U+0000..U+001F (short
# forms \b \t \n \f \r, else \u00xx lowercase); everything else verbatim.
pub fn f25(v22: &text) -> text
    var v4 = "\""
    for v14 in v22.chars()
        let v3 = v14[0] as i64
        if v14 == "\""
            v4 = v4 + "\\\""
        elif v14 == "\\"
            v4 = v4 + "\\\\"
        elif v3 == 8
            v4 = v4 + "\\b"
        elif v3 == 9
            v4 = v4 + "\\t"
        elif v3 == 10
            v4 = v4 + "\\n"
        elif v3 == 12
            v4 = v4 + "\\f"
        elif v3 == 13
            v4 = v4 + "\\r"
        elif v3 < 32
            v4 = v4 + "\\u" + f24(v3)
        else
            v4 = v4 + v14
    return v4 + "\""

# UTF-16 code units of a UTF-8 text (sort key of RFC 8785 3.2.3).
pub fn f26(v22: &text) -> List[i64]
    var v2: List[i64] = []
    var v5: usize = 0
    while v5 < v22.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        let v3 = v22[v5] as i64
        var v58 = v3
        var v8: usize = 1
        if v3 >= 240
            v58 = ((v3 & 7) << 18) | (((v22[v5 + 1] as i64) & 63) << 12) | (((v22[v5 + 2] as i64) & 63) << 6) | ((v22[v5 + 3] as i64) & 63)
            v8 = 4
        elif v3 >= 224
            v58 = ((v3 & 15) << 12) | (((v22[v5 + 1] as i64) & 63) << 6) | ((v22[v5 + 2] as i64) & 63)
            v8 = 3
        elif v3 >= 192
            v58 = ((v3 & 31) << 6) | ((v22[v5 + 1] as i64) & 63)
            v8 = 2
        if v58 >= 65536
            let v59 = v58 - 65536
            v2.push(55296 + (v59 >> 10))
            v2.push(56320 + (v59 & 1023))
        else
            v2.push(v58)
        v5 += v8
    return v2

fn f27(v12: i64) -> text
    let _v17 = 1 / (if v12 <= 9007199254740992 and v12 >= -9007199254740992 then 1 else 0)
    return v12.tostr()

fn f28(v35: List[text]) -> text = "[" + ",".join(v35) + "]"

# Members sorted by UTF-16 code units of the keys; duplicate keys trap.
fn f29(v24: &[text], v25: List[text]) -> text
    var v60: List[List[i64]] = []
    for v34 in v24
        v60.push(f26(v34))
    var v39: List[usize] = []
    for v5 in 0..v24.len()
        var v40 = v39.len()
        v39.push(v5)
        while v40 > 0 and f11(&v60[v39[v40 - 1]], &v60[v5]) > 0 bound 16777216
            v39[v40] = v39[v40 - 1]
            v40 -= 1
        v39[v40] = v5
    for v40 in 1..v39.len()
        let _v17 = 1 / (if f11(&v60[v39[v40 - 1]], &v60[v39[v40]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var v35: List[text] = []
    for v5 in v39
        v35.push(f25(&v24[v5]) + ":" + copy(v25[v5]))
    return "{" + ",".join(v35) + "}"

pub fn f30(v40: &t3) -> text bound 64
    match v40
        k7 -> return "null"
        k8(v12: v12) -> return if v12 then "true" else "false"
        k9(v12: v12) -> return f27(v12)
        k10(v22: v22) -> return f25(v22)
        k11(v23: v23) -> return f28(v23.map(fn(v3: t3) => f30(&v3)))
        k12(v24: v24, v25: v25) -> return f29(v24, v25.map(fn(v3: t3) => f30(&v3)))

module enc

# Encodings (survey M8): base64 (RFC 4648), LEB128 varints with zigzag,
# deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1, core deterministic encoding)
# and the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785). Bytes are List[i64]
# 0..255 (core.bytes). Decoders reject every non-canonical input: padding
# or trailing bits in base64, overlong varints, non-shortest CBOR heads,
# indefinite lengths, unsorted or duplicate map keys.
# Not covered (needs spec, see vectors/SOURCE.md): CBOR and JCS floats (no
# f64 bit access in 5.15), CBOR integers beyond i64, decoding non-ASCII
# CBOR text (no text-from-UTF-8 built-in).

fn enc_cat(a: List[i64], b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- base64 (RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5) ----------------

fn b64_alpha(url: bool) -> List[text] = if url then "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_".chars() else "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/".chars()

# url: the URL-safe alphabet; pad: emit '=' padding.
pub fn b64_encode(b: &[i64], url: bool, pad: bool) -> text
    let a = b64_alpha(url)
    var s = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < b.len() bound 16777216
        let n = b.len() - i
        let x0 = b[i]
        let x1 = if n > 1 then b[i + 1] else 0
        let x2 = if n > 2 then b[i + 2] else 0
        let v = (x0 << 16) | (x1 << 8) | x2
        s = s + copy(a[((v >> 18) & 63) as usize]) + copy(a[((v >> 12) & 63) as usize])
        if n > 1
            s = s + copy(a[((v >> 6) & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        if n > 2
            s = s + copy(a[(v & 63) as usize])
        elif pad
            s = s + "="
        i += 3
    return s

error BadBase64(at: i64)

fn b64_val(c: i64, url: bool) -> i64
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 71
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c + 4
    if c == (if url then 45 else 43)
        return 62
    if c == (if url then 95 else 47)
        return 63
    return -1

# Strict decode: padding exactly as b64_encode(pad) would emit it, no
# whitespace, zero trailing bits (RFC 4648 section 3.5 canonical form).
pub fn b64_decode(s: &text, url: bool, pad: bool) -> List[i64] ! BadBase64
    var n = s.len_bytes()
    if pad
        if n % 4 != 0
            fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)
        if n > 0 and s[n - 1] == 61
            n -= 1
            if s[n - 1] == 61
                n -= 1
    elif n % 4 == 1
        fail BadBase64(at: n as i64)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var acc: i64 = 0
    var bits: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let v = b64_val(s[i] as i64, url)
        if v < 0
            fail BadBase64(at: i as i64)
        acc = ((acc << 6) | v) & 16777215
        bits += 6
        if bits >= 8
            bits -= 8
            o.push((acc >> bits) & 255)
        i += 1
    if bits > 0 and (acc & ((1 << bits) - 1)) != 0
        fail BadBase64(at: (n - 1) as i64)
    return o

# ---------------- LEB128 varints ----------------

pub fn uvarint(v: i64) -> List[i64]
    let _ok = 1 / (if v >= 0 then 1 else 0)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var x = v
    while x >= 128 bound 10
        o.push((x & 127) | 128)
        x = x >> 7
    o.push(x)
    return o

error BadVarint(at: i64)

pub struct VarOut
    v: i64
    next: i64

# Decode at off; rejects truncation, overlong forms (a final 0x00 byte after
# the first) and values above 2^63 - 1.
pub fn uvarint_decode(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> VarOut ! BadVarint
    var v: i64 = 0
    var sh: i64 = 0
    var i = off
    loop bound 10
        if i >= (b.len() as i64)
            fail BadVarint(at: i)
        let x = b[i as usize]
        if sh == 63 and x > 0
            fail BadVarint(at: i)
        v = v | ((x & 127) << sh)
        i += 1
        if x < 128
            if x == 0 and i - off > 1
                fail BadVarint(at: i - 1)
            return VarOut(v: v, next: i)
        sh += 7
    fail BadVarint(at: i)

pub fn zigzag(v: i64) -> i64 = if v >= 0 then 2 * v else 0 - 2 * (v + 1) - 1 + 2

pub fn unzigzag(z: i64) -> i64 = if z % 2 == 0 then z / 2 else 0 - (z - 1) / 2 - 1

# ---------------- Deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 4.2.1) ----------------

pub kind Cbor
    CInt(v: i64)
    CBytes(b: List[i64])
    CText(t: text)
    CArr(items: List[Cbor])
    CMap(keys: List[Cbor], vals: List[Cbor])
    CTag(tag: i64, item: Box[Cbor])
    CSimple(v: i64)

# Simple values: false 20, true 21, null 22, undefined 23.
pub const CBOR_FALSE: i64 = 20
pub const CBOR_TRUE: i64 = 21
pub const CBOR_NULL: i64 = 22
pub const CBOR_UNDEF: i64 = 23

# Shortest head for major type m and argument n >= 0.
pub fn cbor_head(m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    let mt = m << 5
    if n < 24
        return [mt | n]
    if n < 256
        return [mt | 24, n]
    if n < 65536
        return [mt | 25, n >> 8, n & 255]
    if n < 4294967296
        return [mt | 26, (n >> 24) & 255, (n >> 16) & 255, (n >> 8) & 255, n & 255]
    var o: List[i64] = [mt | 27]
    for k in 0..8
        o.push((n >> (8 * (7 - k))) & 255)
    return o

fn lex_cmp(a: &[i64], b: &[i64]) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len() and i < b.len() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return if a[i] < b[i] then -1 else 1
        i += 1
    if a.len() == b.len()
        return 0
    return if a.len() < b.len() then -1 else 1

fn enc_arr(n: usize, parts: List[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o = cbor_head(4, n as i64)
    for p in parts
        o = enc_cat(o, &p)
    return o

# Map: sort entries by the bytes of their encoded keys; a duplicate key
# traps (RFC 8949 5.6: deterministic encoders must not emit duplicates).
fn enc_map(ks: List[List[i64]], vs: List[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var idx: List[usize] = []
    for i in 0..ks.len()
        var j = idx.len()
        idx.push(i)
        while j > 0 and lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[i]) > 0 bound 16777216
            idx[j] = idx[j - 1]
            j -= 1
        idx[j] = i
    for j in 1..idx.len()
        let _ok = 1 / (if lex_cmp(&ks[idx[j - 1]], &ks[idx[j]]) < 0 then 1 else 0)
    var o = cbor_head(5, ks.len() as i64)
    for i in idx
        o = enc_cat(o, &ks[i])
        o = enc_cat(o, &vs[i])
    return o

fn enc_text(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    let b = bytes_of(t)
    return enc_cat(cbor_head(3, b.len() as i64), &b)

fn enc_int(v: i64) -> List[i64] = if v >= 0 then cbor_head(0, v) else cbor_head(1, -1 - v)

fn enc_bytes(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = cbor_head(2, b.len() as i64)
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn enc_simple(v: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if v < 24
        o.push(224 | v)
    else
        o.push(248)
        o.push(v)
    return o

fn enc_tag(t: i64, inner: List[i64]) -> List[i64] = enc_cat(cbor_head(6, t), &inner)

# Nesting depth is bounded by 64.
pub fn cbor_encode(c: &Cbor) -> List[i64] bound 64
    match c
        CInt(v: v) -> return enc_int(v)
        CBytes(b: b) -> return enc_bytes(b)
        CText(t: t) -> return enc_text(t)
        CArr(items: items) -> return enc_arr(items.len(), items.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CMap(keys: keys, vals: vals) -> return enc_map(keys.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)), vals.map(fn(x: Cbor) => cbor_encode(&x)))
        CTag(tag: tag, item: item) -> return enc_tag(tag, cbor_encode(item))
        CSimple(v: v) -> return enc_simple(v)

error BadCbor(at: i64)

pub struct CborOut
    v: Cbor
    next: i64

fn arg_of(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> VarOut ! BadCbor
    # argument of the head at off, shortest form enforced
    if off >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let ai = b[off as usize] & 31
    if ai < 24
        return VarOut(v: ai, next: off + 1)
    if ai > 27
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    let n = if ai == 24 then 1 else (if ai == 25 then 2 else (if ai == 26 then 4 else 8))
    if off + n >= (b.len() as i64)
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    var v: i64 = 0
    for k in 1..(n + 1)
        let x = b[(off + k) as usize]
        if k == 1 and n == 8 and x > 127
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        v = (v << 8) | x
    let lo = if ai == 24 then 24 else (if ai == 25 then 256 else (if ai == 26 then 65536 else 4294967296))
    if v < lo
        fail BadCbor(at: off)
    return VarOut(v: v, next: off + 1 + n)

fn ascii_table() -> List[text] = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~".chars()

# Decode one deterministic data item at off. Text must be ASCII here
# (needs spec: text from UTF-8 bytes); floats are refused.
pub fn cbor_decode_at(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> CborOut ! BadCbor bound 64
    let h = try arg_of(b, off)
    let m = b[off as usize] >> 5
    let n = h.v
    var p = h.next
    if m == 0
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: n), next: p)
    if m == 1
        return CborOut(v: CInt(v: -1 - n), next: p)
    if m == 2 or m == 3
        if p + n > (b.len() as i64)
            fail BadCbor(at: off)
        var bs: List[i64] = []

fn f35(v65: &t0, v66: &mut List[i64], v67: &mut List[i64], v68: i64, v69: i64, v11: usize, v10: usize)
    var v63: List[i64] = [v69]
    var v64: usize = 1
    while v64 > 0 bound 1000000
        v64 -= 1
        let v70 = v63[v64]
        if v67[v70 as usize] == v68
            continue
        v67[v70 as usize] = v68
        let v45 = v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize]
        if v45 == v36
            v64 = f34(&mut v63, v64, v70 + v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize + 1])
        if v45 == v35
            v64 = f34(&mut v63, v64, v70 + v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize + 2])
            v64 = f34(&mut v63, v64, v70 + v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize + 1])
        if v45 == v38 and v11 == 0
            v64 = f34(&mut v63, v64, v70 + 1)
        if v45 == v39 and v11 == v10
            v64 = f34(&mut v63, v64, v70 + 1)
        if v45 != v36 and v45 != v35 and v45 != v38 and v45 != v39
            v66.push(v70)

# Pike VM. full: the match must span the input; else any substring.
fn f36(v65: &t0, v46: &[i64], v71: bool) -> bool
    let v10 = v46.len()
    let v72 = v65.v40.len() / 3
    var v67: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..v72
        v67.push(-1)
    var v73: List[i64] = []
    var v68: i64 = 0
    f35(v65, &mut v73, &mut v67, v68, 0, 0, v10)
    # threads waiting for a multi-byte "." to finish: [pc, resume position]
    var v74: List[i64] = []
    var v11: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        for v70 in v73
            if v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize] == v37 and (not v71 or v11 == v10)
                return true
        if v11 >= v10
            break
        v68 += 1
        var v75: List[i64] = []
        var v76: List[i64] = []
        var v26: usize = 0
        while v26 < v74.len() bound 1000000
            if v74[v26 + 1] == (v11 + 1) as i64
                f35(v65, &mut v75, &mut v67, v68, v74[v26], v11 + 1, v10)
            else
                v76.push(v74[v26])
                v76.push(v74[v26 + 1])
            v26 += 2
        let v9 = v46[v11]
        for v70 in v73
            let v45 = v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize]
            let v8 = v65.v40[3 * v70 as usize + 1]
            let v77 = f33(v9)
            # a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
            # every (ASCII) range
            let v78 = v45 == v34 and f32(&v65.v41, v8 as usize, if v77 > 1 then -1 else v9)
            let v79 = (v45 == v32 and v9 == v8) or (v78 and v77 == 1) or (v45 == v33 and v77 == 1 and v9 != 10)
            if v79
                f35(v65, &mut v75, &mut v67, v68, v70 + 1, v11 + 1, v10)
            if (v45 == v33 or v78) and v77 > 1 and v11 + (v77 as usize) <= v10
                v76.push(v70 + 1)
                v76.push((v11 as i64) + f33(v9))
        # a search restarts only at code point boundaries
        if not v71 and (v11 + 1 >= v10 or v46[v11 + 1] < 128 or v46[v11 + 1] > 191)
            f35(v65, &mut v75, &mut v67, v68, 0, v11 + 1, v10)
        v73 = v75
        v74 = v76
        if v73.len() == 0 and v74.len() == 0 and v71
            return false
        v11 += 1
    return false

pub fn f37(v65: &t0, v5: &text) -> bool
    let v46 = f30(v5)
    return f36(v65, &v46, true)

pub fn f38(v65: &t0, v5: &text) -> bool
    let v46 = f30(v5)
    return f36(v65, &v46, false)

module fmt

# Locale-free formatting, parsing and a linear-time regex (survey M17,
# part 1). No locale, no host call: the same input gives the same text on
# every host.
# - Integers: any radix 2..36, sign, zero/space padding, digit grouping;
#   strict parsing that refuses overflow, empty digits and stray bytes
#   (like C++ from_chars: no whitespace, no "0x", lowercase or uppercase
#   digits).
# - Templates: "{}" takes the next argument, "{N}" argument N, "{{" and
#   "}}" are literal braces.
# - Regex: a Thompson NFA run as a Pike VM, so matching costs
#   O(len(pattern) * len(input)) and never backtracks (RE2's guarantee).
#   Syntax: literals, ".", [...] and [^...] with ranges, \d \w \s \D \W
#   \S, \n \t \r, escapes of metacharacters, * + ? and {m}, {m,},
#   {m,n} (m, n <= 1000), |, (...), (?:...), ^ and $ (the ends of the
#   whole input, no multiline mode). It matches bytes of the UTF-8 text;
#   "." takes one whole UTF-8 sequence except "\n". Class ranges are ASCII;
#   a negated class or \D \W \S takes any whole non-ASCII sequence. No
#   captures or backreferences (not regular).

const DIGITS: text = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"

error BadInt(at: i64)
error BadFormat(at: i64)
error BadRegex(at: i64)

# ---------------- integers ----------------

# Digits of v in radix r (2..36), lowercase, "-" for negatives; the full
# i64 range (the most negative value is handled without negating it).
pub fn int_to(v: i64, r: i64) -> text
    let ds = DIGITS.chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var s = ""
    var x = v
    while x != 0 bound 64
        let d = x % r
        let a = if d < 0 then 0 - d else d
        s = copy(ds[a as usize]) + s
        x = x / r
    return if v < 0 then "-" + s else s

pub fn int_dec(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 10)

pub fn int_hex(v: i64) -> text = int_to(v, 16)

fn digit_val(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 48
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 87
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 55
    return 99

# Strict parse in radix r: optional "+" or "-", then one or more digits,
# nothing else. Overflow of i64 is refused (BadInt at the digit).
pub fn int_parse(s: &text, r: i64) -> i64 ! BadInt
    let n = s.len_bytes()
    if n == 0
        fail BadInt(at: 0)
    var i: usize = 0
    var neg = false
    let c0 = s[0] as i64
    if c0 == 45 or c0 == 43
        neg = c0 == 45
        i = 1
    if i >= n
        fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
    # accumulate as a negative number: -2^63 fits, 2^63 does not
    var acc: i64 = 0
    let lim = (0 - 9223372036854775807 - 1)
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let d = digit_val(s[i] as i64)
        if d >= r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        if acc < (lim + d) / r
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        let m = acc * r
        if m < lim + d
            fail BadInt(at: i as i64)
        acc = m - d
        i += 1
    if not neg
        if acc == lim
            fail BadInt(at: (n - 1) as i64)
        return 0 - acc
    return acc

pub fn int_parse_dec(s: &text) -> i64 ! BadInt = int_parse(s, 10)

# Pad on the left to w code points with fill (one character).
pub fn pad_left(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = copy(fill) + o
        n += 1
    return o

pub fn pad_right(s: &text, w: i64, fill: &text) -> text
    var o = copy(s)
    var n = s.chars().len() as i64
    while n < w bound 1000000
        o = o + copy(fill)
        n += 1
    return o

# Zero padding after the sign: zero_pad(-42, 6) = "-00042".
pub fn zero_pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    let s = int_dec(v)
    let z = "0"
    if v < 0
        let cs = s.chars()
        var body = ""
        for i in 1..cs.len()
            body = body + copy(cs[i])
        return "-" + pad_left(&body, w - 1, &z)
    return pad_left(&s, w, &z)

# Group decimal digits by three with sep: group_dec(-1234567, ",") =
# "-1,234,567".
pub fn group_dec(v: i64, sep: &text) -> text
    let cs = int_dec(v).chars()
    let start: usize = if v < 0 then 1 else 0
    let nd = cs.len() - start
    var o = if v < 0 then "-" else ""
    for k in 0..nd
        if k > 0 and (nd - k) % 3 == 0
            o = o + copy(sep)
        o = o + copy(cs[start + k])
    return o

# ---------------- templates ----------------

pub fn format(t: &text, args: &[text]) -> text ! BadFormat
    let cs = t.chars()
    let n = cs.len()
    var o = ""
    var next: usize = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < n bound 1000000
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        if c == "{"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "{"
                o = o + "{"
                i += 2
            else
                var j = i + 1
                var idx: i64 = -1
                while j < n and cs[j] != "}" bound 1000000
                    let d = digit_val(cs[j][0] as i64)
                    if d > 9
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    idx = (if idx < 0 then 0 else idx) * 10 + d
                    if idx > 1000000
                        fail BadFormat(at: j as i64)
                    j += 1
                if j >= n
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                let k: usize = if idx < 0 then next else idx as usize
                if k >= args.len()
                    fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
                if idx < 0
                    next += 1
                o = o + copy(args[k])
                i = j + 1
            continue
        if c == "}"
            if i + 1 < n and cs[i + 1] == "}"
                o = o + "}"
                i += 2
                continue
            fail BadFormat(at: i as i64)
        o = o + c
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- regex ----------------
# Program: instructions of 3 i64 [op, a, b]; jumps are relative to the
# instruction, so fragments can be concatenated and wrapped freely.
const OP_BYTE: i64 = 0
const OP_ANY: i64 = 1
const OP_CLASS: i64 = 2
const OP_SPLIT: i64 = 3
const OP_JMP: i64 = 4
const OP_MATCH: i64 = 5
const OP_BOL: i64 = 6
const OP_EOL: i64 = 7

pub struct Regex
    code: List[i64]
    classes: List[i64]

struct Parser
    pat: List[i64]
    pos: usize
    classes: List[i64]
    err: i64

fn ins(op: i64, a: i64, b: i64) -> List[i64] = [op, a, b]

fn cat(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o = a
    for x in b
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn ilen(f: &[i64]) -> i64 = (f.len() / 3) as i64

fn star(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 2), f), ins(OP_JMP, 0 - (n + 1), 0))

fn plus(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(f, ins(OP_SPLIT, 0 - n, 1))

fn opt(f: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let n = ilen(&f)
    return cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, n + 1), f)

fn alt(a: List[i64], b: List[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let na = ilen(&a)
    let nb = ilen(&b)
    return cat(cat(cat(ins(OP_SPLIT, 1, na + 2), a), ins(OP_JMP, nb + 1, 0)), b)

fn peek(p: &Parser) -> i64 = if p.pos < p.pat.len() then p.pat[p.pos] else -1

# a class is stored at an offset: [negated, pairs, lo1, hi1, ...]
fn add_class(p: &mut Parser, neg: bool, rs: &[i64]) -> i64
    let at = p.classes.len() as i64
    p.classes.push(if neg then 1 else 0)
    p.classes.push((rs.len() / 2) as i64)
    for x in rs
        p.classes.push(x)
    return at

fn esc_ranges(c: i64) -> List[i64]
    if c == 100 or c == 68
        return [48, 57]
    if c == 119 or c == 87
        return [48, 57, 65, 90, 95, 95, 97, 122]
    if c == 115 or c == 83
        return [9, 13, 32, 32]
    return []

fn esc_byte(c: i64) -> i64
    if c == 110
        return 10
    if c == 116
        return 9
    if c == 114
        return 13
    return c

fn is_meta(c: i64) -> bool = c == 92 or c == 46 or c == 91 or c == 93 or c == 40 or c == 41 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 125 or c == 124 or c == 94 or c == 36 or c == 45 or c == 47

fn is_esc_letter(c: i64) -> bool = c == 110 or c == 116 or c == 114

fn parse_class(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64]
    # after "["
    var neg = false
    if peek(p) == 94
        neg = true
        p.pos += 1
    var rs: List[i64] = []
    var first = true
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        if c == 93 and not first
            p.pos += 1
            break
        first = false
        var lo = c
        p.pos += 1
        if c == 92
            let e = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            let er = esc_ranges(e)
            if er.len() > 0
                if e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                for x in er
                    rs.push(x)
                continue
            if not is_meta(e) and not is_esc_letter(e)
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            lo = esc_byte(e)
        var hi = lo
        if peek(p) == 45 and p.pos + 1 < p.pat.len() and p.pat[p.pos + 1] != 93
            p.pos += 1
            hi = peek(p)
            p.pos += 1
            if hi == 92
                let e2 = peek(p)
                p.pos += 1
                if not is_meta(e2) and not is_esc_letter(e2)
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                hi = esc_byte(e2)
            if hi < lo
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
        rs.push(lo)
        rs.push(hi)
    let at = add_class(p, neg, &rs)
    return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)

fn parse_num(p: &mut Parser) -> i64
    var v: i64 = -1
    while peek(p) >= 48 and peek(p) <= 57 bound 10
        v = (if v < 0 then 0 else v) * 10 + peek(p) - 48
        p.pos += 1
    return v

fn repeat(f: List[i64], m: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..m
        o = cat(o, copy(f))
    if n < 0
        return cat(o, star(f))
    for _ in 0..(n - m)
        o = cat(o, opt(copy(f)))
    return o

fn parse_atom(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    let c = peek(p)
    p.pos += 1
    if c == 40
        if peek(p) == 63
            p.pos += 1
            if peek(p) != 58
                p.err = p.pos as i64
                return []
            p.pos += 1
        let f = parse_alt(p)
        if peek(p) != 41
            p.err = p.pos as i64
            return []
        p.pos += 1
        return f
    if c == 91
        return parse_class(p)
    if c == 46
        return ins(OP_ANY, 0, 0)
    if c == 94
        return ins(OP_BOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 36
        return ins(OP_EOL, 0, 0)
    if c == 92
        let e = peek(p)
        p.pos += 1
        let er = esc_ranges(e)
        if er.len() > 0
            let at = add_class(p, e == 68 or e == 87 or e == 83, &er)
            return ins(OP_CLASS, at, 0)
        if is_meta(e) or is_esc_letter(e)
            return ins(OP_BYTE, esc_byte(e), 0)
        p.err = p.pos as i64
        return []
    if c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 63 or c == 123 or c == 41 or c == 93 or c == 125
        p.err = (p.pos - 1) as i64
        return []
    return ins(OP_BYTE, c, 0)

fn parse_seq(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f: List[i64] = []
    while p.err < 0 bound 100000
        let c = peek(p)
        if c < 0 or c == 124 or c == 41
            break
        var a = parse_atom(p)
        while p.err < 0 bound 100
            let q = peek(p)
            if q == 42
                a = star(a)
            if q == 43
                a = plus(a)
            if q == 63
                a = opt(a)
            if q != 42 and q != 43 and q != 63 and q != 123
                break
            if q == 123
                p.pos += 1
                let m = parse_num(p)
                var n = m
                if peek(p) == 44
                    p.pos += 1
                    n = parse_num(p)
                if m < 0 or peek(p) != 125 or (n >= 0 and n < m) or m > 1000 or n > 1000
                    p.err = p.pos as i64
                    return []
                p.pos += 1
                a = repeat(a, m, n)
            if q != 123
                p.pos += 1
        f = cat(f, a)
    return f

fn parse_alt(p: &mut Parser) -> List[i64] bound 1000
    var f = parse_seq(p)
    while peek(p) == 124 and p.err < 0 bound 100000
        p.pos += 1
        let g = parse_seq(p)
        f = alt(f, g)
    return f

fn bytes_of(s: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < s.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(s[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

pub fn compile(pattern: &text) -> Regex ! BadRegex
    var p = Parser(pat: bytes_of(pattern), pos: 0, classes: [], err: -1)
    let f = parse_alt(&mut p)
    if p.err < 0 and p.pos < p.pat.len()
        p.err = p.pos as i64
    if p.err >= 0
        fail BadRegex(at: p.err)
    return Regex(code: cat(f, ins(OP_MATCH, 0, 0)), classes: copy(p.classes))

fn in_class(cl: &[i64], at: usize, c: i64) -> bool
    let n = cl[at + 1] as usize
    var hit = false
    for k in 0..n
        hit = hit or (c >= cl[at + 2 + 2 * k] and c <= cl[at + 3 + 2 * k])
    return hit != (cl[at] == 1)

fn seq_len(c: i64) -> i64
    if c < 128
        return 1
    if c >= 240
        return 4
    if c >= 224
        return 3
    if c >= 192
        return 2
    return 1

fn spush(st: &mut List[i64], sp: usize, v: i64) -> usize
    if sp < st.len()
        st[sp] = v
    else
        st.push(v)
    return sp + 1

# Add pc and its epsilon closure at input position i to list l (marking
# with stamp so each pc enters once per step).
fn add(re: &Regex, l: &mut List[i64], mark: &mut List[i64], stamp: i64, pc0: i64, i: usize, n: usize)
    var st: List[i64] = [pc0]
    var sp: usize = 1
    while sp > 0 bound 1000000
        sp -= 1
        let pc = st[sp]
        if mark[pc as usize] == stamp
            continue
        mark[pc as usize] = stamp
        let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
        if op == OP_JMP
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_SPLIT
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 2])
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1])
        if op == OP_BOL and i == 0
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op == OP_EOL and i == n
            sp = spush(&mut st, sp, pc + 1)
        if op != OP_JMP and op != OP_SPLIT and op != OP_BOL and op != OP_EOL
            l.push(pc)

# Pike VM. full: the match must span the input; else any substring.
fn run(re: &Regex, b: &[i64], full: bool) -> bool
    let n = b.len()
    let np = re.code.len() / 3
    var mark: List[i64] = []
    for _ in 0..np
        mark.push(-1)
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    var stamp: i64 = 0
    add(re, &mut cur, &mut mark, stamp, 0, 0, n)
    # threads waiting for a multi-byte "." to finish: [pc, resume position]
    var pend: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        for pc in cur
            if re.code[3 * pc as usize] == OP_MATCH and (not full or i == n)
                return true
        if i >= n
            break
        stamp += 1
        var nxt: List[i64] = []
        var keep: List[i64] = []
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < pend.len() bound 1000000
            if pend[k + 1] == (i + 1) as i64
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pend[k], i + 1, n)
            else
                keep.push(pend[k])
                keep.push(pend[k + 1])
            k += 2
        let c = b[i]
        for pc in cur
            let op = re.code[3 * pc as usize]
            let a = re.code[3 * pc as usize + 1]
            let sl = seq_len(c)
            # a class tests a whole code point; non-ASCII ones lie outside
            # every (ASCII) range
            let cls = op == OP_CLASS and in_class(&re.classes, a as usize, if sl > 1 then -1 else c)
            let one = (op == OP_BYTE and c == a) or (cls and sl == 1) or (op == OP_ANY and sl == 1 and c != 10)
            if one
                add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, pc + 1, i + 1, n)
            if (op == OP_ANY or cls) and sl > 1 and i + (sl as usize) <= n
                keep.push(pc + 1)
                keep.push((i as i64) + seq_len(c))
        # a search restarts only at code point boundaries
        if not full and (i + 1 >= n or b[i + 1] < 128 or b[i + 1] > 191)
            add(re, &mut nxt, &mut mark, stamp, 0, i + 1, n)
        cur = nxt
        pend = keep
        if cur.len() == 0 and pend.len() == 0 and full
            return false
        i += 1
    return false

pub fn is_match(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, true)

pub fn search(re: &Regex, s: &text) -> bool
    let b = bytes_of(s)
    return run(re, &b, false)

module hash.f11

# BLAKE3 (https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3, the specification paper and
# reference_impl.rs) in pure RCE: hash, keyed_hash and derive_key, with
# extendable output. Bytes are List[i64] with values 0..255 (as in crypto);
# words are i64 masked to 32 bits. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are in lib/crypto.rce
# and SHA-3/SHAKE in lib/pq.rce; this module adds no second copy of them.
# Cost is linear: about one compression per 64 input bytes plus one per
# 1024-byte chunk merge; the per-input fuel bounds the input size.
const v0: i64 = 4294967295
const v1: i64 = 1
const v2: i64 = 2
const v3: i64 = 4
const v4: i64 = 8
const v5: i64 = 16
const v6: i64 = 32
const v7: i64 = 64

fn f0() -> List[i64] = [1779033703, 3144134277, 1013904242, 2773480762, 1359893119, 2600822924, 528734635, 1541459225]

fn f1() -> List[i64] = [2, 6, 3, 10, 7, 0, 4, 13, 1, 11, 12, 5, 9, 14, 15, 8]

fn f2(v8: i64, v9: i64) -> i64 = ((v8 >> v9) | (v8 << (32 - v9))) & v0

fn f3(v10: &mut List[i64], v11: usize, v12: usize, v13: usize, v14: usize, v15: i64, v16: i64)
    v10[v11] = (v10[v11] + v10[v12] + v15) & v0
    v10[v14] = f2(v10[v14] ^ v10[v11], 16)
    v10[v13] = (v10[v13] + v10[v14]) & v0
    v10[v12] = f2(v10[v12] ^ v10[v13], 12)
    v10[v11] = (v10[v11] + v10[v12] + v16) & v0
    v10[v14] = f2(v10[v14] ^ v10[v11], 8)
    v10[v13] = (v10[v13] + v10[v14]) & v0
    v10[v12] = f2(v10[v12] ^ v10[v13], 7)

# The compression function: 16 output words (the first 8 are the new
# chaining value).
pub fn f4(v17: &[i64], v18: &[i64], v19: i64, v20: i64, v21: i64) -> List[i64]
    let v22 = f0()
    let v23 = f1()
    var v10: List[i64] = [v17[0], v17[1], v17[2], v17[3], v17[4], v17[5], v17[6], v17[7], v22[0], v22[1], v22[2], v22[3], v19 & v0, (v19 >> 32) & v0, v20, v21]
    var v24 = copy(v18)
    for v25 in 0..7
        f3(&mut v10, 0, 4, 8, 12, v24[0], v24[1])
        f3(&mut v10, 1, 5, 9, 13, v24[2], v24[3])
        f3(&mut v10, 2, 6, 10, 14, v24[4], v24[5])
        f3(&mut v10, 3, 7, 11, 15, v24[6], v24[7])
        f3(&mut v10, 0, 5, 10, 15, v24[8], v24[9])
        f3(&mut v10, 1, 6, 11, 12, v24[10], v24[11])
        f3(&mut v10, 2, 7, 8, 13, v24[12], v24[13])
        f3(&mut v10, 3, 4, 9, 14, v24[14], v24[15])
        if v25 < 6
            var v26: List[i64] = []
            for v27 in 0..16
                v26.push(v24[v23[v27] as usize])
            v24 = v26
    for v27 in 0..8
        v10[v27] = v10[v27] ^ v10[v27 + 8]
        v10[v27 + 8] = v10[v27 + 8] ^ v17[v27]
    return v10

# Little-endian words of the 64-byte block at off (zero padded).
fn f5(v28: &[i64], v29: usize) -> List[i64]
    var v30: List[i64] = []
    for v27 in 0..16
        var v8: i64 = 0
        for v31 in 0..4
            let v32 = v29 + 4 * v27 + v31
            if v32 < v28.len()
                v8 = v8 | (v28[v32] << (8 * v31))
        v30.push(v8)
    return v30

pub fn f6(v12: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var v30: List[i64] = []
    var v27: usize = 0
    while v27 + 3 < v12.len() bound 1048576
        v30.push(v12[v27] | (v12[v27 + 1] << 8) | (v12[v27 + 2] << 16) | (v12[v27 + 3] << 24))
        v27 += 4
    return v30

# A pending output: the inputs of a compression whose result is either a
# chaining value or, with ROOT, the root output.
struct t0
    v17: List[i64]
    v30: List[i64]
    v33: i64
    v20: i64
    v21: i64

fn f7(v34: &t0) -> List[i64]
    var v25 = f4(&v34.v17, &v34.v30, v34.v33, v34.v20, v34.v21)
    while v25.len() > 8 bound 8
        let _ = v25.pop()
    return v25

# Output of chunk ci (bytes [1024 ci, min(len, 1024 ci + 1024))).
fn f8(v35: &[i64], v28: &[i64], v36: i64, v21: i64) -> t0
    let v37 = (v36 as usize) * 1024
    var v38 = v37 + 1024
    if v38 > v28.len()
        v38 = v28.len()
    var v39 = (v38 - v37 + 63) / 64
    if v39 == 0
        v39 = 1
    var v17 = copy(v35)
    var v12: usize = 0
    while v12 + 1 < v39 bound 16
        let v40 = if v12 == 0 then v1 else 0
        let v41 = f5(v28, v37 + 64 * v12)
        var v25 = f4(&v17, &v41, v36, 64, v21 | v40)
        while v25.len() > 8 bound 8
            let _ = v25.pop()
        v17 = v25
        v12 += 1
    let v29 = v37 + 64 * v12
    let v40 = if v12 == 0 then v1 else 0
    let v30 = f5(v28, v29)
    let v42 = v38 - v29
    return t0(v17: v17, v30: v30, v33: v36, v20: v42 as i64, v21: v21 | v40 | v2)

fn f9(v35: &[i64], v43: &[i64], v25: &[i64], v21: i64) -> t0
    var v30 = copy(v43)
    for v8 in v25
        v30.push(v8)
    return t0(v17: copy(v35), v30: v30, v33: 0, v20: 64, v21: v21 | v3)

# Core tree hash: key words, mode flags, input bytes, output length.
pub fn f10(v35: &[i64], v21: i64, v28: &[i64], v44: i64) -> List[i64]
    var v9 = ((v28.len() + 1023) / 1024) as i64
    if v9 == 0
        v9 = 1
    var v45: List[List[i64]] = []
    var v36: i64 = 0
    while v36 + 1 < v9 bound 1048576
        let v46 = f8(v35, v28, v36, v21)
        var v17 = f7(&v46)
        var v47 = v36 + 1
        while v47 & 1 == 0 bound 64
            let v48 = copy(v45[v45.len() - 1])
            let _ = v45.pop()
            let v49 = f9(v35, &v48, &v17, v21)
            v17 = f7(&v49)
            v47 = v47 >> 1
        v45.push(v17)
        v36 += 1
    var v34 = f8(v35, v28, v9 - 1, v21)
    while v45.len() > 0 bound 64
        let v48 = copy(v45[v45.len() - 1])
        let _ = v45.pop()
        let v50 = f7(&v34)
        v34 = f9(v35, &v48, &v50, v21)
    var v51: List[i64] = []
    var v33: i64 = 0
    while (v51.len() as i64) < v44 bound 1048576
        let v52 = f4(&v34.v17, &v34.v30, v33, v34.v20, v34.v21 | v4)
        for v8 in v52
            for v31 in 0..4
                if (v51.len() as i64) < v44
                    v51.push((v8 >> (8 * v31)) & 255)
        v33 += 1
    return v51

pub fn f11(v28: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let v22 = f0()
    return f10(&v22, 0, v28, 32)

pub fn f12(v28: &[i64], v44: i64) -> List[i64]
    let v22 = f0()
    return f10(&v22, 0, v28, v44)

# key: exactly 32 bytes.
pub fn f13(v35: &[i64], v28: &[i64], v44: i64) -> List[i64]
    let _v53 = 1 / (if v35.len() == 32 then 1 else 0)
    let v54 = f6(v35)
    return f10(&v54, v5, v28, v44)

# context: a hardcoded, globally unique application string (as bytes).
pub fn f14(v55: &[i64], v56: &[i64], v44: i64) -> List[i64]
    let v22 = f0()
    let v57 = f10(&v22, v6, v55, 32)
    let v54 = f6(&v57)
    return f10(&v54, v7, v56, v44)

module hash.blake3

# BLAKE3 (https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3, the specification paper and
# reference_impl.rs) in pure RCE: hash, keyed_hash and derive_key, with
# extendable output. Bytes are List[i64] with values 0..255 (as in crypto);
# words are i64 masked to 32 bits. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are in lib/crypto.rce
# and SHA-3/SHAKE in lib/pq.rce; this module adds no second copy of them.
# Cost is linear: about one compression per 64 input bytes plus one per
# 1024-byte chunk merge; the per-input fuel bounds the input size.

const M32: i64 = 4294967295
const CHUNK_START: i64 = 1
const CHUNK_END: i64 = 2
const PARENT: i64 = 4
const ROOT: i64 = 8
const KEYED_HASH: i64 = 16
const DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT: i64 = 32
const DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL: i64 = 64

fn b3_iv() -> List[i64] = [1779033703, 3144134277, 1013904242, 2773480762, 1359893119, 2600822924, 528734635, 1541459225]

fn b3_perm() -> List[i64] = [2, 6, 3, 10, 7, 0, 4, 13, 1, 11, 12, 5, 9, 14, 15, 8]

fn rotr32(x: i64, n: i64) -> i64 = ((x >> n) | (x << (32 - n))) & M32

fn b3_g(v: &mut List[i64], a: usize, b: usize, c: usize, d: usize, mx: i64, my: i64)
    v[a] = (v[a] + v[b] + mx) & M32
    v[d] = rotr32(v[d] ^ v[a], 16)
    v[c] = (v[c] + v[d]) & M32
    v[b] = rotr32(v[b] ^ v[c], 12)
    v[a] = (v[a] + v[b] + my) & M32
    v[d] = rotr32(v[d] ^ v[a], 8)
    v[c] = (v[c] + v[d]) & M32
    v[b] = rotr32(v[b] ^ v[c], 7)

# The compression function: 16 output words (the first 8 are the new
# chaining value).
pub fn b3_compress(cv: &[i64], block: &[i64], counter: i64, blen: i64, flags: i64) -> List[i64]
    let iv = b3_iv()
    let perm = b3_perm()
    var v: List[i64] = [cv[0], cv[1], cv[2], cv[3], cv[4], cv[5], cv[6], cv[7], iv[0], iv[1], iv[2], iv[3], counter & M32, (counter >> 32) & M32, blen, flags]
    var m = copy(block)
    for r in 0..7
        b3_g(&mut v, 0, 4, 8, 12, m[0], m[1])
        b3_g(&mut v, 1, 5, 9, 13, m[2], m[3])
        b3_g(&mut v, 2, 6, 10, 14, m[4], m[5])
        b3_g(&mut v, 3, 7, 11, 15, m[6], m[7])
        b3_g(&mut v, 0, 5, 10, 15, m[8], m[9])
        b3_g(&mut v, 1, 6, 11, 12, m[10], m[11])
        b3_g(&mut v, 2, 7, 8, 13, m[12], m[13])
        b3_g(&mut v, 3, 4, 9, 14, m[14], m[15])
        if r < 6
            var p: List[i64] = []
            for i in 0..16
                p.push(m[perm[i] as usize])
            m = p
    for i in 0..8
        v[i] = v[i] ^ v[i + 8]
        v[i + 8] = v[i + 8] ^ cv[i]
    return v

# Little-endian words of the 64-byte block at off (zero padded).
fn block_words(input: &[i64], off: usize) -> List[i64]
    var w: List[i64] = []
    for i in 0..16
        var x: i64 = 0
        for k in 0..4
            let j = off + 4 * i + k
            if j < input.len()
                x = x | (input[j] << (8 * k))
        w.push(x)
    return w

pub fn words_le(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var w: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 3 < b.len() bound 1048576
        w.push(b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8) | (b[i + 2] << 16) | (b[i + 3] << 24))
        i += 4
    return w

# A pending output: the inputs of a compression whose result is either a
# chaining value or, with ROOT, the root output.
struct Out
    cv: List[i64]
    w: List[i64]
    ctr: i64
    blen: i64
    flags: i64

fn out_cv(o: &Out) -> List[i64]
    var r = b3_compress(&o.cv, &o.w, o.ctr, o.blen, o.flags)
    while r.len() > 8 bound 8
        let _ = r.pop()
    return r

# Output of chunk ci (bytes [1024 ci, min(len, 1024 ci + 1024))).
fn chunk_out(key: &[i64], input: &[i64], ci: i64, flags: i64) -> Out
    let lo = (ci as usize) * 1024
    var hi = lo + 1024
    if hi > input.len()
        hi = input.len()
    var nblocks = (hi - lo + 63) / 64
    if nblocks == 0
        nblocks = 1
    var cv = copy(key)
    var b: usize = 0
    while b + 1 < nblocks bound 16
        let st = if b == 0 then CHUNK_START else 0
        let bw = block_words(input, lo + 64 * b)
        var r = b3_compress(&cv, &bw, ci, 64, flags | st)
        while r.len() > 8 bound 8
            let _ = r.pop()
        cv = r
        b += 1
    let off = lo + 64 * b
    let st = if b == 0 then CHUNK_START else 0
    let w = block_words(input, off)
    let bl = hi - off
    return Out(cv: cv, w: w, ctr: ci, blen: bl as i64, flags: flags | st | CHUNK_END)

fn parent_out(key: &[i64], l: &[i64], r: &[i64], flags: i64) -> Out
    var w = copy(l)
    for x in r
        w.push(x)
    return Out(cv: copy(key), w: w, ctr: 0, blen: 64, flags: flags | PARENT)

# Core tree hash: key words, mode flags, input bytes, output length.
pub fn b3_core(key: &[i64], flags: i64, input: &[i64], outlen: i64) -> List[i64]
    var n = ((input.len() + 1023) / 1024) as i64
    if n == 0
        n = 1
    var stack: List[List[i64]] = []
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci + 1 < n bound 1048576
        let co = chunk_out(key, input, ci, flags)
        var cv = out_cv(&co)
        var total = ci + 1
        while total & 1 == 0 bound 64
            let left = copy(stack[stack.len() - 1])
            let _ = stack.pop()
            let po = parent_out(key, &left, &cv, flags)
            cv = out_cv(&po)
            total = total >> 1
        stack.push(cv)
        ci += 1
    var o = chunk_out(key, input, n - 1, flags)
    while stack.len() > 0 bound 64
        let left = copy(stack[stack.len() - 1])
        let _ = stack.pop()
        let rcv = out_cv(&o)
        o = parent_out(key, &left, &rcv, flags)
    var out: List[i64] = []
    var ctr: i64 = 0
    while (out.len() as i64) < outlen bound 1048576
        let words = b3_compress(&o.cv, &o.w, ctr, o.blen, o.flags | ROOT)
        for x in words
            for k in 0..4
                if (out.len() as i64) < outlen
                    out.push((x >> (8 * k)) & 255)
        ctr += 1
    return out

pub fn blake3(input: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let iv = b3_iv()
    return b3_core(&iv, 0, input, 32)

pub fn blake3_xof(input: &[i64], outlen: i64) -> List[i64]
    let iv = b3_iv()
    return b3_core(&iv, 0, input, outlen)

# key: exactly 32 bytes.
pub fn blake3_keyed(key: &[i64], input: &[i64], outlen: i64) -> List[i64]
    let _n = 1 / (if key.len() == 32 then 1 else 0)
    let kw = words_le(key)
    return b3_core(&kw, KEYED_HASH, input, outlen)

# context: a hardcoded, globally unique application string (as bytes).
pub fn blake3_derive_key(context: &[i64], material: &[i64], outlen: i64) -> List[i64]
    let iv = b3_iv()
    let ck = b3_core(&iv, DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT, context, 32)
    let kw = words_le(&ck)
    return b3_core(&kw, DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL, material, outlen)

module io

# Reader/writer and request/result patterns over host adapters (survey
# M18). A program asks for an effect by emitting a request struct with a
# `req: u64` field (FileRead, NetSend, PtyRead, ...); the host answers each
# request with exactly one logged result event `<Kind>Done(req, status,
# data: T?, err)` (Appendix E, HC-3, HC-10). Events and request structs
# belong to the program (a library cannot declare them), so this module
# holds the pure parts around them: result well-formedness, a table that
# pairs each result with the one request it answers, a line reader over
# received chunks, a writer that resends what a partial write left, and
# the file adapter's path rule. Nothing here reads a clock, a file or a
# socket; every value it sees came from a logged event.

# ---------------- results (HC-3) ----------------
pub const v0: text = "delivered"
pub const v1: text = "failed"
pub const v2: text = "timed_out"
pub const v3: text = "unreachable"

# The four outcomes of HC-3, as the host spells them.
pub fn f0(v4: &text) -> bool
    return v4 == v0 or v4 == v1 or v4 == v2 or v4 == v3

# A result is well formed when its status is known, a delivered result
# carries data and no error, and any other result carries no data. The
# data is taken by value (rce 0.1.3 does not infer T from a borrowed T?).
fn f1[T](v5: T?) -> bool
    match v5
        some(_x) -> return true
        none -> return false

pub fn f2[T](v6: &text, v7: T?, v8: &text) -> bool
    if not f0(v6)
        return false
    if v6 == v0
        return f1(v7) and v8 == ""
    return not f1(v7)

# The data of a delivered, well-formed result; none otherwise.
pub fn f3[T](v6: &text, v7: T?, v8: &text) -> T?
    if not f2(v6, copy(v7), v8)
        return none
    return v7

# ---------------- request table ----------------
# Request ids are 1, 2, 3, ... in issue order. Each outstanding request
# remembers its kind and a caller tag. A result settles a request only when
# its id is outstanding and its kind matches; anything else (an unknown id,
# a second result for the same id, a result of the wrong kind) is counted
# as stray and changes nothing else.
pub struct t0
    v9: u64
    v10: List[u64]
    v11: List[text]
    v12: List[text]
    v13: u64
    v14: u64

pub fn f4() -> t0 = t0(v9: 0, v10: [], v11: [], v12: [], v13: 0, v14: 0)

# Register a request of `kind` and return its id (to put in `req`).
pub fn f5(v15: &mut t0, v16: &text, v17: &text) -> u64
    v15.v9 += 1
    v15.v10.push(v15.v9)
    v15.v11.push(copy(v16))
    v15.v12.push(copy(v17))
    return v15.v9

fn f6(v15: &t0, v18: u64) -> i64
    var v19: usize = 0
    while v19 < v15.v10.len() bound 16777216
        if v15.v10[v19] == v18
            return v19 as i64
        v19 += 1
    return -1

fn f7(v15: &mut t0, v20: usize)
    var v21: List[u64] = []
    var v22: List[text] = []
    var v23: List[text] = []
    var v19: usize = 0
    while v19 < v15.v10.len() bound 16777216
        if v19 != v20
            v21.push(v15.v10[v19])
            v22.push(copy(v15.v11[v19]))
            v23.push(copy(v15.v12[v19]))
        v19 += 1
    v15.v10 = v21
    v15.v11 = v22
    v15.v12 = v23

# Settle the request a `<kind>Done(req, ...)` result answers; its tag, or
# none when the result is stray.
pub fn f8(v15: &mut t0, v16: &text, v18: u64) -> text?
    let v19 = f6(v15, v18)
    if v19 < 0
        v15.v14 += 1
        return none
    let v20 = v19 as usize
    if v15.v11[v20] != v16
        v15.v14 += 1
        return none
    let v24 = copy(v15.v12[v20])
    f7(v15, v20)
    v15.v13 += 1
    return some(v24)

pub fn f9(v15: &t0) -> usize = v15.v10.len()

pub fn f10(v15: &t0, v18: u64) -> bool = f6(v15, v18) >= 0

# ---------------- line reader ----------------
# Chunks (FileRead data, NetRecv or PtyRead text) arrive split anywhere;
# feed returns the lines they complete, without "\n" and without one "\r"
# before it, and keeps the rest. finish ends the stream (eof): the rest,
# when not empty, is the last line; later feeds return nothing.
pub struct t1
    v25: text
    v26: bool
    v27: u64

pub fn f11() -> t1 = t1(v25: "", v26: false, v27: 0)

fn f12(v4: &text) -> text
    let v28 = v4.chars()
    let v29 = v28.len()
    if v29 == 0 or v28[v29 - 1] != "\r"
        return copy(v4)
    var v30 = ""
    var v19: usize = 0
    while v19 + 1 < v29 bound 16777216
        v30 = v30 + v28[v19]
        v19 += 1
    return v30

pub fn f13(v21: &mut t1, v31: &text) -> List[text]
    var v32: List[text] = []
    if v21.v26
        return v32
    let v33 = v21.v25 + v31
    let v28 = v33.chars()
    var v34 = ""
    var v19: usize = 0
    while v19 < v28.len() bound 16777216
        if v28[v19] == "\n"
            v32.push(f12(&v34))
            v34 = ""
        else
            v34 = v34 + v28[v19]
        v19 += 1
    v21.v25 = v34
    v21.v27 += v32.len() as u64
    return v32

pub fn f14(v21: &mut t1) -> List[text]
    var v32: List[text] = []
    if v21.v26
        return v32
    v21.v26 = true
    if v21.v25 != ""
        v32.push(f12(&v21.v25))
        v21.v25 = ""
        v21.v27 += 1
    return v32

# ---------------- writer ----------------
# A writer holds text to send in chunks of at most `max` bytes, cut only
# between characters (so every chunk is valid UTF-8; a character longer
# than max is sent whole; max 0 acts as 1). One chunk is in flight at a
# time; a delivered result reports how many bytes went out, which may be
# fewer than the chunk (a partial NetSend or PtyWrite), and the rest is
# sent again.
pub struct t2
    v7: text
    v35: usize
    v36: usize
    v37: usize
    v38: u64

error x0(v39: text)

pub fn f15(v7: &text, v37: usize) -> t2 = t2(v7: copy(v7), v35: 0, v36: 0, v37: v37, v38: 0)

pub fn f16(v40: &t2) -> bool = v40.v35 >= v40.v7.len_bytes()

# The next chunk to send, or none while one is in flight or nothing is
# left. Its bytes count as in flight until ack or nack.
pub fn f17(v40: &mut t2) -> text?
    if v40.v36 > 0 or v40.v35 >= v40.v7.len_bytes()
        return none
    let v28 = v40.v7.chars()
    var v41: usize = 0
    var v30 = ""
    var v19: usize = 0
    while v19 < v28.len() bound 16777216
        let v42 = v28[v19].len_bytes()
        if v41 >= v40.v35

module io

# Reader/writer and request/result patterns over host adapters (survey
# M18). A program asks for an effect by emitting a request struct with a
# `req: u64` field (FileRead, NetSend, PtyRead, ...); the host answers each
# request with exactly one logged result event `<Kind>Done(req, status,
# data: T?, err)` (Appendix E, HC-3, HC-10). Events and request structs
# belong to the program (a library cannot declare them), so this module
# holds the pure parts around them: result well-formedness, a table that
# pairs each result with the one request it answers, a line reader over
# received chunks, a writer that resends what a partial write left, and
# the file adapter's path rule. Nothing here reads a clock, a file or a
# socket; every value it sees came from a logged event.

# ---------------- results (HC-3) ----------------

pub const DELIVERED: text = "delivered"
pub const FAILED: text = "failed"
pub const TIMED_OUT: text = "timed_out"
pub const UNREACHABLE: text = "unreachable"

# The four outcomes of HC-3, as the host spells them.
pub fn status_known(s: &text) -> bool
    return s == DELIVERED or s == FAILED or s == TIMED_OUT or s == UNREACHABLE

# A result is well formed when its status is known, a delivered result
# carries data and no error, and any other result carries no data. The
# data is taken by value (rce 0.1.3 does not infer T from a borrowed T?).
fn has[T](d: T?) -> bool
    match d
        some(_x) -> return true
        none -> return false

pub fn result_ok[T](status: &text, data: T?, err: &text) -> bool
    if not status_known(status)
        return false
    if status == DELIVERED
        return has(data) and err == ""
    return not has(data)

# The data of a delivered, well-formed result; none otherwise.
pub fn delivered[T](status: &text, data: T?, err: &text) -> T?
    if not result_ok(status, copy(data), err)
        return none
    return data

# ---------------- request table ----------------
# Request ids are 1, 2, 3, ... in issue order. Each outstanding request
# remembers its kind and a caller tag. A result settles a request only when
# its id is outstanding and its kind matches; anything else (an unknown id,
# a second result for the same id, a result of the wrong kind) is counted
# as stray and changes nothing else.

pub struct Pending
    next: u64
    reqs: List[u64]
    kinds: List[text]
    tags: List[text]
    settled: u64
    stray: u64

pub fn pending_new() -> Pending = Pending(next: 0, reqs: [], kinds: [], tags: [], settled: 0, stray: 0)

# Register a request of `kind` and return its id (to put in `req`).
pub fn issue(p: &mut Pending, what: &text, tag: &text) -> u64
    p.next += 1
    p.reqs.push(p.next)
    p.kinds.push(copy(what))
    p.tags.push(copy(tag))
    return p.next

fn find_req(p: &Pending, req: u64) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < p.reqs.len() bound 16777216
        if p.reqs[i] == req
            return i as i64
        i += 1
    return -1

fn drop_at(p: &mut Pending, k: usize)
    var r: List[u64] = []
    var ks: List[text] = []
    var ts: List[text] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < p.reqs.len() bound 16777216
        if i != k
            r.push(p.reqs[i])
            ks.push(copy(p.kinds[i]))
            ts.push(copy(p.tags[i]))
        i += 1
    p.reqs = r
    p.kinds = ks
    p.tags = ts

# Settle the request a `<kind>Done(req, ...)` result answers; its tag, or
# none when the result is stray.
pub fn settle(p: &mut Pending, what: &text, req: u64) -> text?
    let i = find_req(p, req)
    if i < 0
        p.stray += 1
        return none
    let k = i as usize
    if p.kinds[k] != what
        p.stray += 1
        return none
    let t = copy(p.tags[k])
    drop_at(p, k)
    p.settled += 1
    return some(t)

pub fn outstanding(p: &Pending) -> usize = p.reqs.len()

pub fn is_outstanding(p: &Pending, req: u64) -> bool = find_req(p, req) >= 0

# ---------------- line reader ----------------
# Chunks (FileRead data, NetRecv or PtyRead text) arrive split anywhere;
# feed returns the lines they complete, without "\n" and without one "\r"
# before it, and keeps the rest. finish ends the stream (eof): the rest,
# when not empty, is the last line; later feeds return nothing.

pub struct LineReader
    rest: text
    eof: bool
    lines: u64

pub fn reader_new() -> LineReader = LineReader(rest: "", eof: false, lines: 0)

fn strip_cr(s: &text) -> text
    let cs = s.chars()
    let n = cs.len()
    if n == 0 or cs[n - 1] != "\r"
        return copy(s)
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < n bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

pub fn feed(r: &mut LineReader, chunk: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    if r.eof
        return out
    let all = r.rest + chunk
    let cs = all.chars()
    var cur = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if cs[i] == "\n"
            out.push(strip_cr(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + cs[i]
        i += 1
    r.rest = cur
    r.lines += out.len() as u64
    return out

pub fn finish(r: &mut LineReader) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    if r.eof
        return out
    r.eof = true
    if r.rest != ""
        out.push(strip_cr(&r.rest))
        r.rest = ""
        r.lines += 1
    return out

# ---------------- writer ----------------
# A writer holds text to send in chunks of at most `max` bytes, cut only
# between characters (so every chunk is valid UTF-8; a character longer
# than max is sent whole; max 0 acts as 1). One chunk is in flight at a
# time; a delivered result reports how many bytes went out, which may be
# fewer than the chunk (a partial NetSend or PtyWrite), and the rest is
# sent again.

pub struct Writer
    data: text
    off: usize
    flight: usize
    max: usize
    sent: u64

error BadWrite(why: text)

pub fn writer_new(data: &text, max: usize) -> Writer = Writer(data: copy(data), off: 0, flight: 0, max: max, sent: 0)

pub fn writer_done(w: &Writer) -> bool = w.off >= w.data.len_bytes()

# The next chunk to send, or none while one is in flight or nothing is
# left. Its bytes count as in flight until ack or nack.
pub fn next_chunk(w: &mut Writer) -> text?
    if w.flight > 0 or w.off >= w.data.len_bytes()
        return none
    let cs = w.data.chars()
    var pos: usize = 0
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        let l = cs[i].len_bytes()
        if pos >= w.off
            if o != "" and o.len_bytes() + l > w.max
                break
            o = o + cs[i]
        pos += l
        i += 1
    w.flight = o.len_bytes()
    return some(o)

# A delivered write of n bytes of the chunk in flight. n beyond the chunk
# is refused. A partial count must end on a character boundary, since the
# rest is resent as text. Returns the bytes sent so far.
pub fn ack(w: &mut Writer, n: u64) -> u64 ! BadWrite
    if w.flight == 0
        fail BadWrite(why: "nothing in flight")
    if n > (w.flight as u64)
        fail BadWrite(why: "more than sent")
    let k = w.off + (n as usize)
    if not char_boundary(&w.data, k)
        fail BadWrite(why: "inside a character")
    w.off = k
    w.flight = 0
    w.sent += n
    return w.sent

# A failed, timed-out or unreachable write: nothing went out, the chunk is
# sent again by the next next_chunk.
pub fn nack(w: &mut Writer)
    w.flight = 0

fn char_boundary(s: &text, k: usize) -> bool
    if k >= s.len_bytes()
        return k == s.len_bytes()
    let b = s[k] as i64
    return b < 128 or b >= 192

# ---------------- file paths ----------------
# The file adapter's rule (least privilege, HC-5): a path is relative, not
# empty (FileList alone may name the root with ""), and made of normal
# names and "." only; ".." anywhere is refused. Empty segments ("a//b",
# "a/") are allowed, as the host's path split skips them. Symlinks leaving
# the root are refused by the host, which only it can see.

pub fn path_ok(p: &text, list: bool) -> bool
    if p == ""
        return list
    let cs = p.chars()
    if cs[0] == "/"
        return false
    var seg = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 16777216
        if i == cs.len() or cs[i] == "/"
            if seg == ".."
                return false
            seg = ""
        else
            seg = seg + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return true

module math

# Correctly rounded binary64 elementary functions, written once in RCE so
# every emit target (Rust, Python, JS, Scala, interpreter) gives the same
# bits. Only + - * / and sqrt are used, each correctly rounded (6.3 N3); no
# FMA, no native libm.
#
# Method. Each function computes a candidate on the output grid and then
# proves it is the correctly rounded value by comparing the input with the
# rounding midpoints next to it in exact arithmetic: products are split
# exactly with Dekker/Veltkamp TwoProduct, sums with Knuth TwoSum, and a
# difference is a Shewchuk nonoverlapping expansion whose sign is exact.
# A candidate one grid step off is moved until both midpoints bracket the
# exact value, so the answer does not depend on the candidate's accuracy
# and no worst-case table is needed. Exact ties round to even.
#
# Validated against CORE-MATH's worst cases (MIT, Copyright (c) 2021-2022
# Alexei Sibidanov, Paul Zimmermann et al., https://core-math.gitlabpages.inria.fr/)
# and MPFR 4.2.2 vectors; see vectors/SOURCE.md.
#
# Non-finite results trap like every f64 op (6.3 N3): hypot and exp trap
# when the true result overflows, log when x <= 0; cbrt, sin and cos never.
const v0: f64 = 134217729.0
const v1: f64 = 4503599627370496.0

# Knuth TwoSum: [s, e] with s = fl(a + b), s + e == a + b exactly.
pub fn f0(v2: f64, v3: f64) -> List[f64]
    let v4 = v2 + v3
    let v5 = v4 - v2
    let v6 = (v2 - (v4 - v5)) + (v3 - v5)
    return [v4, v6]

pub fn f1(v2: f64) -> List[f64]
    let v7 = v0 * v2
    let v8 = v7 - (v7 - v2)
    return [v8, v2 - v8]

# when no intermediate under- or overflows (callers keep |a|,|b| near 1).
pub fn f2(v2: f64, v3: f64) -> List[f64]

    let v10 = f1(v2)
    let v11 = f1(v3)
    let v6 = ((v10[0] * v11[0] - v9) + v10[0] * v11[1] + v10[1] * v11[0]) + v10[1] * v11[1]
    return [v9, v6]

pub fn f3(v6: &[f64], v3: f64) -> List[f64]

        v12 = f3(&v12, v9[0])

    let v20 = f7(&v22)
    let v23 = f4(v4, &v20)

    let v19 = v25[1] as i64
