module net.dns

# DNS messages (RFC 1035 section 4, survey M25 pure part): encode and
# decode over bytes (List[i64]). Names are text in presentation form
# (RFC 1035 5.1): labels joined by ".", a label byte that is not
# printable ASCII written \DDD, and the specials " $ ( ) . ; @ \ escaped
# with a backslash (as BIND and dnspython write them); the root is ".".
# Decoding follows compression pointers (4.1.4) only backwards, at most 128 of them, and refuses names over 255
# bytes, labels over 63, and the reserved label types 01 and 10. Record
# data of NS, CNAME, PTR, MX, SOA and SRV is returned uncompressed (names
# expanded), so it compares and re-encodes the same; other types are
# kept as bytes. Encoding writes no compression (always valid). No
# resolver here: sending a query is an io request through a host
# adapter (no UDP adapter exists in rce 0.1.3).

error BadDns(why: text)

pub struct Question
    name: text
    qtype: i64
    qclass: i64

pub struct Record
    name: text
    rtype: i64
    rclass: i64
    ttl: i64
    rdata: List[i64]

pub struct Dns
    id: i64
    flags: i64
    questions: List[Question]
    answers: List[Record]
    authority: List[Record]
    additional: List[Record]

pub const A: i64 = 1
pub const NS: i64 = 2
pub const CNAME: i64 = 5
pub const SOA: i64 = 6
pub const PTR: i64 = 12
pub const MX: i64 = 15
pub const TXT: i64 = 16
pub const AAAA: i64 = 28
pub const SRV: i64 = 33
pub const IN: i64 = 1

const DN_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

fn dch(x: i64) -> text = copy(DN_ASCII.chars()[(x - 32) as usize])

fn d3(x: i64) -> text = (x / 100).tostr() + ((x / 10) % 10).tostr() + (x % 10).tostr()

# ---------------- flags ----------------

pub fn qr(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 15) & 1 == 1
pub fn opcode(f: i64) -> i64 = (f >> 11) & 15
pub fn aa(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 10) & 1 == 1
pub fn tc(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 9) & 1 == 1
pub fn rd(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 8) & 1 == 1
pub fn ra(f: i64) -> bool = (f >> 7) & 1 == 1
pub fn rcode(f: i64) -> i64 = f & 15

pub fn make_flags(is_qr: bool, op: i64, is_aa: bool, is_tc: bool, is_rd: bool, is_ra: bool, rc: i64) -> i64
    var f = (op & 15) << 11 | (rc & 15)
    if is_qr
        f = f | 32768
    if is_aa
        f = f | 1024
    if is_tc
        f = f | 512
    if is_rd
        f = f | 256
    if is_ra
        f = f | 128
    return f

# ---------------- names ----------------

# Wire labels of a presentation name (without compression).
pub fn name_wire(n: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDns
    var out: List[i64] = []
    if n == "." or n == ""
        out.push(0)
        return out
    let cs = n.chars()
    var lab: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    var labels: List[List[i64]] = []
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        if c.len_bytes() != 1
            fail BadDns(why: "non-ASCII name")
        if c == "\\"
            if i + 1 >= cs.len()
                fail BadDns(why: "escape")
            let d = cs[i + 1][0] as i64
            if d >= 48 and d <= 57
                if i + 3 >= cs.len() + 0 and i + 4 > cs.len()
                    fail BadDns(why: "escape")
                var v: i64 = 0
                for k in 1..4
                    let x = cs[i + k][0] as i64
                    if x < 48 or x > 57
                        fail BadDns(why: "escape")
                    v = v * 10 + x - 48
                if v > 255
                    fail BadDns(why: "escape")
                lab.push(v)
                i += 4
            else
                lab.push(d)
                i += 2
        elif c == "."
            if lab.len() == 0
                fail BadDns(why: "empty label")
            labels.push(lab)
            lab = []
            i += 1
        else
            lab.push(c[0] as i64)
            i += 1
    if lab.len() > 0
        labels.push(lab)
    for l in labels
        if l.len() > 63
            fail BadDns(why: "label over 63")
        out.push(l.len() as i64)
        for x in l
            out.push(x)
    out.push(0)
    if out.len() > 255
        fail BadDns(why: "name over 255")
    return out

fn label_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, n: usize) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < n bound 64
        let x = b[lo + k]
        if x == 34 or x == 36 or x == 40 or x == 41 or x == 46 or x == 59 or x == 64 or x == 92
            o = o + "\\" + dch(x)
        elif x > 32 and x < 127
            o = o + dch(x)
        else
            o = o + "\\" + d3(x)
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct NameAt
    name: text
    next: i64

# The name at offset off of message b, and the offset after it.
pub fn read_name(b: &[i64], off: i64) -> NameAt ! BadDns
    var p = off
    var next: i64 = -1
    var hops: i64 = 0
    var limit = off
    var o = ""
    var wire: i64 = 1
    loop bound 16777216
        if p < 0 or p >= b.len() as i64
            fail BadDns(why: "name out of bounds")
        let l = b[p as usize]
        if l & 192 == 192
            if p + 1 >= b.len() as i64
                fail BadDns(why: "name out of bounds")
            let t = ((l & 63) << 8) | b[(p + 1) as usize]
            if next < 0
                next = p + 2
            if t >= limit
                fail BadDns(why: "forward pointer")
            hops += 1
            if hops > 128
                fail BadDns(why: "pointer loop")
            limit = t
            p = t
            continue
        if l & 192 != 0
            fail BadDns(why: "label type")
        if l == 0
            if next < 0
                next = p + 1
            return NameAt(name: if o == "" then "." else o, next: next)
        if p + 1 + l > b.len() as i64
            fail BadDns(why: "name out of bounds")
        wire += l + 1
        if wire > 255
            fail BadDns(why: "name over 255")
        o = o + label_text(b, (p + 1) as usize, l as usize) + "."
        p += l + 1
    fail BadDns(why: "name")

# ---------------- messages ----------------

fn u16(b: &[i64], p: i64) -> i64 ! BadDns
    if p < 0 or p + 2 > b.len() as i64
        fail BadDns(why: "truncated")
    return b[p as usize] * 256 + b[(p + 1) as usize]

fn push16(o: &mut List[i64], v: i64)
    o.push((v >> 8) & 255)
    o.push(v & 255)

fn push32(o: &mut List[i64], v: i64)
    push16(o, (v >> 16) & 65535)
    push16(o, v & 65535)

fn cat(o: &mut List[i64], b: &[i64])
    for x in b
        o.push(x)

fn slice(b: &[i64], lo: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n bound 16777216
        o.push(b[(lo + k) as usize])
        k += 1
    return o

# Record data with names expanded, for the types that hold names.
fn rdata_of(b: &[i64], t: i64, p: i64, n: i64) -> List[i64] ! BadDns
    let end = p + n
    if t == NS or t == CNAME or t == PTR or t == MX or t == SOA or t == SRV
        var o: List[i64] = []
        var q = p
        let fixed_before = if t == MX then 2 else (if t == SRV then 6 else 0)
        let pre = slice(b, q, fixed_before)
        cat(&mut o, &pre)
        q += fixed_before
        let r = try read_name(b, q)
        let w = try name_wire(&r.name)
        cat(&mut o, &w)
        q = r.next
        if t == SOA
            let r2 = try read_name(b, q)
            let w2 = try name_wire(&r2.name)
            cat(&mut o, &w2)
            q = r2.next
            if q + 20 != end
                fail BadDns(why: "rdata length")
            let tail = slice(b, q, 20)
            cat(&mut o, &tail)
            return o
        if q != end
            fail BadDns(why: "rdata length")
        return o
    if t == A and n != 4
        fail BadDns(why: "A length")
    if t == AAAA and n != 16
        fail BadDns(why: "AAAA length")
    return slice(b, p, n)

fn read_records(b: &[i64], p0: i64, count: i64, out: &mut List[Record]) -> i64 ! BadDns
    var p = p0
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < count bound 65536
        let r = try read_name(b, p)
        p = r.next
        let t = try u16(b, p)
        let c = try u16(b, p + 2)
        let hi = try u16(b, p + 4)
        let lo = try u16(b, p + 6)
        let n = try u16(b, p + 8)
        p += 10
        if p + n > b.len() as i64
            fail BadDns(why: "truncated")
        let d = try rdata_of(b, t, p, n)
        out.push(Record(name: copy(r.name), rtype: t, rclass: c, ttl: hi * 65536 + lo, rdata: d))
        p += n
        k += 1
    return p

pub fn decode(b: &[i64]) -> Dns ! BadDns
    for x in b
        if x < 0 or x > 255
            fail BadDns(why: "not bytes")
    let id = try u16(b, 0)
    let fl = try u16(b, 2)
    let qd = try u16(b, 4)
    let an = try u16(b, 6)
    let ns = try u16(b, 8)
    let ar = try u16(b, 10)
    var p: i64 = 12
    var qs: List[Question] = []
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < qd bound 65536
        let r = try read_name(b, p)
        let t = try u16(b, r.next)
        let c = try u16(b, r.next + 2)
        qs.push(Question(name: copy(r.name), qtype: t, qclass: c))
        p = r.next + 4
        k += 1
    var a1: List[Record] = []
    var a2: List[Record] = []
    var a3: List[Record] = []
    p = try read_records(b, p, an, &mut a1)
    p = try read_records(b, p, ns, &mut a2)
    p = try read_records(b, p, ar, &mut a3)
    if p != b.len() as i64
        fail BadDns(why: "trailing bytes")
    return Dns(id: id, flags: fl, questions: qs, answers: a1, authority: a2, additional: a3)

fn put_records(o: &mut List[i64], rs: &[Record]) -> bool ! BadDns
    for r in rs
        let w = try name_wire(&r.name)
        cat(o, &w)
        push16(o, r.rtype)
        push16(o, r.rclass)
        push32(o, r.ttl)
        if r.rdata.len() > 65535
            fail BadDns(why: "rdata over 65535")
        push16(o, r.rdata.len() as i64)
        cat(o, &r.rdata)
    return true

pub fn encode(m: &Dns) -> List[i64] ! BadDns
    var o: List[i64] = []
    push16(&mut o, m.id & 65535)
    push16(&mut o, m.flags & 65535)
    push16(&mut o, m.questions.len() as i64)
    push16(&mut o, m.answers.len() as i64)
    push16(&mut o, m.authority.len() as i64)
    push16(&mut o, m.additional.len() as i64)
    for q in m.questions
        let w = try name_wire(&q.name)
        cat(&mut o, &w)
        push16(&mut o, q.qtype)
        push16(&mut o, q.qclass)
    let _x = try put_records(&mut o, &m.answers)
    let _y = try put_records(&mut o, &m.authority)
    let _z = try put_records(&mut o, &m.additional)
    return o

# A recursive query for name and type (RD set, class IN).

module net.http

# HTTP/1.1 messages (RFC 9112, survey M25 pure part): parse and serialize
# requests and responses over bytes (List[i64], 0..255), with message

# LF is refused), obs-fold is refused (5.2), whitespace before a field
# colon is refused (5.1), Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length
# is refused (6.1, request smuggling), differing Content-Length values
# are refused (6.3). Field values must be ASCII (obs-text needs text built
# from bytes, which RCE 0.1.3 cannot do). No socket here: a connection is
# the io module's request/result pattern; parse fails with a why that
# starts "incomplete" when more bytes are needed.

error BadHttp(why: text)

pub struct Message
    request: bool
    method: text
    target: text
    major: i64
    minor: i64
    status: i64
    reason: text
    names: List[text]
    values: List[text]
    body: List[i64]
    trailer_names: List[text]
    trailer_values: List[text]
    used: i64

pub fn message_empty() -> Message = Message(request: true, method: "", target: "", major: 1, minor: 1, status: 0, reason: "", names: [], values: [], body: [], trailer_names: [], trailer_values: [], used: 0)

const HT_ASCII: text = " !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~"

    if (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or (c >= 65 and c <= 90) or (c >= 97 and c <= 122)
        return true
    return c == 33 or c == 35 or c == 36 or c == 37 or c == 38 or c == 39 or c == 42 or c == 43 or c == 45 or c == 46 or c == 94 or c == 95 or c == 96 or c == 124 or c == 126

fn vchar(c: i64) -> bool = c >= 33 and c <= 126

fn lower(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        o = o + (if x >= 65 and x <= 90 then ch(x + 32) else c)
    return o

pub fn bytes_of(t: &text) -> List[i64]

        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# Index of the CRLF ending the line that starts at i, or -1 when the
# buffer ends first. A bare CR or LF is refused.
fn line_end(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 ! BadHttp

    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        if b[k] == 13
            if k + 1 >= b.len()
                return -1
            if b[k + 1] != 10

fn ascii_text(b: &[i64], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text ! BadHttp
    var o = ""
    var k = lo

        elif x < 32 or x > 126

fn version(t: &text, m: &mut Message) -> bool
    let cs = t.chars()

        return false

    let b = cs[7][0] as i64
    if a < 48 or a > 57 or b < 48 or b > 57
        return false
    m.major = a - 48
    m.minor = b - 48
    return true

fn split_sp(t: &text) -> List[text]
    var parts: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == " "
            parts.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    parts.push(cur)
    return parts

fn start_line(t: &text, m: &mut Message, req: bool) -> bool ! BadHttp

                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        for c in ps[1].chars()
            if not vchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "target")

            fail BadHttp(why: "version")

        m.target = copy(ps[1])

        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")

    var i: usize = 0

        v = v + cs[i]
        i += 1

    var k: usize = 9

        k += 1

        fail BadHttp(why: "status line")

    var j: usize = 13
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        r = r + cs[j]
        j += 1

    let cs = t.chars()
    var lo: usize = 0
    var hi = cs.len()
    while lo < hi and (cs[lo] == " " or cs[lo] == "\t") bound 16777216
        lo += 1
    while hi > lo and (cs[hi - 1] == " " or cs[hi - 1] == "\t") bound 16777216
        hi -= 1
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]

fn field(t: &text, names: &mut List[text], values: &mut List[text]) -> bool ! BadHttp
    let cs = t.chars()

        fail BadHttp(why: "obs-fold")

    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != ":" bound 16777216
        if not tchar(cs[i][0] as i64)
            fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        name = name + cs[i]
        i += 1

        fail BadHttp(why: "field line")
    var v = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        v = v + cs[j]
        j += 1
    names.push(name)
    values.push(trim_ows(&v))
    return true

# with ", " (RFC 9110 5.3), or none.
pub fn header(names: &[text], values: &[text], name: &text) -> text?
    let want = lower(name)
    var found = false
    var o = ""
    for i in 0..names.len()
        if lower(&names[i]) == want
            o = if found then o + ", " + values[i] else copy(values[i])
            found = true
    return if found then some(o) else none

fn list_items(v: &text) -> List[text]
    var out: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in v.chars()
        if c == ","
            out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    out.push(trim_ows(&cur))
    return out

fn dec(t: &text) -> i64

        return -1

    for c in t.chars()
        let x = c[0] as i64
        if x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + x - 48
    return v

fn hexnum(t: &text) -> i64
    if t == "" or t.len_bytes() > 15
        return -1

        let x = c[0] as i64

            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70

        var vs = copy(m.values)

        m.values = vs

            loop bound 16777216
                let f = try line_end(b, i)

                    return -1

                    return (i + 2) as i64

                var ns = copy(m.trailer_names)
                var vs = copy(m.trailer_values)
                let _y = try field(&t, &mut ns, &mut vs)
                m.trailer_names = ns
                m.trailer_values = vs
                i = (f + 2) as usize
        if i + (n as usize) + 2 > b.len()
            return -1
        var k: usize = 0

            k += 1

# connection (a response without a length then ends there). `head_req`
# says the response answers a HEAD request (no body). BadHttp(why:
# "incomplete ...") when b holds only part of the message.
pub fn parse_message(b: &[i64], req: bool, head_req: bool, eof: bool) -> Message ! BadHttp
    var m = message_empty()
    m.request = req
    let h = try head(b, &mut m, req)
    if h < 0
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete head")
    let ten = "transfer-encoding"
    let cln = "content-length"
    let te = header(&m.names, &m.values, &ten)
    let cl = header(&m.names, &m.values, &cln)
    let no_body = not req and (head_req or (m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)

        m.used = h
        return m

        if cl != none
            fail BadHttp(why: "both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length")
        let tv = te.or("")
        let items = list_items(&tv)

            if req
                fail BadHttp(why: "transfer coding")
            # a response: read until close (6.3 rule 4)
            if not eof
                fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
            m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
            m.used = b.len() as i64
            return m
        for k in 0..items.len() - 1
            if lower(&items[k]) == "chunked"
                fail BadHttp(why: "chunked twice")
        if items.len() > 1
            fail BadHttp(why: "unsupported transfer coding")
        let used = try chunked(b, h as usize, &mut m)
        if used < 0
            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete chunk")
        m.used = used
        return m

        let cv = cl.or("")
        let items = list_items(&cv)
        let n = dec(&items[0])
        for it in items
            if dec(&it) != n
                fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")

            fail BadHttp(why: "Content-Length")

            fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete body")

        var k: usize = 0
        while k < n as usize bound 16777216
            body.push(b[(h as usize) + k])
            k += 1
        m.body = body
        m.used = h + n
        return m
    if req
        m.used = h
        return m
    if not eof
        fail BadHttp(why: "incomplete close")
    m.body = rest(b, h as usize)
    m.used = b.len() as i64
    return m

fn rest(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var k = i
    while k < b.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

fn put(o: &mut List[i64], t: &text)
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1

# body unless a Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding field is given or the
# message has no body by its status. The body is written as is (a caller
# that set Transfer-Encoding: chunked passes chunked bytes, see chunk).
pub fn serialize(m: &Message) -> List[i64] ! BadHttp
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if m.request
        for c in m.method.chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "method")
        let line = m.method + " " + m.target + " HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    else
        if m.status < 100 or m.status > 999
            fail BadHttp(why: "status code")
        let line = "HTTP/" + m.major.tostr() + "." + m.minor.tostr() + " " + m.status.tostr() + " " + m.reason + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    var framed = false
    for i in 0..m.names.len()
        for c in m.names[i].chars()
            if not tchar(c[0] as i64)
                fail BadHttp(why: "field name")
        for c in m.values[i].chars()
            let x = c[0] as i64
            if c.len_bytes() != 1 or (x < 32 and x != 9) or x == 127
                fail BadHttp(why: "field value")
        let l = lower(&m.names[i])
        if l == "content-length" or l == "transfer-encoding"
            framed = true
        let line = m.names[i] + ": " + m.values[i] + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let bodyless = not m.request and ((m.status >= 100 and m.status < 200) or m.status == 204 or m.status == 304)
    if not framed and not bodyless and (not m.request or m.body.len() > 0)
        let line = "Content-Length: " + m.body.len().tostr() + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
    let crlf = "\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &crlf)
    for x in m.body
        o.push(x)
    return o

fn hexlow(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "0"
    let hs = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = n
    while x > 0 bound 16
        o = copy(hs[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
    return o

# Chunked transfer coding of data in chunks of at most size bytes, with
# the last chunk and an empty trailer.
pub fn chunk(data: &[i64], size: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    let sz = if size < 1 then 1 else size
    var i: i64 = 0
    let n = data.len() as i64
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let k = if n - i < sz then n - i else sz
        let line = hexlow(k) + "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &line)
        var j: i64 = 0
        while j < k bound 16777216
            o.push(data[(i + j) as usize])
            j += 1
        let crlf = "\r\n"
        put(&mut o, &crlf)
        i += k
    let last = "0\r\n\r\n"
    put(&mut o, &last)
    return o

module net.idna

# UTS #46 Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing (revision 33, Unicode
# 16.0.0) and the Punycode codec of RFC 3492, in pure RCE over code
# points (List[i64]). Steps of section 4: map with the IdnaMappingTable,
# normalize to NFC (UAX #15, canonical decomposition, reordering and
# composition, Hangul algorithmic), break at U+002E, convert and validate
# each label (4.1: hyphens, leading mark, status, STD3 ASCII, ContextJ of
# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 and A.2, the six bidi rules of RFC 5893 section
# 2). ToASCII (4.2) adds Punycode with the "xn--" prefix and the DNS
# length checks; ToUnicode (4.3) returns code points, since rce 0.1.3
# cannot build text from arbitrary code points. Every operation returns
# its output together with an error flag, as UTS #46 specifies ("the
# conversion is performed as much as is possible"); the status codes are
# not reproduced (IdnaTestV2.txt requires only the error flag).
# The data section below is generated from the pinned Unicode files
# (vectors/SOURCE.md lists each file with its sha256).

pub struct Flags
    std3: bool
    hyphens: bool
    bidi: bool
    joiners: bool
    transitional: bool
    dns_length: bool
    ignore_bad_punycode: bool

pub struct Cps
    cps: List[i64]
    err: bool

pub struct Ascii
    host: text
    err: bool

# The flags of IdnaTestV2.txt (all checks on) and of the WHATWG URL
# Standard "domain to ASCII" with beStrict false.
pub fn test_flags(transitional: bool) -> Flags = Flags(std3: true, hyphens: true, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: transitional, dns_length: true, ignore_bad_punycode: false)
pub fn url_flags() -> Flags = Flags(std3: false, hyphens: false, bidi: true, joiners: true, transitional: false, dns_length: false, ignore_bad_punycode: false)

# ---------------- NFC (UAX #15) ----------------

const S_BASE: i64 = 44032
const L_BASE: i64 = 4352
const V_BASE: i64 = 4449
const T_BASE: i64 = 4519
const S_COUNT: i64 = 11172
const T_COUNT: i64 = 28
const N_COUNT: i64 = 588

fn decompose_into(o: &mut List[i64], c: i64)
    if c >= S_BASE and c < S_BASE + S_COUNT
        let s = c - S_BASE
        o.push(L_BASE + s / N_COUNT)
        o.push(V_BASE + (s % N_COUNT) / T_COUNT)
        if s % T_COUNT != 0
            o.push(T_BASE + s % T_COUNT)
        return
    let d = decomposition(c)
    if d.len() == 0
        o.push(c)
        return
    for x in d
        o.push(x)

# Canonical decomposition followed by the canonical ordering algorithm.
pub fn nfd(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        decompose_into(&mut o, c)
    var cc: List[i64] = []
    for c in o
        cc.push(ccc(c))
    # stable insertion sort of each run of non-starters by class
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < o.len() bound 16777216
        var j = i
        while j > 0 and cc[j] != 0 and cc[j - 1] > cc[j] bound 16777216
            let t = o[j]
            o[j] = o[j - 1]
            o[j - 1] = t
            let u = cc[j]
            cc[j] = cc[j - 1]
            cc[j - 1] = u
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    return o

fn compose_pair(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
    if a >= L_BASE and a < L_BASE + 19 and b >= V_BASE and b < V_BASE + 21
        return S_BASE + ((a - L_BASE) * 21 + (b - V_BASE)) * T_COUNT
    if a >= S_BASE and a < S_BASE + S_COUNT and (a - S_BASE) % T_COUNT == 0 and b > T_BASE and b < T_BASE + T_COUNT
        return a + (b - T_BASE)
    return composite(a * 1114112 + b)

pub fn nfc(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let d = nfd(cps)
    var o: List[i64] = []
    if d.len() == 0
        return o
    var sp: usize = 0
    var last = ccc(d[0])
    var starter = last == 0
    o.push(d[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < d.len() bound 16777216
        let c = d[i]
        let cl = ccc(c)
        let comp = if starter then compose_pair(o[sp], c) else -1
        if starter and (last < cl or last == 0) and comp >= 0
            o[sp] = comp
            i += 1
            continue
        if cl == 0
            sp = o.len()
            starter = true
        last = cl
        o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# ---------------- Punycode (RFC 3492) ----------------

const P_BASE: i64 = 36
const P_TMIN: i64 = 1
const P_TMAX: i64 = 26
const P_MAX: i64 = 2147483647

fn adapt(delta0: i64, numpoints: i64, first: bool) -> i64
    var delta = if first then delta0 / 700 else delta0 / 2
    delta += delta / numpoints
    var k: i64 = 0
    while delta > ((P_BASE - P_TMIN) * P_TMAX) / 2 bound 64
        delta = delta / (P_BASE - P_TMIN)
        k += P_BASE
    return k + (P_BASE - P_TMIN + 1) * delta / (delta + 38)

fn digit_value(c: i64) -> i64
    if c >= 48 and c <= 57
        return c - 22
    if c >= 65 and c <= 90
        return c - 65
    if c >= 97 and c <= 122
        return c - 97
    return -1

fn digit_char(d: i64) -> i64 = if d < 26 then d + 97 else d + 22

fn thresh(k: i64, bias: i64) -> i64
    if k <= bias
        return P_TMIN
    if k >= bias + P_TMAX
        return P_TMAX
    return k - bias

# Decoding; a failure (bad digit, end inside a number, overflow, a
# result that is not a scalar value) gives err.
pub fn puny_decode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var b: usize = 0
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < input.len() bound 16777216
        if input[j] == 45
            b = j
        j += 1
    var k: usize = 0
    while k < b bound 16777216
        if input[k] >= 128
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(input[k])
        k += 1
    var p: usize = if b > 0 then b + 1 else 0
    var n: i64 = 128
    var i: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    while p < input.len() bound 16777216
        let oldi = i
        var w: i64 = 1
        var kk: i64 = P_BASE
        loop bound 64
            if p >= input.len()
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            let d = digit_value(input[p])
            p += 1
            if d < 0
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if d > (P_MAX - i) / w
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            i += d * w
            let t = thresh(kk, bias)
            if d < t
                break
            if w > P_MAX / (P_BASE - t)
                return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            w = w * (P_BASE - t)
            kk += P_BASE
        let len = o.len() as i64 + 1
        bias = adapt(i - oldi, len, oldi == 0)
        if i / len > P_MAX - n
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        n += i / len
        i = i % len
        if n > 1114111 or (n >= 55296 and n <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        o.push(n)
        var q = o.len() - 1
        while q > i as usize bound 16777216
            o[q] = o[q - 1]
            q -= 1
        o[i as usize] = n
        i += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

pub fn puny_encode(input: &[i64]) -> Cps
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        if c < 0 or c > 1114111 or (c >= 55296 and c <= 57343)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        if c < 128
            o.push(c)
    let basic = o.len() as i64
    var h = basic
    if basic > 0
        o.push(45)
    var n: i64 = 128
    var delta: i64 = 0
    var bias: i64 = 72
    let total = input.len() as i64
    while h < total bound 16777216
        var m: i64 = P_MAX
        for c in input
            if c >= n and c < m
                m = c
        if m - n > (P_MAX - delta) / (h + 1)
            return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
        delta += (m - n) * (h + 1)
        n = m
        for c in input
            if c < n
                delta += 1
                if delta > P_MAX
                    return Cps(cps: o, err: true)
            if c == n
                var q = delta
                var k: i64 = P_BASE
                loop bound 64
                    let t = thresh(k, bias)
                    if q < t
                        break
                    o.push(digit_char(t + (q - t) % (P_BASE - t)))
                    q = (q - t) / (P_BASE - t)
                    k += P_BASE
                o.push(digit_char(q))
                bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == basic)
                delta = 0
                h += 1
        delta += 1
        n += 1
    return Cps(cps: o, err: false)

# ---------------- UTS #46 processing ----------------

fn is_xn(l: &[i64]) -> bool = l.len() >= 4 and (l[0] == 120 or l[0] == 88) and (l[1] == 110 or l[1] == 78) and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45

fn all_ascii(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        if c >= 128
            return false
    return true

fn is_rtl_label(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 1 or b == 2 or b == 3
            return true
    return false

# RFC 5893 section 2, rules 1 to 6, for one label of a bidi domain.
pub fn bidi_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    let f = bidi_class(l[0])
    if f != 0 and f != 1 and f != 2
        return false
    var e = l.len()
    while e > 0 and bidi_class(l[e - 1]) == 10 bound 16777216
        e -= 1
    if e == 0
        return false
    let last = bidi_class(l[e - 1])
    if f == 0
        for c in l
            let b = bidi_class(c)
            if b != 0 and b != 4 and b != 5 and b != 6 and b != 7 and b != 8 and b != 9 and b != 10
                return false
        return last == 0 or last == 4
    var en = false
    var an = false
    for c in l
        let b = bidi_class(c)
        if b == 0 or b > 10
            return false
        if b == 4
            en = true
        if b == 3
            an = true
    if en and an
        return false
    return last == 1 or last == 2 or last == 4 or last == 3

# RFC 5892 appendix A.1 (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER) and A.2 (ZERO WIDTH JOINER).
pub fn joiners_ok(l: &[i64]) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < l.len() bound 16777216
        let c = l[i]
        if c == 8204 or c == 8205
            let virama = i > 0 and ccc(l[i - 1]) == 9
            if not virama
                if c == 8205
                    return false
                var a = i
                var left = false
                while a > 0 bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[a - 1])
                    if t == 5
                        a -= 1
                        continue
                    left = t == 2 or t == 4
                    break
                var z = i + 1
                var right = false
                while z < l.len() bound 16777216
                    let t = joining_type(l[z])
                    if t == 5
                        z += 1
                        continue
                    right = t == 2 or t == 3
                    break
                if not (left and right)
                    return false
        i += 1
    return true

# Validity criteria 4.1 except the bidi rules (checked per domain).
fn valid_label(l: &[i64], f: &Flags, transitional: bool, decoded: bool) -> bool
    if l.len() == 0
        return true
    if decoded
        let n = nfc(l)
        if n != copy(l)
            return false
    if f.hyphens
        if l.len() >= 4 and l[2] == 45 and l[3] == 45
            return false
        if l[0] == 45 or l[l.len() - 1] == 45
            return false
    elif is_xn(l)
        return false
    if is_mark(l[0])
        return false
    for c in l
        if c == 46
            return false
        let s = status(c)
        if not (s == 0 or (s == 2 and not transitional))
            return false
        if f.std3 and c < 128 and not ((c >= 97 and c <= 122) or (c >= 48 and c <= 57) or c == 45)
            return false
    if f.joiners and not joiners_ok(l)
        return false
    return true

pub struct Labels
    labels: List[List[i64]]
    err: bool

# Section 4 processing: the converted labels and the error flag.
pub fn process(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Labels
    var m: List[i64] = []
    for c in input
        let s = status(c)
        if s == 4
            continue
        if s == 1
            if f.transitional and c == 7838
                m.push(115)
                m.push(115)
            else
                for x in mapping(c)
                    m.push(x)
        elif s == 2 and f.transitional
            for x in mapping(c)
                m.push(x)
        else
            m.push(c)
    let n = nfc(&m)
    var raw: List[List[i64]] = []
    var cur: List[i64] = []
    for c in n
        if c == 46
            raw.push(cur)
            cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    raw.push(cur)
    var err = false
    var out: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in raw
        if is_xn(&l)
            if not all_ascii(&l)
                err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var rest: List[i64] = []
            var k: usize = 4
            while k < l.len() bound 16777216
                rest.push(l[k])
                k += 1
            let d = puny_decode(&rest)
            if d.err
                if not f.ignore_bad_punycode
                    err = true
                    out.push(copy(l))
                    continue
                if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                    err = true
                out.push(copy(l))
                continue
            if d.cps.len() == 0 or all_ascii(&d.cps)
                err = true
            if not valid_label(&d.cps, f, false, true)
                err = true
            out.push(d.cps)
        else
            if not valid_label(&l, f, f.transitional, false)
                err = true
            out.push(copy(l))
    if f.bidi
        var rtl = false
        for l in out
            if is_rtl_label(&l)
                rtl = true
        if rtl
            for l in out
                if not bidi_ok(&l)
                    err = true
    return Labels(labels: out, err: err)

fn join_dots(ls: &[List[i64]]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ls.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o.push(46)
        for c in ls[i]
            o.push(c)
        i += 1
    return o

# 4.3 ToUnicode.
pub fn to_unicode(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    return Cps(cps: join_dots(&p.labels), err: p.err)

const ASCII_TAB: text = "\u{0}\u{1}\u{2}\u{3}\u{4}\u{5}\u{6}\u{7}\u{8}\t\n\u{b}\u{c}\r\u{e}\u{f}\u{10}\u{11}\u{12}\u{13}\u{14}\u{15}\u{16}\u{17}\u{18}\u{19}\u{1a}\u{1b}\u{1c}\u{1d}\u{1e}\u{1f} !\"#$%&'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~\u{7f}"

# ASCII code points as text; any other code point is written U+FFFD
# (only reachable in an output that also carries err).
pub fn ascii_text(cps: &[i64]) -> text
    let t = ASCII_TAB.chars()
    var o = ""
    for c in cps
        o = o + (if c >= 0 and c < 128 then copy(t[c as usize]) else "\u{fffd}")
    return o

# 4.2 ToASCII.
pub fn to_ascii_cps(input: &[i64], f: &Flags) -> Cps
    let p = process(input, f)
    var err = p.err
    var ls: List[List[i64]] = []
    for l in p.labels
        if all_ascii(&l)
            ls.push(copy(l))
        else
            let e = puny_encode(&l)
            if e.err
                err = true
                ls.push(copy(l))
                continue
            var x: List[i64] = [120, 110, 45, 45]
            for c in e.cps
                x.push(c)
