module num.linalg

# Dense real linear algebra over IEEE 754 binary64 (survey workstream A).
#
# Determinism. Every result is a fixed sequence of correctly rounded
# + - * / and sqrt (spec 6.3 N3: one result per operation on every
# target, no FMA contraction), so a call gives the same bits on every
# emit target. The order of every reduction is fixed and documented, and
# it is the order of the Reference BLAS and LAPACK 3.12.1 routine each
# function ports: a sum runs left to right in increasing index unless the
# routine says otherwise. Ported routines are checked bit for bit against
# Reference LAPACK 3.12.1 (tests/num/linalg_checks*.rce).
#
# Storage. A matrix is column major, element (i, j) of an m x n matrix at
# a[i + j * m] (0-based), like LAPACK with lda = m. Functions on raw
# storage take an offset and a leading dimension (or stride) so the
# LAPACK index arithmetic carries over unchanged.
#
# Non-finite values trap like every f64 operation (6.3 N3), so NaN and
# infinity never appear; the NaN branches of LAPACK are dead here.

pub struct Mat
    m: usize
    n: usize
    a: List[f64]

# One error type: why is "shape", "singular" (at = 0-based column of the
# first zero pivot) or "not positive definite" (at = failing column).
error LaError(why: text, at: i64)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- model
# Binary64 parameters (LAPACK DLAMCH): eps = 2^-53 ('E', round to
# nearest), safe minimum = 2^-1022 ('S'), overflow = (1 - 2^-53) 2^1024.

pub fn la_pow2(k: i64) -> f64
    var r = 1.0
    var i: i64 = 0
    if k >= 0
        while i < k bound 1100
            r = r * 2.0
            i += 1
    else
        while i > k bound 1100
            r = r * 0.5
            i -= 1
    return r

pub const LA_EPS: f64 = 1.1102230246251565e-16
pub const LA_SFMIN: f64 = 2.2250738585072014e-308
pub const LA_HUGE: f64 = 1.7976931348623157e308

pub fn la_abs(x: f64) -> f64 = if x < 0.0 then 0.0 - x else x

# Fortran SIGN(a, b): |a| with the sign of b (b >= 0 counts as positive;
# there is no negative zero).
pub fn la_sign(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64 = if b >= 0.0 then la_abs(a) else 0.0 - la_abs(a)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- BLAS 1
# Vectors are (list, offset, stride); strides are positive.

# DDOT: sum of x[i] * y[i], i = 0..n-1 in order (the unrolled reference
# loop associates left to right, so it is the same order).
pub fn ddot(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize) -> f64
    var t = 0.0
    for i in 0..n
        t = t + x[ox + i * ix] * y[oy + i * iy]
    return t

# DAXPY: y := y + alpha * x (no-op when alpha == 0).
pub fn daxpy(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, y: &mut List[f64], oy: usize, iy: usize)
    if alpha == 0.0
        return
    for i in 0..n
        y[oy + i * iy] = y[oy + i * iy] + alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSCAL: x := alpha * x.
pub fn dscal(n: usize, alpha: f64, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize)
    for i in 0..n
        x[ox + i * ix] = alpha * x[ox + i * ix]

# DSWAP.
pub fn dswap(n: usize, x: &mut List[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize, oy: usize, iy: usize)
    for i in 0..n
        let t = x[ox + i * ix]
        x[ox + i * ix] = x[oy + i * iy]
        x[oy + i * iy] = t

# DASUM: sum of |x[i]| in order.
pub fn dasum(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
    var t = 0.0
    for i in 0..n
        t = t + la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
    return t

# IDAMAX: first index (0-based) of the largest |x[i]|; 0 for n == 0.
pub fn idamax(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> usize
    var k: usize = 0
    if n == 0
        return 0
    var mx = la_abs(x[ox])
    for i in 1..n
        let v = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
        if v > mx
            k = i
            mx = v
    return k

# DNRM2 of Reference BLAS 3.10+ (Anderson 2017, Blue's three
# accumulators): no overflow or harmful underflow for any finite input.
# tsml = 2^-511, tbig = 2^486, ssml = 2^537, sbig = 2^-538.
pub fn dnrm2(n: usize, x: &[f64], ox: usize, ix: usize) -> f64
    if n == 0
        return 0.0
    let tsml = la_pow2(-511)
    let tbig = la_pow2(486)
    let ssml = la_pow2(537)
    let sbig = la_pow2(-538)
    var notbig = true
    var asml = 0.0
    var amed = 0.0
    var abig = 0.0
    for i in 0..n
        let ax = la_abs(x[ox + i * ix])
        if ax > tbig
            let t = ax * sbig
            abig = abig + t * t
            notbig = false
        elif ax < tsml
            if notbig
                let t = ax * ssml
                asml = asml + t * t
        else
            amed = amed + ax * ax
    var scl = 1.0
    var sumsq = 0.0
    if abig > 0.0
        if amed > 0.0
            abig = abig + (amed * sbig) * sbig
        scl = 1.0 / sbig
        sumsq = abig
    elif asml > 0.0
        if amed > 0.0
            let am = amed.sqrt()
            let asm = asml.sqrt() / ssml
            var ymin = asm
            var ymax = am
            if asm > am
                ymin = am
                ymax = asm
            let r = ymin / ymax
            sumsq = ymax * ymax * (1.0 + r * r)
        else
            scl = 1.0 / ssml
            sumsq = asml
    else
        sumsq = amed
    return scl * sumsq.sqrt()

# DLAPY2: sqrt(x^2 + y^2) without needless overflow.
pub fn dlapy2(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64
    let xa = la_abs(x)
    let ya = la_abs(y)
    let w = xa.max(ya)
    let z = xa.min(ya)
    if z == 0.0
        return w
    let r = z / w
    return w * (1.0 + r * r).sqrt()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- kernels
# The BLAS 2/3 and LAPACK kernels below work in place on one buffer w, so
# the operand aliasing of the reference code (a routine updating part of
# A from another part of A) is expressed with offsets. Arguments follow
# the Fortran ones: o* offsets, ld* leading dimensions, inc* strides.

pub fn axpy_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, alpha: f64, ox: usize, ix: usize, oy: usize, iy: usize)
    if alpha == 0.0
        return
    for i in 0..n
        w[oy + i * iy] = w[oy + i * iy] + alpha * w[ox + i * ix]

# DGEMV: y := alpha op(A) x + beta y, A m x n. trans false: y has m
# entries, columns j = 0.. in order add (alpha x[j]) A[:, j]. trans true:
# y[j] += alpha (sum over i in order of A[i, j] x[i]).
pub fn gemv_b(w: &mut List[f64], trans: bool, m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ox: usize, incx: usize, beta: f64, oy: usize, incy: usize)
    if m == 0 or n == 0 or (alpha == 0.0 and beta == 1.0)
        return
    let leny = if trans then n else m
    if beta != 1.0
        for i in 0..leny
            if beta == 0.0
                w[oy + i * incy] = 0.0
            else
                w[oy + i * incy] = beta * w[oy + i * incy]
    if alpha == 0.0
        return
    if not trans
        for j in 0..n
            let t = alpha * w[ox + j * incx]
            for i in 0..m
                w[oy + i * incy] = w[oy + i * incy] + t * w[oa + i + j * lda]
    else
        for j in 0..n
            var t = 0.0
            for i in 0..m
                t = t + w[oa + i + j * lda] * w[ox + i * incx]
            w[oy + j * incy] = w[oy + j * incy] + alpha * t

# DGER: A := A + alpha x y^T, column by column, skipping y[j] == 0.
pub fn ger_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, ox: usize, incx: usize, oy: usize, incy: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize)
    if m == 0 or n == 0 or alpha == 0.0
        return
    for j in 0..n
        if w[oy + j * incy] != 0.0
            let t = alpha * w[oy + j * incy]
            for i in 0..m
                w[oa + i + j * lda] = w[oa + i + j * lda] + w[ox + i * incx] * t

# DTRSM, left side: B := alpha inv(op(A)) B, A m x m triangular, B m x n.
pub fn trsm_b(w: &mut List[f64], upper: bool, trans: bool, unit: bool, m: usize, n: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize)
    if m == 0 or n == 0
        return
    if alpha == 0.0
        for j in 0..n
            for i in 0..m
                w[ob + i + j * ldb] = 0.0
        return
    for j in 0..n
        let c = ob + j * ldb
        if not trans
            if alpha != 1.0
                for i in 0..m
                    w[c + i] = alpha * w[c + i]
            if upper
                var k = m
                while k > 0 bound 1048576
                    k -= 1
                    if w[c + k] != 0.0
                        if not unit
                            w[c + k] = w[c + k] / w[oa + k + k * lda]
                        let bk = w[c + k]
                        for i in 0..k
                            w[c + i] = w[c + i] - bk * w[oa + i + k * lda]
            else
                for k in 0..m
                    if w[c + k] != 0.0
                        if not unit
                            w[c + k] = w[c + k] / w[oa + k + k * lda]
                        let bk = w[c + k]
                        for i in (k + 1)..m
                            w[c + i] = w[c + i] - bk * w[oa + i + k * lda]
        else
            if upper
                for i in 0..m
                    var t = alpha * w[c + i]
                    for k in 0..i
                        t = t - w[oa + k + i * lda] * w[c + k]
                    if not unit
                        t = t / w[oa + i + i * lda]
                    w[c + i] = t
            else
                var i = m
                while i > 0 bound 1048576
                    i -= 1
                    var t = alpha * w[c + i]
                    for k in (i + 1)..m
                        t = t - w[oa + k + i * lda] * w[c + k]
                    if not unit
                        t = t / w[oa + i + i * lda]
                    w[c + i] = t

# DGEMM: C := alpha op(A) op(B) + beta C, C m x n, inner dimension k.
# The four loop orders are those of the reference routine: for op(A) = A
# the update is column-oriented (C[:, j] += (alpha B[l, j]) A[:, l] for
# l = 0.. in order); for op(A) = A^T each C[i, j] is one dot product in
# increasing l, then alpha t + beta C[i, j].
pub fn gemm_b(w: &mut List[f64], ta: bool, tb: bool, m: usize, n: usize, k: usize, alpha: f64, oa: usize, lda: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize, beta: f64, oc: usize, ldc: usize)
    if m == 0 or n == 0 or ((alpha == 0.0 or k == 0) and beta == 1.0)
        return
    if alpha == 0.0
        for j in 0..n
            for i in 0..m
                if beta == 0.0
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = 0.0
                else
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]
        return
    for j in 0..n
        if not ta
            if beta == 0.0
                for i in 0..m
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = 0.0
            elif beta != 1.0
                for i in 0..m
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]
            for l in 0..k
                let bl = if tb then w[ob + j + l * ldb] else w[ob + l + j * ldb]
                let t = alpha * bl
                for i in 0..m
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = w[oc + i + j * ldc] + t * w[oa + i + l * lda]
        else
            for i in 0..m
                var t = 0.0
                for l in 0..k
                    let bl = if tb then w[ob + j + l * ldb] else w[ob + l + j * ldb]
                    t = t + w[oa + l + i * lda] * bl
                if beta == 0.0
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = alpha * t
                else
                    w[oc + i + j * ldc] = alpha * t + beta * w[oc + i + j * ldc]

# DGETF2: unblocked LU with partial pivoting (first largest |a| wins),
# multipliers scaled by the reciprocal of the pivot when |pivot| >= SFMIN
# (as the reference does), else divided. piv[j] is the 0-based row
# swapped with row j. Returns LAPACK INFO: 0, or j + 1 for the first exact
# zero pivot (the factorization still completes).
pub fn getf2_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, piv: &mut List[i64]) -> i64
    var info: i64 = 0
    let mn = if m < n then m else n
    for j in 0..mn
        let jp = j + idamax(m - j, w, oa + j + j * lda, 1)
        piv.push(jp as i64)
        if w[oa + jp + j * lda] != 0.0
            if jp != j
                dswap(n, w, oa + j, lda, oa + jp, lda)
            if j + 1 < m
                let p = w[oa + j + j * lda]
                if la_abs(p) >= LA_SFMIN
                    dscal(m - j - 1, 1.0 / p, w, oa + j + 1 + j * lda, 1)
                else
                    for i in 1..(m - j)
                        w[oa + j + i + j * lda] = w[oa + j + i + j * lda] / p
        elif info == 0
            info = (j + 1) as i64
        if j + 1 < mn
            ger_b(w, m - j - 1, n - j - 1, -1.0, oa + j + 1 + j * lda, 1, oa + j + (j + 1) * lda, lda, oa + j + 1 + (j + 1) * lda, lda)
    return info

# DLASWP over columns 0..n-1 of B, rows k1..k2-1, forward or backward.
pub fn laswp_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, ob: usize, ldb: usize, k1: usize, k2: usize, piv: &[i64], forward: bool)
    var s: usize = 0
    while s < k2 - k1 bound 1048576
        let i = if forward then k1 + s else k2 - 1 - s
        let p = piv[i] as usize
        if p != i
            dswap(n, w, ob + i, ldb, ob + p, ldb)
        s += 1

# DPOTF2, lower: A = L L^T column by column; ajj = a[j, j] minus the dot
# of row j of L with itself (increasing k). Returns INFO (0 or j + 1).
pub fn potf2_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize) -> i64
    for j in 0..n
        let ajj = w[oa + j + j * lda] - ddot(j, w, oa + j, lda, w, oa + j, lda)
        if ajj <= 0.0
            w[oa + j + j * lda] = ajj
            return (j + 1) as i64
        let r = ajj.sqrt()
        w[oa + j + j * lda] = r
        if j + 1 < n
            gemv_b(w, false, n - j - 1, j, -1.0, oa + j + 1, lda, oa + j, lda, 1.0, oa + j + 1 + j * lda, 1)
            dscal(n - j - 1, 1.0 / r, w, oa + j + 1 + j * lda, 1)
    return 0

# DLARFG: elementary reflector H = I - tau v v^T with H [alpha; x] =
# [beta; 0], v[0] = 1. Overwrites alpha (at oalpha) with beta and x with
# v[1..]. Returns tau.
pub fn larfg_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: usize, oalpha: usize, ox: usize, incx: usize) -> f64
    if n <= 1
        return 0.0
    var xnorm = dnrm2(n - 1, w, ox, incx)
    if xnorm == 0.0
        return 0.0
    var alpha = w[oalpha]
    var beta = 0.0 - la_sign(dlapy2(alpha, xnorm), alpha)
    let safmin = LA_SFMIN / LA_EPS
    var knt = 0
    if la_abs(beta) < safmin
        let rsafmn = 1.0 / safmin
        while knt < 20 bound 21
            knt += 1
            dscal(n - 1, rsafmn, w, ox, incx)
            beta = beta * rsafmn
            alpha = alpha * rsafmn
            if la_abs(beta) >= safmin
                break
        xnorm = dnrm2(n - 1, w, ox, incx)
        beta = 0.0 - la_sign(dlapy2(alpha, xnorm), alpha)
    let tau = (beta - alpha) / beta
    dscal(n - 1, 1.0 / (alpha - beta), w, ox, incx)
    for _ in 0..knt
        beta = beta * safmin
    w[oalpha] = beta
    return tau

# ILADLC: 1 + last column of the m x n block with a nonzero entry (0 if
# none). ILADLR: 1 + last such row.
pub fn iladlc_b(w: &[f64], m: usize, n: usize, oc: usize, ldc: usize) -> usize
    var j = n
    while j > 0 bound 1048576
        for i in 0..m
            if w[oc + i + (j - 1) * ldc] != 0.0
                return j
        j -= 1
    return 0

pub fn iladlr_b(w: &[f64], m: usize, n: usize, oc: usize, ldc: usize) -> usize
    var r: usize = 0
    for j in 0..n
        var i = m
        while i > 0 bound 1048576
            if w[oc + (i - 1) + j * ldc] != 0.0
                break
            i -= 1
        if i > r
            r = i
    return r

# DLARF1F: apply H = I - tau v v^T (v[0] = 1 implied, v[1..] stored at
# ov + incv..) to the m x n block C from the left (left true) or right,
# using the scratch area owork (n or m entries).
pub fn larf1f_b(w: &mut List[f64], left: bool, m: usize, n: usize, ov: usize, incv: usize, tau: f64, oc: usize, ldc: usize, owork: usize)
    var lastv: usize = 1
    var lastc: usize = 0
    if tau != 0.0
        lastv = if left then m else n
        while lastv > 1 and w[ov + (lastv - 1) * incv] == 0.0 bound 1048576
            lastv -= 1
        lastc = if left then iladlc_b(w, lastv, n, oc, ldc) else iladlr_b(w, m, lastv, oc, ldc)
    if lastc == 0
        return
    if left
        if lastv == 1
            dscal(lastc, 1.0 - tau, w, oc, ldc)
        else
            gemv_b(w, true, lastv - 1, lastc, 1.0, oc + 1, ldc, ov + incv, incv, 0.0, owork, 1)
            for j in 0..lastc
                w[owork + j] = w[owork + j] + w[oc + j * ldc]
            for j in 0..lastc
                w[oc + j * ldc] = w[oc + j * ldc] + (0.0 - tau) * w[owork + j]
            ger_b(w, lastv - 1, lastc, 0.0 - tau, ov + incv, incv, owork, 1, oc + 1, ldc)
    else
        if lastv == 1
            dscal(lastc, 1.0 - tau, w, oc, 1)
        else
            gemv_b(w, false, lastc, lastv - 1, 1.0, oc + ldc, ldc, ov + incv, incv, 0.0, owork, 1)
            for i in 0..lastc
                w[owork + i] = w[owork + i] + w[oc + i]
            for i in 0..lastc
                w[oc + i] = w[oc + i] + (0.0 - tau) * w[owork + i]
            ger_b(w, lastc, lastv - 1, 0.0 - tau, owork, 1, ov + incv, incv, oc + ldc, ldc)

# DGEQR2: A = Q R by Householder reflectors, column by column. R is left
# in the upper triangle, the reflectors below it, tau at otau.. (k =
# min(m, n) entries). Scratch at owork (n entries).
pub fn geqr2_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, otau: usize, owork: usize)
    let k = if m < n then m else n
    for i in 0..k
        let below = if i + 1 < m then i + 1 else m - 1
        let t = larfg_b(w, m - i, oa + i + i * lda, oa + below + i * lda, 1)
        w[otau + i] = t
        if i + 1 < n
            larf1f_b(w, true, m - i, n - i - 1, oa + i + i * lda, 1, t, oa + i + (i + 1) * lda, lda, owork)

# DORG2R: overwrite the m x n block (holding k reflectors from geqr2)
# with the first n columns of Q.
pub fn org2r_b(w: &mut List[f64], m: usize, n: usize, k: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, otau: usize, owork: usize)
    for j in k..n
        for l in 0..m
            w[oa + l + j * lda] = 0.0
        w[oa + j + j * lda] = 1.0
    var i = k
    while i > 0 bound 1048576
        i -= 1
        let t = w[otau + i]
        if i + 1 < n
            larf1f_b(w, true, m - i, n - i - 1, oa + i + i * lda, 1, t, oa + i + (i + 1) * lda, lda, owork)
        if i + 1 < m
            dscal(m - i - 1, 0.0 - t, w, oa + i + 1 + i * lda, 1)
        w[oa + i + i * lda] = 1.0 - t
        for l in 0..i
            w[oa + l + i * lda] = 0.0

# DORM2R, left side: C := Q^T C (trans) or Q C, Q from k reflectors of
# geqr2 stored at oa (m x k, lda), C m x n.
pub fn orm2r_b(w: &mut List[f64], trans: bool, m: usize, n: usize, k: usize, oa: usize, lda: usize, otau: usize, oc: usize, ldc: usize, owork: usize)
    for s in 0..k
        let i = if trans then s else k - 1 - s
        larf1f_b(w, true, m - i, n, oa + i + i * lda, 1, w[otau + i], oc + i, ldc, owork)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- matrices

pub fn mat(m: usize, n: usize, a: List[f64]) -> Mat ! LaError
    if a.len() != m * n
        fail LaError(why: "data length is not m * n", at: -1)
    return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

# From row-major data (the order matrices are usually written in).
pub fn from_rows(m: usize, n: usize, r: &[f64]) -> Mat ! LaError
    if r.len() != m * n
        fail LaError(why: "data length is not m * n", at: -1)
    var a: List[f64] = []
    for j in 0..n
        for i in 0..m
            a.push(r[i * n + j])
    return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

pub fn to_rows(x: &Mat) -> List[f64]
    var r: List[f64] = []
    for i in 0..x.m
        for j in 0..x.n
            r.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
    return r

pub fn zeros(m: usize, n: usize) -> Mat
    var a: List[f64] = []
    for _ in 0..(m * n)
        a.push(0.0)
    return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: a)

pub fn eye(n: usize) -> Mat
    var z = zeros(n, n)
    for i in 0..n
        z.a[i + i * n] = 1.0
    return z

pub fn mat_at(x: &Mat, i: usize, j: usize) -> f64 = x.a[i + j * x.m]

pub fn transpose(x: &Mat) -> Mat
    var a: List[f64] = []
    for i in 0..x.m
        for j in 0..x.n
            a.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
    return Mat(m: x.n, n: x.m, a: a)

pub fn mat_col(x: &Mat, j: usize) -> List[f64]
    var c: List[f64] = []
    for i in 0..x.m
        c.push(x.a[i + j * x.m])
    return c

fn la_cat(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> List[f64]
    var w: List[f64] = []
    for v in a
        w.push(v)
    for v in b
        w.push(v)
    return w

fn la_slice(w: &[f64], o: usize, n: usize) -> List[f64]
    var r: List[f64] = []
    for i in 0..n
        r.push(w[o + i])
    return r

# C = alpha op(A) op(B) + beta C (DGEMM order).
pub fn gemm(ta: bool, tb: bool, alpha: f64, a: &Mat, b: &Mat, beta: f64, c: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let m = if ta then a.n else a.m
    let k = if ta then a.m else a.n
    let kb = if tb then b.n else b.m
    let n = if tb then b.m else b.n
    if k != kb or c.m != m or c.n != n
        fail LaError(why: "gemm dimensions", at: -1)
    let ob = a.a.len()
    let oc = ob + b.a.len()
    let ab = la_cat(&a.a, &b.a)
    var w = la_cat(&ab, &c.a)
    gemm_b(&mut w, ta, tb, m, n, k, alpha, 0, a.m, ob, b.m, beta, oc, m)
    return Mat(m: m, n: n, a: la_slice(&w, oc, m * n))

pub fn matmul(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let c = zeros(a.m, b.n)
    return try gemm(false, false, 1.0, a, b, 0.0, &c)

# y = alpha op(A) x + beta y (DGEMV order).
pub fn gemv(trans: bool, alpha: f64, a: &Mat, x: &[f64], beta: f64, y: &[f64]) -> List[f64] ! LaError
    let lx = if trans then a.m else a.n
    let ly = if trans then a.n else a.m
    if x.len() != lx or y.len() != ly
        fail LaError(why: "gemv dimensions", at: -1)
    let ox = a.a.len()
    let oy = ox + x.len()
    let ax = la_cat(&a.a, x)
    var w = la_cat(&ax, y)
    gemv_b(&mut w, trans, a.m, a.n, alpha, 0, a.m, ox, 1, beta, oy, 1)
    return la_slice(&w, oy, ly)

pub fn matvec(a: &Mat, x: &[f64]) -> List[f64] ! LaError
    var y: List[f64] = []
    for _ in 0..a.m
        y.push(0.0)
    return try gemv(false, 1.0, a, x, 0.0, &y)

# A + alpha x y^T (DGER order).
pub fn ger(alpha: f64, x: &[f64], y: &[f64], a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    if x.len() != a.m or y.len() != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "ger dimensions", at: -1)
    let ox = a.a.len()
    let oy = ox + x.len()
    let ax = la_cat(&a.a, x)
    var w = la_cat(&ax, y)
    ger_b(&mut w, a.m, a.n, alpha, ox, 1, oy, 1, 0, a.m)
    return Mat(m: a.m, n: a.n, a: la_slice(&w, 0, a.a.len()))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- LU

pub struct Lu
    lu: Mat
    piv: List[i64]
    info: i64

# P A = L U (DGETF2). info > 0 marks an exact zero pivot (U singular).
pub fn lu(a: &Mat) -> Lu
    var w = copy(a.a)
    var piv: List[i64] = []
    let info = getf2_b(&mut w, a.m, a.n, 0, a.m, &mut piv)
    return Lu(lu: Mat(m: a.m, n: a.n, a: w), piv: piv, info: info)

# Solve A X = B (trans false) or A^T X = B from a square LU (DGETRS).
pub fn lu_solve(f: &Lu, trans: bool, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let n = f.lu.n
    if f.lu.m != n or b.m != n
        fail LaError(why: "lu_solve dimensions", at: -1)
    if f.info > 0
        fail LaError(why: "singular", at: f.info - 1)
    let ob = n * n
    var w = la_cat(&f.lu.a, &b.a)
    if not trans
        laswp_b(&mut w, b.n, ob, n, 0, n, &f.piv, true)
        trsm_b(&mut w, false, false, true, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
        trsm_b(&mut w, true, false, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
    else
        trsm_b(&mut w, true, true, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
        trsm_b(&mut w, false, true, true, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
        laswp_b(&mut w, b.n, ob, n, 0, n, &f.piv, false)
    return Mat(m: n, n: b.n, a: la_slice(&w, ob, n * b.n))

pub fn solve(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    if a.m != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "solve needs a square matrix", at: -1)
    let f = lu(a)
    return try lu_solve(&f, false, b)

# Inverse as the solution of A X = I (DGETRS on the identity).
pub fn inv(a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let i = eye(a.n)
    return try solve(a, &i)

# Determinant: product of the U diagonal in increasing index, negated
# once per row swap.
pub fn det(a: &Mat) -> f64 ! LaError
    if a.m != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "det needs a square matrix", at: -1)
    let f = lu(a)
    var d = 1.0
    for i in 0..a.n
        d = d * f.lu.a[i + i * a.n]
        if f.piv[i] != i as i64
            d = 0.0 - d
    return d

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Cholesky

# A = L L^T for symmetric positive definite A (DPOTF2, lower; only the
# lower triangle of A is read). L is returned with a zero upper triangle.
pub fn chol(a: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    if a.m != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "chol needs a square matrix", at: -1)
    let n = a.n
    var w = copy(a.a)
    let info = potf2_b(&mut w, n, 0, n)
    if info > 0
        fail LaError(why: "not positive definite", at: info - 1)
    for j in 0..n
        for i in 0..j
            w[i + j * n] = 0.0
    return Mat(m: n, n: n, a: w)

# Solve A X = B from L (DPOTRS, lower).
pub fn chol_solve(l: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let n = l.n
    if l.m != n or b.m != n
        fail LaError(why: "chol_solve dimensions", at: -1)
    let ob = n * n
    var w = la_cat(&l.a, &b.a)
    trsm_b(&mut w, false, false, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
    trsm_b(&mut w, false, true, false, n, b.n, 1.0, 0, n, ob, n)
    return Mat(m: n, n: b.n, a: la_slice(&w, ob, n * b.n))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- QR

pub struct Qr
    qr: Mat
    tau: List[f64]

# A = Q R, Householder (DGEQR2): R in the upper triangle of qr, the
# reflectors below it.
pub fn qr(a: &Mat) -> Qr
    let m = a.m
    let n = a.n
    let k = if m < n then m else n
    let ot = m * n
    let ow = ot + k
    var w = copy(a.a)
    for _ in 0..(k + n)
        w.push(0.0)
    geqr2_b(&mut w, m, n, 0, m, ot, ow)
    return Qr(qr: Mat(m: m, n: n, a: la_slice(&w, 0, m * n)), tau: la_slice(&w, ot, k))

# The m x k orthonormal factor (DORG2R), k = min(m, n).
pub fn qr_q(f: &Qr) -> Mat
    let m = f.qr.m
    let k = f.tau.len()
    let ot = m * k
    var w = la_slice(&f.qr.a, 0, m * k)
    for t in &f.tau
        w.push(t)
    for _ in 0..k
        w.push(0.0)
    org2r_b(&mut w, m, k, k, 0, m, ot, ot + k)
    return Mat(m: m, n: k, a: la_slice(&w, 0, m * k))

# The k x n upper triangular factor.
pub fn qr_r(f: &Qr) -> Mat
    let m = f.qr.m
    let n = f.qr.n
    let k = f.tau.len()
    var r = zeros(k, n)
    for j in 0..n
        for i in 0..k
            if i <= j
                r.a[i + j * k] = f.qr.a[i + j * m]
    return r

# Least squares min ||A X - B|| for m >= n and full rank (DGELS 'N' for
# matrices below the blocking crossover: DGEQR2, DORM2R, DTRTRS; the
# DGELS rescaling only acts outside [SFMIN/EPS, EPS/SFMIN] and is not
# reproduced: such inputs are refused with Shape).
pub fn lstsq(a: &Mat, b: &Mat) -> Mat ! LaError
    let m = a.m
    let n = a.n
    if m < n or b.m != m
        fail LaError(why: "lstsq needs m >= n and b with m rows", at: -1)
    var amax = 0.0
    for v in &a.a
        amax = amax.max(la_abs(v))
    let smlnum = LA_SFMIN / (2.0 * LA_EPS)
    if amax == 0.0 or amax < smlnum or amax > 1.0 / smlnum
        fail LaError(why: "lstsq: A is zero or outside the unscaled range", at: -1)
    let nrhs = b.n
    let ot = m * n
    let ob = ot + n
    let ow = ob + m * nrhs
    let z = zeros(n, 1)
    let az = la_cat(&a.a, &z.a)
    var w = la_cat(&az, &b.a)
    let wl = if n > nrhs then n else nrhs
    for _ in 0..wl
        w.push(0.0)
    geqr2_b(&mut w, m, n, 0, m, ot, ow)
    orm2r_b(&mut w, true, m, nrhs, n, 0, m, ot, ob, m, ow)
    for i in 0..n
        if w[i + i * m] == 0.0
            fail LaError(why: "singular", at: i as i64)
    trsm_b(&mut w, true, false, false, n, nrhs, 1.0, 0, m, ob, m)
    var x = zeros(n, nrhs)
    for j in 0..nrhs
        for i in 0..n
            x.a[i + j * n] = w[ob + i + j * m]
    return x

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Jacobi
# Symmetric eigenproblem and SVD by Jacobi rotations (Jacobi 1846;
# Rutishauser's update, Handbook for Automatic Computation II/1; one-sided
# form of Hestenes 1958). Chosen over QR iteration because Jacobi computes
# small eigenvalues and singular values of well-scaled matrices to high
# relative accuracy (Demmel and Veselic, SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 13,
# 1992) and its sweep order is a fixed, simple sequence. Order: cyclic by
# rows, (p, q) = (0, 1), (0, 2), .., (0, n-1), (1, 2), ..; a sweep without
# a rotation ends the iteration (at most 80 sweeps). Rotation for a pivot
# with off-diagonal g and diagonal (or squared column norms) a, b:
#   zeta = (b - a) / (2 g), t = sign(zeta) / (|zeta| + sqrt(1 + zeta^2)),
#   c = 1 / sqrt(1 + t^2), s = c t   (|zeta| > 2^500: t = 1 / (2 zeta)).
# A pivot is skipped when |g| <= EPS sqrt(|a| |b|) (the relative
# criterion), and also when |g| is below SFMIN / EPS.

fn la_rot(a: f64, b: f64, g: f64) -> List[f64]
    let zeta = (b - a) / (2.0 * g)
    var t = 0.0
    if la_abs(zeta) > la_pow2(500)
        t = 1.0 / (2.0 * zeta)
    else
        t = la_sign(1.0, zeta) / (la_abs(zeta) + (1.0 + zeta * zeta).sqrt())
    let c = 1.0 / (1.0 + t * t).sqrt()
    return [c, c * t, t]

pub struct Eigh
    values: List[f64]
    vectors: Mat

# Sort key order: ascending (asc) or descending; ties keep index order.
fn la_order(v: &[f64], asc: bool) -> List[usize]
    var idx: List[usize] = []
    for i in 0..v.len()
        idx.push(i)
    for i in 0..v.len()
        var best = i
        for j in (i + 1)..v.len()
            let better = if asc then v[idx[j]] < v[idx[best]] else v[idx[j]] > v[idx[best]]
            if better
                best = j
        let t = idx[i]
        idx[i] = idx[best]
        idx[best] = t
    return idx

# Sign convention for a computed vector: the entry of largest magnitude
# (first one on ties) is made positive.
fn la_fix_sign(w: &mut List[f64], o: usize, n: usize)
    let k = idamax(n, w, o, 1)
    if w[o + k] < 0.0
        for i in 0..n
            w[o + i] = 0.0 - w[o + i]

# Eigenvalues (ascending) and orthonormal eigenvectors (columns) of a
# symmetric matrix; only the lower triangle is read.
pub fn eigh(a: &Mat) -> Eigh ! LaError
    if a.m != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "eigh needs a square matrix", at: -1)
    let n = a.n
    var w: List[f64] = []
    for j in 0..n
        for i in 0..n
            w.push(if i >= j then a.a[i + j * n] else a.a[j + i * n])
    var v = eye(n).a
    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < 80 bound 81
        sweep += 1
        var rotated = false
        for p in 0..n
            for q in (p + 1)..n
                let g = w[p + q * n]
                let app = w[p + p * n]
                let aqq = w[q + q * n]
                if la_abs(g) > LA_EPS * (la_abs(app) * la_abs(aqq)).sqrt() and la_abs(g) > LA_SFMIN / LA_EPS
                    rotated = true
                    let r = la_rot(app, aqq, g)
                    let c = r[0]
                    let s = r[1]
                    let t = r[2]
                    w[p + p * n] = app - t * g
                    w[q + q * n] = aqq + t * g
                    w[p + q * n] = 0.0
                    w[q + p * n] = 0.0
                    for k in 0..n
                        if k != p and k != q
                            let akp = w[k + p * n]
                            let akq = w[k + q * n]
                            let np = c * akp - s * akq
                            let nq = s * akp + c * akq
                            w[k + p * n] = np
                            w[p + k * n] = np
                            w[k + q * n] = nq
                            w[q + k * n] = nq
                    for k in 0..n
                        let vkp = v[k + p * n]
                        let vkq = v[k + q * n]
                        v[k + p * n] = c * vkp - s * vkq
                        v[k + q * n] = s * vkp + c * vkq
        if not rotated
            break
    var d: List[f64] = []
    for i in 0..n
        d.push(w[i + i * n])
    let idx = la_order(&d, true)
    var vals: List[f64] = []
    var vs: List[f64] = []
    for j in 0..n
        vals.push(d[idx[j]])
        for i in 0..n
            vs.push(v[i + idx[j] * n])
        la_fix_sign(&mut vs, j * n, n)
    return Eigh(values: vals, vectors: Mat(m: n, n: n, a: vs))

# One-sided rotation from the column norms np, nq and their cosine cs:
# zeta = (nq/np - np/nq) / (2 cs); when the norms differ by more than
# 2^500, t = cs nq/np or -cs np/nq (the first-order value, exact to
# working precision there).
fn la_rot2(np: f64, nq: f64, cs: f64) -> List[f64]
    var t = 0.0
    let big = la_pow2(500)
    if np < nq and nq / big > np
        t = cs * (np / nq)
    elif nq < np and np / big > nq
        t = 0.0 - cs * (nq / np)
    else
        let zeta = (nq / np - np / nq) / (2.0 * cs)
        if la_abs(zeta) > big
            t = 1.0 / (2.0 * zeta)
        else
            t = la_sign(1.0, zeta) / (la_abs(zeta) + (1.0 + zeta * zeta).sqrt())
    let c = 1.0 / (1.0 + t * t).sqrt()
    return [c, c * t]

# Complete the columns j with zero singular value to an orthonormal set:
# column j becomes the standard basis vector e_i (smallest i among those
# with the largest residual) orthogonalized twice (classical Gram-Schmidt,
# DDOT order) against the columns already set, then normalized.
fn la_complete(u: &mut List[f64], m: usize, k: usize, s: &[f64])
    var done: List[usize] = []
    for j in 0..k
        if s[j] > 0.0
            done.push(j)
    for j in 0..k
        if s[j] > 0.0
            continue
        var best: List[f64] = []
        var bn = -1.0
        for i in 0..m
            var x: List[f64] = []
            for r in 0..m
                x.push(if r == i then 1.0 else 0.0)
            for _ in 0..2
                for c in &done
                    let d = ddot(m, u, c * m, 1, &x, 0, 1)
                    for r in 0..m
                        x[r] = x[r] - d * u[r + c * m]
            let xn = dnrm2(m, &x, 0, 1)
            if xn > bn
                bn = xn
                best = x
        for r in 0..m
            u[r + j * m] = best[r] / bn
        done.push(j)

pub struct Svd
    u: Mat
    s: List[f64]
    v: Mat

# Thin SVD A = U diag(s) V^T, s descending, k = min(m, n): U m x k, V n x
# k. One-sided Jacobi on the columns (on A^T when m < n). The matrix is
# first scaled by a power of two (exact) so its largest entry is in
# [1, 2). At every pivot the column norms are recomputed (DNRM2) and the
# cosine is the DDOT-order sum of the normalized entries, so neither
# underflows for badly scaled columns; the pivot is skipped when
# |cos| <= EPS. A U column whose (scaled) singular value is below
# SFMIN / EPS has no reliable direction (its entries are subnormal); it
# and the columns of zero singular values are completed to an
# orthonormal basis (la_complete).
pub fn svd(a: &Mat) -> Svd
    if a.m < a.n
        let tr = transpose(a)
        let r = la_svd_tall(&tr)
        return Svd(u: copy(r.v), s: copy(r.s), v: copy(r.u))
    return la_svd_tall(a)

fn la_svd_tall(a: &Mat) -> Svd
    let m = a.m
    let n = a.n
    var amax = 0.0
    for x in &a.a
        amax = amax.max(la_abs(x))
    var e: i64 = 0
    var sc = 1.0
    if amax > 0.0
        while amax * sc >= 2.0 bound 1100
            sc = sc * 0.5
            e += 1
        while amax * sc < 1.0 bound 1100
            sc = sc * 2.0
            e -= 1
    var w: List[f64] = []
    for x in &a.a
        w.push(x * sc)
    var v = eye(n).a
    var sweep = 0
    while sweep < 80 bound 81
        sweep += 1
        var rotated = false
        for p in 0..n
            for q in (p + 1)..n
                let np = dnrm2(m, &w, p * m, 1)
                let nq = dnrm2(m, &w, q * m, 1)
                var cs = 0.0
                if np > 0.0 and nq > 0.0
                    for k in 0..m
                        cs = cs + (w[k + p * m] / np) * (w[k + q * m] / nq)
                if la_abs(cs) > LA_EPS
                    rotated = true
                    let r = la_rot2(np, nq, cs)
                    let c = r[0]
                    let s = r[1]
                    for k in 0..m
                        let x = w[k + p * m]
                        let y = w[k + q * m]
                        w[k + p * m] = c * x - s * y
                        w[k + q * m] = s * x + c * y
                    for k in 0..n
                        let x = v[k + p * n]
                        let y = v[k + q * n]
                        v[k + p * n] = c * x - s * y
                        v[k + q * n] = s * x + c * y
        if not rotated
            break
    var sv: List[f64] = []
    for j in 0..n
        sv.push(dnrm2(m, &w, j * m, 1))
    let idx = la_order(&sv, false)
    let unsc = la_pow2(e)
    let tiny = LA_SFMIN / LA_EPS
    var s: List[f64] = []
    var live: List[f64] = []
    var u: List[f64] = []
    var vv: List[f64] = []
    for j in 0..n
        let k = idx[j]
        let sj = sv[k]
        s.push(sj * unsc)
        live.push(if sj >= tiny then sj else 0.0)
        for i in 0..m
            u.push(if sj >= tiny then w[i + k * m] / sj else 0.0)
        for i in 0..n
            vv.push(v[i + k * n])
        let ku = idamax(m, &u, j * m, 1)
        let kv = idamax(n, &vv, j * n, 1)
        let neg = if sj >= tiny then u[j * m + ku] < 0.0 else vv[j * n + kv] < 0.0
        if neg
            for i in 0..m
                u[j * m + i] = 0.0 - u[j * m + i]
            for i in 0..n
                vv[j * n + i] = 0.0 - vv[j * n + i]
    la_complete(&mut u, m, n, &live)
    return Svd(u: Mat(m: m, n: n, a: u), s: s, v: Mat(m: n, n: n, a: vv))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- nonsymmetric eigenvalues
# Eigenvalues of a general real matrix as Reference LAPACK 3.12.1 DGEEV
# computes them without vectors for n below its blocking crossovers
# (n <= 32 here): DGEBAL ('B': permute, then scale by powers of 2),
# DGEHD2 (Householder Hessenberg reduction), DHSEQR -> DLAHQR (double
# shift QR, exceptional shifts every 10 iterations, the Ahues and Tisseur
# deflation test) with DLANV2 for 2 x 2 blocks. Indices below are 1-based
# as in the Fortran so the port reads line for line.

fn fx(i: i64, j: i64, ld: i64) -> usize = ((i - 1) + (j - 1) * ld) as usize

pub struct Balanced
    ilo: i64
    ihi: i64
    scale: List[f64]

# DGEBAL, job 'B', in place on the n x n matrix at w[0..].
pub fn gebal_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: i64) -> Balanced
    var scale: List[f64] = []
    for _ in 0..n
        scale.push(1.0)
    if n == 0
        return Balanced(ilo: 1, ihi: 0, scale: scale)
    var k: i64 = 1
    var l: i64 = n
    var noconv = true
    while noconv bound 1048576
        noconv = false
        let l0 = l
        var i = l0
        while i >= 1 bound 1048576
            var canswap = true
            var j: i64 = 1
            while j <= l bound 1048576
                if i != j and w[fx(i, j, n)] != 0.0
                    canswap = false
                    break
                j += 1
            if canswap
                scale[(l - 1) as usize] = i as f64
                if i != l
                    dswap(l as usize, w, fx(1, i, n), 1, fx(1, l, n), 1)
                    dswap((n - k + 1) as usize, w, fx(i, k, n), n as usize, fx(l, k, n), n as usize)
                noconv = true
                if l == 1
                    return Balanced(ilo: 1, ihi: 1, scale: scale)
                l -= 1
            i -= 1
    noconv = true
    while noconv bound 1048576
        noconv = false
        let k0 = k
        let l0 = l
        var j = k0
        while j <= l0 bound 1048576
            var canswap = true
            var i = k
            while i <= l bound 1048576
                if i != j and w[fx(i, j, n)] != 0.0
                    canswap = false
                    break
                i += 1
            if canswap
                scale[(k - 1) as usize] = j as f64
                if j != k
                    dswap(l as usize, w, fx(1, j, n), 1, fx(1, k, n), 1)
                    dswap((n - k + 1) as usize, w, fx(j, k, n), n as usize, fx(k, k, n), n as usize)
                noconv = true
                k += 1
            j += 1
    let sfmin1 = LA_SFMIN / (2.0 * LA_EPS)
    let sfmax1 = 1.0 / sfmin1
    let sfmin2 = sfmin1 * 2.0
    let sfmax2 = 1.0 / sfmin2
    noconv = true
    while noconv bound 1048576
        noconv = false
        var i = k
        while i <= l bound 1048576
            var c = dnrm2((l - k + 1) as usize, w, fx(k, i, n), 1)
            var r = dnrm2((l - k + 1) as usize, w, fx(i, k, n), n as usize)
            let ica = idamax(l as usize, w, fx(1, i, n), 1)
            var ca = la_abs(w[fx(1, i, n) + ica])
            let ira = idamax((n - k + 1) as usize, w, fx(i, k, n), n as usize)
            var ra = la_abs(w[fx(i, k, n) + ira * (n as usize)])
            if c == 0.0 or r == 0.0
                i += 1
                continue
            var g = r / 2.0
            var f = 1.0
            let s = c + r
            while c < g and f.max(c).max(ca) < sfmax2 and r.min(g).min(ra) > sfmin2 bound 4096
                f = f * 2.0
                c = c * 2.0
                ca = ca * 2.0
                r = r / 2.0
                g = g / 2.0
                ra = ra / 2.0
            g = c / 2.0
            while g >= r and r.max(ra) < sfmax2 and f.min(c).min(g).min(ca) > sfmin2 bound 4096
                f = f / 2.0
                c = c / 2.0
                g = g / 2.0
                ca = ca / 2.0
                r = r * 2.0
                ra = ra * 2.0
            let si = scale[(i - 1) as usize]
            var skip = c + r >= 0.95 * s
            if not skip and f < 1.0 and si < 1.0 and f * si <= sfmin1
                skip = true
            if not skip and f > 1.0 and si > 1.0 and si >= sfmax1 / f
                skip = true
            if not skip
                scale[(i - 1) as usize] = si * f
                noconv = true
                dscal((n - k + 1) as usize, 1.0 / f, w, fx(i, k, n), n as usize)
                dscal(l as usize, f, w, fx(1, i, n), 1)
            i += 1
    return Balanced(ilo: k, ihi: l, scale: scale)

# DGEHD2 on rows/columns ilo..ihi of the n x n matrix at w[0..]; tau
# and work areas at otau (n entries) and owork (n entries).
pub fn gehd2_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: i64, ilo: i64, ihi: i64, otau: usize, owork: usize)
    var i = ilo
    while i <= ihi - 1 bound 1048576
        let below = if i + 2 < n then i + 2 else n
        let t = larfg_b(w, (ihi - i) as usize, fx(i + 1, i, n), fx(below, i, n), 1)
        w[otau + (i - 1) as usize] = t
        larf1f_b(w, false, ihi as usize, (ihi - i) as usize, fx(i + 1, i, n), 1, t, fx(1, i + 1, n), n as usize, owork)
        larf1f_b(w, true, (ihi - i) as usize, (n - i) as usize, fx(i + 1, i, n), 1, t, fx(i + 1, i + 1, n), n as usize, owork)
        i += 1

# DLANV2: Schur factorization of a real 2 x 2 nonsymmetric matrix in
# standardized form. Returns [a, b, c, d, rt1r, rt1i, rt2r, rt2i, cs, sn].
pub fn lanv2(a0: f64, b0: f64, c0: f64, d0: f64) -> List[f64]
    var a = a0
    var b = b0
    var c = c0
    var d = d0
    let eps = 2.0 * LA_EPS
    let safmn2 = la_pow2(-485)
    let safmx2 = 1.0 / safmn2
    var cs = 1.0
    var sn = 0.0
    if c == 0.0
        cs = 1.0
        sn = 0.0
    elif b == 0.0
        cs = 0.0
        sn = 1.0
        let t = d
        d = a
        a = t
        b = 0.0 - c
        c = 0.0
    elif a - d == 0.0 and la_sign(1.0, b) != la_sign(1.0, c)
        cs = 1.0
        sn = 0.0
    else
        var temp = a - d
        var p = 0.5 * temp
        let bcmax = la_abs(b).max(la_abs(c))
        let bcmis = la_abs(b).min(la_abs(c)) * la_sign(1.0, b) * la_sign(1.0, c)
        var scale = la_abs(p).max(bcmax)
        var z = (p / scale) * p + (bcmax / scale) * bcmis
        if z >= 4.0 * eps
            z = p + la_sign(scale.sqrt() * z.sqrt(), p)
            a = d + z
            d = d - (bcmax / z) * bcmis
            let tau = dlapy2(c, z)
            cs = z / tau

# DLAHQR with WANTT = WANTZ = false on the Hessenberg matrix at w[0..]
# (n x n, active block ilo..ihi). Eigenvalues go to wr, wi (1-based i at
# index i - 1). Returns INFO (0, or the index where 30 max(10, nh)
# iterations did not converge).
pub fn lahqr_b(w: &mut List[f64], n: i64, ilo: i64, ihi: i64, wr: &mut List[f64], wi: &mut List[f64]) -> i64
    if n == 0
        return 0
    if ilo == ihi
        wr[(ilo - 1) as usize] = w[fx(ilo, ilo, n)]
        wi[(ilo - 1) as usize] = 0.0
        return 0

    while jj <= ihi - 3 bound 1048576
        w[fx(jj + 2, jj, n)] = 0.0
        w[fx(jj + 3, jj, n)] = 0.0
        jj += 1
    if ilo <= ihi - 2
        w[fx(ihi, ihi - 2, n)] = 0.0
    let nh = ihi - ilo + 1
    let safmin = LA_SFMIN
    let ulp = 2.0 * LA_EPS
    let smlnum = safmin * ((nh as f64) / ulp)
    let itmax = 30 * (if nh > 10 then nh else 10)
    var kdefl: i64 = 0
    var i = ihi
    var v: List[f64] = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    while i >= ilo bound 1048576
        var l = ilo
        var converged = false
        var its: i64 = 0
        while its <= itmax bound 1048576
            var k = i
            while k >= l + 1 bound 1048576
                let hk = la_abs(w[fx(k, k - 1, n)])
                if hk <= smlnum
                    break
                var tst = la_abs(w[fx(k - 1, k - 1, n)]) + la_abs(w[fx(k, k, n)])
                if tst == 0.0
                    if k - 2 >= ilo
                        tst = tst + la_abs(w[fx(k - 1, k - 2, n)])
                    if k + 1 <= ihi
                        tst = tst + la_abs(w[fx(k + 1, k, n)])
                if hk <= ulp * tst
                    let hu = la_abs(w[fx(k - 1, k, n)])
                    let ab = hk.max(hu)
                    let ba = hk.min(hu)
                    let hkk = la_abs(w[fx(k, k, n)])
                    let hdf = la_abs(w[fx(k - 1, k - 1, n)] - w[fx(k, k, n)])
                    let aa = hkk.max(hdf)
                    let bb = hkk.min(hdf)
                    let s = aa + ab
                    if ba * (ab / s) <= smlnum.max(ulp * (bb * (aa / s)))
                        break
                k -= 1
            l = k
            if l > ilo
                w[fx(l, l - 1, n)] = 0.0
            if l >= i - 1
                converged = true
                break
            kdefl += 1
            let i1 = l
            let i2 = i
            var h11 = 0.0
            var h12 = 0.0
            var h21 = 0.0
            var h22 = 0.0
            if kdefl % 20 == 0
                let s = la_abs(w[fx(i, i - 1, n)]) + la_abs(w[fx(i - 1, i - 2, n)])
                h11 = 0.75 * s + w[fx(i, i, n)]
                h12 = -0.4375 * s
                h21 = s
                h22 = h11
            elif kdefl % 10 == 0
                let s = la_abs(w[fx(l + 1, l, n)]) + la_abs(w[fx(l + 2, l + 1, n)])
                h11 = 0.75 * s + w[fx(l, l, n)]
                h12 = -0.4375 * s
                h21 = s
                h22 = h11
            else
                h11 = w[fx(i - 1, i - 1, n)]
                h21 = w[fx(i, i - 1, n)]
                h12 = w[fx(i - 1, i, n)]
                h22 = w[fx(i, i, n)]
            let s = la_abs(h11) + la_abs(h12) + la_abs(h21) + la_abs(h22)
            var rt1r = 0.0
            var rt1i = 0.0
            var rt2r = 0.0
            var rt2i = 0.0
            if s != 0.0
                h11 = h11 / s
                h21 = h21 / s
                h12 = h12 / s
                h22 = h22 / s
                let tr = (h11 + h22) / 2.0
                let dt = (h11 - tr) * (h22 - tr) - h12 * h21
                let rtdisc = la_abs(dt).sqrt()

                    rt1r = tr * s
                    rt2r = rt1r
                    rt1i = rtdisc * s
                    rt2i = 0.0 - rt1i
                else

                    rt2r = tr - rtdisc

                        rt2r = rt1r

                    rt2i = 0.0

                v[2] = h21s * w[fx(m + 2, m + 1, n)]

                v[0] = v[0] / s3
                v[1] = v[1] / s3
                v[2] = v[2] / s3

                    let t3 = t1 * v3

                    while j <= i2 bound 1048576

                        w[fx(kk + 1, j, n)] = w[fx(kk + 1, j, n)] - sm * t2
                        w[fx(kk + 2, j, n)] = w[fx(kk + 2, j, n)] - sm * t3

                        w[fx(j, kk + 1, n)] = w[fx(j, kk + 1, n)] - sm * t2
                        w[fx(j, kk + 2, n)] = w[fx(j, kk + 2, n)] - sm * t3
                        j += 1

                    while j <= i2 bound 1048576

                        w[fx(kk, j, n)] = w[fx(kk, j, n)] - sm * t1
                        w[fx(kk + 1, j, n)] = w[fx(kk + 1, j, n)] - sm * t2
                        j += 1

                        w[fx(j, kk, n)] = w[fx(j, kk, n)] - sm * t1
                        w[fx(j, kk + 1, n)] = w[fx(j, kk + 1, n)] - sm * t2

            wi[(i - 1) as usize] = 0.0
        elif l == i - 1

            w[fx(i - 1, i - 1, n)] = r[0]
            w[fx(i - 1, i, n)] = r[1]
            w[fx(i, i - 1, n)] = r[2]
            w[fx(i, i, n)] = r[3]
            wr[(i - 2) as usize] = r[4]
            wi[(i - 2) as usize] = r[5]
            wr[(i - 1) as usize] = r[6]
            wi[(i - 1) as usize] = r[7]
        kdefl = 0
        i = l - 1
    return 0

pub struct Eigvals
    re: List[f64]
    im: List[f64]

# Eigenvalues of a general square matrix, in DGEEV order (complex pairs
# adjacent, positive imaginary part first). Fails with why
# "no convergence" (at = LAPACK INFO) in the rare case DLAHQR gives up.
# Inputs whose largest entry lies outside [sqrt(SFMIN)/EPS,
# EPS/sqrt(SFMIN)] would be rescaled by DGEEV first; they are refused.
pub fn eigvals(a: &Mat) -> Eigvals ! LaError
    if a.m != a.n
        fail LaError(why: "eigvals needs a square matrix", at: -1)
    let n = a.n as i64
    var amax = 0.0
    for x in &a.a
        amax = amax.max(la_abs(x))
    let smlnum = LA_SFMIN.sqrt() / (2.0 * LA_EPS)
    if amax > 0.0 and (amax < smlnum or amax > 1.0 / smlnum)
        fail LaError(why: "eigvals: entries outside the unscaled range", at: -1)
    var w = copy(a.a)
    let otau = w.len()
    for _ in 0..(2 * a.n)
        w.push(0.0)
    let bal = gebal_b(&mut w, n)
    gehd2_b(&mut w, n, bal.ilo, bal.ihi, otau, otau + a.n)
    var wr: List[f64] = []
    var wi: List[f64] = []
    for _ in 0..a.n
        wr.push(0.0)
        wi.push(0.0)
    var q: i64 = 1
    while q <= n bound 1048576
        if q < bal.ilo or q > bal.ihi
            wr[(q - 1) as usize] = w[fx(q, q, n)]
        q += 1
    let info = lahqr_b(&mut w, n, bal.ilo, bal.ihi, &mut wr, &mut wi)
    if info > 0
        fail LaError(why: "no convergence", at: info)
    return Eigvals(re: wr, im: wi)

# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.

        let v22 = if v36 >= 0 then v36 else v44
        v23 = v23 + "."
        var v15: i64 = 0
        while v15 < v22
            v23 = v23 + (if v15 < v51 then copy(v41[v15 as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            v15 += 1
        v52 = v52 + 1 + v22 as usize
    v23 = v23 + v40
    if v37 < 0 or v37 as usize <= v52
        return v23
    let v53 = v37 - v52 as i64
    let v54 = if v38 == ">" then v53 else (if v38 == "^" then v53 / 2 else 0)
    return f34(v54) + v23 + f34(v53 - v54)

pub fn f36(v21: &t0, v36: i64, v37: i64, v38: &text, v55: bool) -> text
    let v56 = if v55 then "+" else ""
    let v11 = "s"
    let v57 = "ms"
    let v58 = "µs"
    let v59 = "ns"
    if v21.v6 > 0
        return f35(v21.v6, v21.v7, v1 / 10, v36, v37, v38, &v56, &v11)
    if v21.v7 >= 1000000
        return f35((v21.v7 / 1000000) as u64, v21.v7 % 1000000, 100000, v36, v37, v38, &v56, &v57)
    if v21.v7 >= 1000
        return f35((v21.v7 / 1000) as u64, v21.v7 % 1000, 100, v36, v37, v38, &v56, &v58)
    return f35(v21.v7 as u64, 0, 1, v36, v37, v38, &v56, &v59)

pub fn f37(v21: &t0) -> text
    let v26 = ""
    return f36(v21, -1, -1, &v26, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------
pub struct t1
    v6: i64
    v7: i64

pub fn f38(v6: i64, v7: i64) -> t1 ! x0
    if v7 < 0 or v7 >= v1
        fail x0(v0: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return t1(v6: v6, v7: v7)

pub fn f39() -> t1 = t1(v6: v5, v7: 0)
pub fn f40() -> t1 = t1(v6: v4, v7: v1 - 1)

pub fn f41(v26: &t1, v27: &t1) -> i64
    if v26.v6 != v27.v6
        return if v26.v6 < v27.v6 then -1 else 1
    if v26.v7 != v27.v7
        return if v26.v7 < v27.v7 then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn f42(v26: &t1, v27: &t1) -> bool = f41(v26, v27) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn f43(v13: i64, v21: u64) -> i64?
    if v13 >= 0
        if v21 > (v4 - v13) as u64
            return none
        return some(v13 + v21 as i64)
    let v60 = v4 as u64 + (0 - (v13 + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if v21 > v60
        return none
    if v21 <= v4 as u64
        return some(v13 + v21 as i64)
    return some((v13 + v4 + 1) + (v21 - v4 as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn f44(v13: i64, v21: u64) -> i64?
    if v13 < 0
        if v21 > (v13 - v5) as u64
            return none
        return some(v13 - v21 as i64)
    let v60 = v13 as u64 + v4 as u64 + 1
    if v21 > v60
        return none
    if v21 <= v4 as u64
        return some(v13 - v21 as i64)
    return some((v13 - v4 - 1) - (v21 - v4 as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn f45(v13: &t1, v21: &t0) -> t1?
    var v9: i64 = 0
    match f43(v13.v6, v21.v6)
        some(v78) -> v9 = v78
        none -> return none
    var v19 = v13.v7 + v21.v7
    if v19 >= v1
        if v9 == v4
            return none
        v9 += 1
        v19 -= v1
    return some(t1(v6: v9, v7: v19))

pub fn f46(v13: &t1, v21: &t0) -> t1?
    var v9: i64 = 0
    match f44(v13.v6, v21.v6)
        some(v78) -> v9 = v78
        none -> return none
    var v19 = v13.v7 - v21.v7
    if v19 < 0
        if v9 == v5
            return none
        v9 -= 1
        v19 += v1
    return some(t1(v6: v9, v7: v19))

pub fn f47(v13: &t1, v21: &t0) -> t1 = f45(v13, v21).or(f40())
pub fn f48(v13: &t1, v21: &t0) -> t1 = f46(v13, v21).or(f39())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct t2
    v61: bool
    v21: t0

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn f49(v26: i64, v27: i64) -> u64
    if v27 >= 0 or v26 < 0
        return (v26 - v27) as u64
    return v26 as u64 + (0 - (v27 + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn f50(v26: &t1, v27: &t1) -> t0
    if v26.v7 >= v27.v7
        return t0(v6: f49(v26.v6, v27.v6), v7: v26.v7 - v27.v7)
    return t0(v6: f49(v26.v6, v27.v6) - 1, v7: v26.v7 + v1 - v27.v7)

pub fn f51(v26: &t1, v27: &t1) -> t2
    if f41(v26, v27) >= 0
        return t2(v61: true, v21: f50(v26, v27))
    return t2(v61: false, v21: f50(v27, v26))

pub fn f52(v26: &t1, v62: &t1) -> t0?
    let v50 = f51(v26, v62)
    if v50.v61
        return some(copy(v50.v21))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn f53(v26: &t1, v62: &t1) -> t0 = f52(v26, v62).or(f0())

# ---------------- wasi:clocks@0.2.8 ----------------

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn f54(v12: u64) -> t1 = t1(v6: (v12 / v2) as i64, v7: (v12 % v2) as i64)

pub fn f55(v13: &t1) -> u64 ! x0
    if v13.v6 < 0 or v13.v6 as u64 > (v3 - v13.v7 as u64) / v2
        fail x0(v0: "instant out of range")
    return v13.v6 as u64 * v2 + v13.v7 as u64

# wall-clock datetime: "The nanoseconds field of the output is always less than 1000000000."
# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn f56(v63: u64, v64: i64) -> t1 ! x0
    if v63 > v4 as u64
        fail x0(v0: "seconds out of range")
    return f38(v63 as i64, v64)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------
pub struct t3
    v65: t1
    v66: bool
    v67: i64

pub fn f57() -> t3 = t3(v65: t1(v6: 0, v7: 0), v66: false, v67: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn f58(v68: &mut t3, v50: &t1) -> t1
    if v68.v66 and f41(v50, &v68.v65) < 0
        v68.v67 += 1
        return copy(v68.v65)
    v68.v65 = copy(v50)
    v68.v66 = true
    return copy(v50)

# ---------------- timers ----------------
pub struct t4
    v69: i64
    v70: t1
    v71: i64

pub struct t5
    v72: List[t4]
    v73: i64

pub fn f59() -> t5 = t5(v72: [], v73: 0)

fn f60(v26: &t4, v27: &t4) -> bool
    let v17 = f41(&v26.v70, &v27.v70)
    return v17 < 0 or (v17 == 0 and v26.v71 < v27.v71)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn f61(v74: &mut t5, v75: &t1, v69: i64)
    let v13 = t4(v69: v69, v70: copy(v75), v71: v74.v73)
    v74.v73 += 1
    var v76: List[t4] = []
    var v77 = false
    for v78 in v74.v72
        if not v77 and f60(&v13, &v78)
            v76.push(copy(v13))
            v77 = true
        v76.push(copy(v78))
    if not v77
        v76.push(copy(v13))
    v74.v72 = v76

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn f62(v74: &mut t5, v79: &t1, v21: &t0, v69: i64)
    let v70 = f47(v79, v21)
    f61(v74, &v70, v69)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn f63(v74: &mut t5, v69: i64) -> bool
    var v76: List[t4] = []
    var v80 = false
    for v78 in v74.v72
        if v78.v69 == v69
            v80 = true
        else
            v76.push(copy(v78))
    v74.v72 = v76
    return v80

pub fn f64(v74: &t5) -> usize = v74.v72.len()

pub fn f65(v74: &t5) -> t1?
    if v74.v72.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(v74.v72[0].v70))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn f66(v74: &mut t5, v79: &t1) -> List[i64]
    var v81: List[i64] = []
    var v82: List[t4] = []
    for v78 in v74.v72
        if f41(&v78.v70, v79) <= 0
            v81.push(v78.v69)
        else
            v82.push(copy(v78))
    v74.v72 = v82
    return v81

module os.clock

# Clocks and timers (survey M37), pure. A program never reads a clock: the
# host admits each monotonic or wall reading as a logged event, and it
# admits each timer firing as an event in D order, so replay is exact.
# This module holds what a program does with those values:
# - Dur, Rust's core::time::Duration (secs plus nanos below one second)
#   with its constructors, accessors, checked and saturating arithmetic and
#   its Debug formatting ("1.5s", "7.1µs", precision, width, alignment).
#   Secs are u64 as in Rust, so the full range holds.
# - Timespec, the point type behind Rust's unix Instant and SystemTime
#   (secs i64, nanos 0..1e9), with checked and saturating add/sub and
#   duration_since in Rust's forms (saturating, checked, signed result).
# - wasi:clocks@0.2.8 values: a monotonic instant (u64 ns) and a wall
#   datetime (seconds, nanoseconds < 1e9) mapped to Timespec.
# - Mono, the admission rule for monotonic readings: a reading below the
#   last admitted one is raised to it (non-decreasing, as wasi-clocks
#   promises and as Rust's monotonize enforces).
# - Timers, the pure timer queue: subscribe at an instant or after a
#   duration; a tick at `now` fires every due timer in (deadline, subscribe
#   order) order. The host admits those firings as events in that order.

error BadClock(why: text)

pub const NANOS_PER_SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const NPS: u64 = 1000000000
pub const MAX_U: u64 = 18446744073709551615
pub const MAX_SECS: i64 = 9223372036854775807
pub const MIN_SECS: i64 = -9223372036854775808

# secs is u64 as in Rust, so the full range up to u64::MAX seconds holds.
pub struct Dur
    secs: u64
    nanos: i64

pub fn dur_zero() -> Dur = Dur(secs: 0, nanos: 0)
pub fn dur_max() -> Dur = Dur(secs: MAX_U, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

# Duration::new: nanos beyond a second carry into secs; overflow fails.
pub fn dur_new(secs: u64, nanos: i64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0
        fail BadClock(why: "negative nanoseconds")
    let extra = (nanos / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64
    if extra > MAX_U - secs
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::new")
    return Dur(secs: secs + extra, nanos: nanos % NANOS_PER_SEC)

pub fn from_secs(s: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: s, nanos: 0)
pub fn from_millis(ms: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ms / 1000, nanos: (ms % 1000) as i64 * 1000000)
pub fn from_micros(us: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: us / 1000000, nanos: (us % 1000000) as i64 * 1000)
pub fn from_nanos(ns: u64) -> Dur = Dur(secs: ns / NPS, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

# Duration::from_nanos_u128 for a u128 given as decimal digits: the last
# nine digits are the nanos, the rest the secs (must fit u64).
pub fn from_nanos_text(t: &text) -> Dur ! BadClock
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        fail BadClock(why: "empty")
    var secs: u64 = 0
    var nanos: i64 = 0
    var k: usize = 0
    let cut: usize = if cs.len() > 9 then cs.len() - 9 else 0
    for c in cs
        let v = c[0] as i64 - 48
        if v < 0 or v > 9
            fail BadClock(why: "not a decimal")
        if k < cut
            if secs > (MAX_U - v as u64) / 10
                fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration::from_nanos_u128")
            secs = secs * 10 + v as u64
        else
            nanos = nanos * 10 + v
        k += 1
    return Dur(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

fn from_unit(n: u64, unit: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock
    if n > MAX_U / unit
        fail BadClock(why: "overflow in Duration constructor")
    return Dur(secs: n * unit, nanos: 0)

pub fn from_mins(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 60)
pub fn from_hours(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 3600)
pub fn from_days(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 86400)
pub fn from_weeks(n: u64) -> Dur ! BadClock = from_unit(n, 604800)

pub fn as_secs(d: &Dur) -> u64 = d.secs
pub fn subsec_millis(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000000
pub fn subsec_micros(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos / 1000
pub fn subsec_nanos(d: &Dur) -> i64 = d.nanos
pub fn is_zero(d: &Dur) -> bool = d.secs == 0 and d.nanos == 0
# Total as decimal text (Rust's u128 as_nanos, as_micros, as_millis), exact.
fn pad9(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var o = v.tostr()
    while (o.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 9
        o = "0" + o
    return o
fn in_units(d: &Dur, digits: i64, unit: i64) -> text
    let part = d.nanos / unit
    if d.secs == 0
        return part.tostr()
    return d.secs.tostr() + pad9(part, digits)
pub fn as_nanos(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 9, 1)
pub fn as_micros(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 6, 1000)
pub fn as_millis(d: &Dur) -> text = in_units(d, 3, 1000000)

pub fn dur_cmp(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn dur_eq(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> bool = dur_cmp(a, b) == 0

pub fn checked_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if b.secs > MAX_U - a.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs + b.secs
    var n = a.nanos + b.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_U
            return none
        s += 1
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn checked_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur?
    if a.secs < b.secs
        return none
    var s = a.secs - b.secs
    var n = a.nanos - b.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == 0
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Dur(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn saturating_add(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_add(a, b).or(dur_max())
pub fn saturating_sub(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur = checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())

pub fn abs_diff(a: &Dur, b: &Dur) -> Dur
    if dur_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return checked_sub(a, b).or(dur_zero())
    return checked_sub(b, a).or(dur_zero())

# Multiplier and divisor are u32 in Rust: 0 ..= 4294967295.
pub fn checked_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k < 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let total = a.nanos as u64 * ku
    let extra = total / NPS
    if ku != 0 and a.secs > (MAX_U - extra) / ku
        return none
    return some(Dur(secs: a.secs * ku + extra, nanos: (total % NPS) as i64))

pub fn saturating_mul(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur = checked_mul(a, k).or(dur_max())

pub fn checked_div(a: &Dur, k: i64) -> Dur?
    if k <= 0 or k > 4294967295
        return none
    let ku = k as u64
    let s = a.secs / ku
    let carry = a.secs % ku
    let extra = (carry * NPS + a.nanos as u64 % ku) / ku
    let n = a.nanos / k + extra as i64
    return some(Dur(secs: s + (n / NANOS_PER_SEC) as u64, nanos: n % NANOS_PER_SEC))

pub fn dur_sum(ds: &[Dur]) -> Dur?
    var acc = dur_zero()
    for d in ds
        match checked_add(&acc, &d)
            some(x) -> acc = x
            none -> return none
    return some(acc)

# ---------------- Debug formatting ----------------
# Rust's `{:?}` for Duration. prec < 0 means no precision; width < 0 means
# no width; align is "<", ">", "^" or "" (default left); plus is `{:+?}`.

fn spaces(n: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < n
        o = o + " "
        k += 1
    return o

fn fmt_decimal(ip0: u64, fp0: i64, div0: i64, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, prefix: &text, postfix: &text) -> text
    var buf: List[i64] = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    var fp = fp0
    var dv = div0
    var pos = 0
    let lim = if prec < 0 then 9 else prec
    while fp > 0 and pos < lim and pos < 9
        buf[pos as usize] = fp / dv
        fp = fp % dv
        dv = dv / 10
        pos += 1
    var ip = ip0
    var big = false
    if fp > 0 and fp >= dv * 5
        let tie = fp == dv * 5
        let odd = if pos > 0 then copy(buf[(pos - 1) as usize]) % 2 == 1 else ip % 2 == 1
        if not (tie and not odd)
            var r = pos
            var carry = true
            while carry and r > 0
                r -= 1
                if buf[r as usize] < 9
                    buf[r as usize] = copy(buf[r as usize]) + 1
                    carry = false
                else
                    buf[r as usize] = 0
            if carry
                if ip == MAX_U
                    big = true
                else
                    ip += 1
    let end = if prec >= 0 then (if prec < 9 then prec else 9) else pos
    var o = copy(prefix) + (if big then "18446744073709551616" else ip.tostr())
    var cells = prefix.chars().len() + postfix.chars().len() + (if big then 20 else ip.tostr().len_bytes())
    if end > 0
        let w = if prec >= 0 then prec else pos
        o = o + "."
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < w
            o = o + (if k < end then copy(buf[k as usize]).tostr() else "0")
            k += 1
        cells = cells + 1 + w as usize
    o = o + postfix
    if width < 0 or width as usize <= cells
        return o
    let padn = width - cells as i64
    let pre = if align == ">" then padn else (if align == "^" then padn / 2 else 0)
    return spaces(pre) + o + spaces(padn - pre)

pub fn dur_debug_with(d: &Dur, prec: i64, width: i64, align: &text, plus: bool) -> text
    let p = if plus then "+" else ""
    let us = "s"
    let ums = "ms"
    let uus = "µs"
    let uns = "ns"
    if d.secs > 0
        return fmt_decimal(d.secs, d.nanos, NANOS_PER_SEC / 10, prec, width, align, &p, &us)
    if d.nanos >= 1000000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000000, 100000, prec, width, align, &p, &ums)
    if d.nanos >= 1000
        return fmt_decimal((d.nanos / 1000) as u64, d.nanos % 1000, 100, prec, width, align, &p, &uus)
    return fmt_decimal(d.nanos as u64, 0, 1, prec, width, align, &p, &uns)

pub fn dur_debug(d: &Dur) -> text
    let a = ""
    return dur_debug_with(d, -1, -1, &a, false)

# ---------------- points in time ----------------

pub struct Timespec
    secs: i64
    nanos: i64

pub fn ts_new(secs: i64, nanos: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if nanos < 0 or nanos >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        fail BadClock(why: "nanoseconds out of range")
    return Timespec(secs: secs, nanos: nanos)

pub fn ts_min() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MIN_SECS, nanos: 0)
pub fn ts_max() -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: MAX_SECS, nanos: NANOS_PER_SEC - 1)

pub fn ts_cmp(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> i64
    if a.secs != b.secs
        return if a.secs < b.secs then -1 else 1
    if a.nanos != b.nanos
        return if a.nanos < b.nanos then -1 else 1
    return 0

pub fn ts_eq(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> bool = ts_cmp(a, b) == 0

# i64 + u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_add_unsigned.
fn add_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t >= 0
        if d > (MAX_SECS - t) as u64
            return none
        return some(t + d as i64)
    let room = MAX_SECS as u64 + (0 - (t + 1)) as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t + d as i64)
    return some((t + MAX_SECS + 1) + (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

# i64 - u64 exactly, as Rust's checked_sub_unsigned.
fn sub_unsigned(t: i64, d: u64) -> i64?
    if t < 0
        if d > (t - MIN_SECS) as u64
            return none
        return some(t - d as i64)
    let room = t as u64 + MAX_SECS as u64 + 1
    if d > room
        return none
    if d <= MAX_SECS as u64
        return some(t - d as i64)
    return some((t - MAX_SECS - 1) - (d - MAX_SECS as u64 - 1) as i64)

pub fn ts_checked_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match add_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos + d.nanos
    if n >= NANOS_PER_SEC
        if s == MAX_SECS
            return none
        s += 1
        n -= NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_checked_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec?
    var s: i64 = 0
    match sub_unsigned(t.secs, d.secs)
        some(x) -> s = x
        none -> return none
    var n = t.nanos - d.nanos
    if n < 0
        if s == MIN_SECS
            return none
        s -= 1
        n += NANOS_PER_SEC
    return some(Timespec(secs: s, nanos: n))

pub fn ts_saturating_add(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_add(t, d).or(ts_max())
pub fn ts_saturating_sub(t: &Timespec, d: &Dur) -> Timespec = ts_checked_sub(t, d).or(ts_min())

# Rust's sub_timespec: a - b as (sign, magnitude). ok is true when a >= b
# (SystemTime::duration_since Ok); otherwise the Dur is b - a (the Err
# value, SystemTimeError::duration).
pub struct Diff
    ok: bool
    d: Dur

# a - b for a >= b; the seconds difference can reach u64::MAX.
fn diff_u(a: i64, b: i64) -> u64
    if b >= 0 or a < 0
        return (a - b) as u64
    return a as u64 + (0 - (b + 1)) as u64 + 1

fn mag(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Dur
    if a.nanos >= b.nanos
        return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs), nanos: a.nanos - b.nanos)
    return Dur(secs: diff_u(a.secs, b.secs) - 1, nanos: a.nanos + NANOS_PER_SEC - b.nanos)

pub fn sub_timespec(a: &Timespec, b: &Timespec) -> Diff
    if ts_cmp(a, b) >= 0
        return Diff(ok: true, d: mag(a, b))
    return Diff(ok: false, d: mag(b, a))

pub fn checked_duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur?
    let r = sub_timespec(a, earlier)
    if r.ok
        return some(copy(r.d))
    return none

# Instant::duration_since and saturating_duration_since (zero when earlier is later).
pub fn duration_since(a: &Timespec, earlier: &Timespec) -> Dur = checked_duration_since(a, earlier).or(dur_zero())

# ---------------- wasi:clocks@0.2.8 ----------------

# monotonic-clock instant and duration are u64 ns.
pub fn mono_from_wasi(ns: u64) -> Timespec = Timespec(secs: (ns / NPS) as i64, nanos: (ns % NPS) as i64)

pub fn mono_to_wasi(t: &Timespec) -> u64 ! BadClock
    if t.secs < 0 or t.secs as u64 > (MAX_U - t.nanos as u64) / NPS
        fail BadClock(why: "instant out of range")
    return t.secs as u64 * NPS + t.nanos as u64

# wall-clock datetime: "The nanoseconds field of the output is always less than 1000000000."
# seconds is u64; past i64::MAX seconds it is beyond the unix point type.
pub fn wall_from_wasi(seconds: u64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Timespec ! BadClock
    if seconds > MAX_SECS as u64
        fail BadClock(why: "seconds out of range")
    return ts_new(seconds as i64, nanoseconds)

# ---------------- admission of monotonic readings ----------------

pub struct Mono
    last: Timespec
    seen: bool
    raised: i64

pub fn mono_new() -> Mono = Mono(last: Timespec(secs: 0, nanos: 0), seen: false, raised: 0)

# Admit one reading; returns the value the program sees.
pub fn mono_admit(m: &mut Mono, r: &Timespec) -> Timespec
    if m.seen and ts_cmp(r, &m.last) < 0
        m.raised += 1
        return copy(m.last)
    m.last = copy(r)
    m.seen = true
    return copy(r)

# ---------------- timers ----------------

pub struct Timer
    id: i64
    at: Timespec
    seq: i64

pub struct Timers
    list: List[Timer]
    next: i64

pub fn timers_new() -> Timers = Timers(list: [], next: 0)

fn before(a: &Timer, b: &Timer) -> bool
    let c = ts_cmp(&a.at, &b.at)
    return c < 0 or (c == 0 and a.seq < b.seq)

# wasi subscribe-instant. Timers are kept in firing order.
pub fn subscribe_instant(q: &mut Timers, when: &Timespec, id: i64)
    let t = Timer(id: id, at: copy(when), seq: q.next)
    q.next += 1
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in q.list
        if not placed and before(&t, &x)
            out.push(copy(t))
            placed = true
        out.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        out.push(copy(t))
    q.list = out

# wasi subscribe-duration: due at now + d (saturating at the end of time).
pub fn subscribe_duration(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec, d: &Dur, id: i64)
    let at = ts_saturating_add(now, d)
    subscribe_instant(q, &at, id)

# Cancel every pending timer with this id; true when one was pending.
pub fn cancel(q: &mut Timers, id: i64) -> bool
    var out: List[Timer] = []
    var hit = false
    for x in q.list
        if x.id == id
            hit = true
        else
            out.push(copy(x))
    q.list = out
    return hit

pub fn pending(q: &Timers) -> usize = q.list.len()

pub fn next_deadline(q: &Timers) -> Timespec?
    if q.list.len() == 0
        return none
    return some(copy(q.list[0].at))

# A tick at `now`: the ids of every timer due (deadline <= now), in the
# order the host admits their events; they leave the queue.
pub fn fire(q: &mut Timers, now: &Timespec) -> List[i64]
    var ids: List[i64] = []
    var rest: List[Timer] = []
    for x in q.list
        if ts_cmp(&x.at, now) <= 0
            ids.push(x.id)
        else
            rest.push(copy(x))
    q.list = rest
    return ids

#  - SPI: the spidev mode bits (uapi spi.h), clock idle level and edges
#    per mode, word bit order;

error BadDevice(why: text)

const HEX: text = "0123456789abcdef"

fn hexv(c: &text) -> i64
    let d = HEX.chars()
    let l = c.lower()
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 16 bound 16
        if d[i as usize] == l
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

fn hex2(b: i64) -> text
    let d = HEX.chars()
    return d[((b >> 4) & 15) as usize] + d[(b & 15) as usize]

# ---------------- UEFI ----------------

# The 16 bytes of an EFI_GUID in memory from its registry text
# "aabbccdd-eeff-gghh-iijj-kkllmmnnoopp": Data1 (u32), Data2, Data3 (u16)
# little endian, Data4 as written.
pub fn guid_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64] ! BadDevice
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() != 36 or cs[8] != "-" or cs[13] != "-" or cs[18] != "-" or cs[23] != "-"
        fail BadDevice(why: "bad GUID")
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < 36 bound 64
        if i == 8 or i == 13 or i == 18 or i == 23
            i += 1
            continue
        let a = hexv(&cs[i])

pub const MAX_BIT: i64 = -9223372036854775808

        return 0

    for e in STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if e == name and e != "-"
            return MAX_BIT | i
        i += 1
    i = 1
    for w in STATUS_WARNINGS.split(" ")
        if w == name
            return i
        i += 1

    if v == 0
        return "SUCCESS"
    let code = v & 9223372036854775807
    if v < 0
        let es = STATUS_ERRORS.split(" ")
        if code >= 1 and code <= es.len() as i64 and es[(code - 1) as usize] != "-"
            return copy(es[(code - 1) as usize])
        return ""

    if code <= ws.len() as i64
        return copy(ws[(code - 1) as usize])
    return ""

const MEMORY_TYPES: text = "EfiReservedMemoryType EfiLoaderCode EfiLoaderData EfiBootServicesCode EfiBootServicesData EfiRuntimeServicesCode EfiRuntimeServicesData EfiConventionalMemory EfiUnusableMemory EfiACPIReclaimMemory EfiACPIMemoryNVS EfiMemoryMappedIO EfiMemoryMappedIOPortSpace EfiPalCode EfiPersistentMemory EfiUnacceptedMemoryType EfiMaxMemoryType"

    var i: i64 = 0

        if x == name
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn memory_type(name: &text) -> i64 = index_of(&MEMORY_TYPES, name)

        return -1

    var i = prefix.chars().len()

pub const I2C_M_TEN: i64 = 16

pub fn i2c_addr_valid(addr: i64, ten: bool) -> bool
    if ten
        return addr >= 0 and addr <= 1023
    return addr > 0 and addr <= 127

pub fn i2c_addr_valid_strict(addr: i64) -> bool = addr >= 8 and addr <= 119

pub fn i2c_addr_byte(addr: i64, flags: i64) -> i64 = ((addr << 1) | (flags & I2C_M_RD)) & 255

pub fn i2c_ten_bit_bytes(addr: i64, read: bool) -> List[i64] = [240 | ((addr >> 7) & 6) | (if read then 1 else 0), addr & 255]

fn crc8_step(d: i64) -> i64
    var data = d & 65535
    var i = 0
    while i < 8 bound 8
        if data & 32768 != 0
            data = data ^ (4208 << 3)
        data = data << 1
        i += 1
    return (data >> 8) & 255

pub fn smbus_pec(crc: i64, bytes: &List[i64]) -> i64
    var c = crc
    for b in bytes
        c = crc8_step(((c ^ b) & 255) << 8)
    return c

# each message adds its address byte, then its data.

    addr: i64
    flags: i64
    data: List[i64]

    var pec: i64 = 0

        pec = smbus_pec(pec, &ab)
        pec = smbus_pec(pec, &m.data)

    addr: i64
    bytes: List[i64]

        let e = copy(expected[i])
        let a = copy(actual[i])

            return i as i64
        i += 1
    if i < expected.len()
        return i as i64
    return -1

pub const SPI_CPOL: i64 = 2
pub const SPI_CS_HIGH: i64 = 4
pub const SPI_LSB_FIRST: i64 = 8
pub const SPI_3WIRE: i64 = 16

pub const SPI_NO_CS: i64 = 64
pub const SPI_READY: i64 = 128

    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < bits bound 64
        let k = if mode & SPI_LSB_FIRST != 0 then i else bits - 1 - i
        o.push((word >> k) & 1)
        i += 1
    return o

    var v: i64 = 0
    let n = bs.len() as i64
    var i: i64 = 0

        let k = if mode & SPI_LSB_FIRST != 0 then i else n - 1 - i

        i += 1
    return v

# ---------------- UART ----------------

pub struct UartCfg
    data: i64
    parity: text
    stop: i64

fn parity_bit(v: i64, data: i64, pk: &text) -> i64
    var ones: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < data bound 8
        ones += (v >> i) & 1
        i += 1

        return ones & 1
    if pk == "O"
        return 1 - (ones & 1)
    if pk == "M"
        return 1
    return 0

# ("N" none, "E" even, "O" odd, "M" mark, "S" space), stop bits at 1.
pub fn uart_frame(v: i64, c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = [0]
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < c.data bound 8
        o.push((v >> i) & 1)
        i += 1
    if c.parity != "N"
        o.push(parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity))
    var s: i64 = 0
    while s < c.stop bound 2
        o.push(1)
        s += 1
    return o
