# -1 for a framing error (a stop bit at 0) and -2 for a parity error.
pub fn uart_decode(line: &List[i64], c: &UartCfg) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    let flen = 1 + c.data + (if c.parity == "N" then 0 else 1) + c.stop
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < line.len() bound 16777216
        if line[i] == 1
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + flen as usize > line.len()
            break
        var v: i64 = 0
        var k: i64 = 0
        while k < c.data bound 8
            v = v | (line[i + 1 + k as usize] << k)
            k += 1
        var res = v
        var p = i + 1 + c.data as usize
        if c.parity != "N"
            if line[p] != parity_bit(v, c.data, &c.parity)
                res = -2
            p += 1
        var s: i64 = 0
        while s < c.stop bound 2
            if line[p + s as usize] != 1
                res = -1
            s += 1
        out.push(res)
        i += flen as usize
    return out

# base); -1 when the rate is not an exact divisor.
pub fn uart_divisor(baud: i64) -> i64
    if baud <= 0 or 115200 % baud != 0
        return -1
    return 115200 / baud

# ---------------- register maps ----------------

pub struct Field
    name: text
    lsb: i64
    width: i64
    access: text

fn mask(f: &Field) -> i64 = ((1 << f.width) - 1) << f.lsb

pub fn field_get(reg: i64, f: &Field) -> i64 = (reg >> f.lsb) & ((1 << f.width) - 1)

# The register value after a software write of v to field f, given the
# current value: read-only fields keep their bits; for a write-1-to-clear
# field ("w1c") the written ones clear bits and the others stay.
pub fn field_set(reg: i64, f: &Field, v: i64) -> i64 ! BadDevice
    if v < 0 or v >= (1 << f.width)
        fail BadDevice(why: "value does not fit the field")
    if f.access == "ro"
        fail BadDevice(why: "read-only field")
    if f.access == "w1c"
        return reg & ~(v << f.lsb)
    return (reg & ~mask(f)) | (v << f.lsb)

# Fields must not overlap and must fit the register width.
pub fn fields_ok(fs: &List[Field], width: i64) -> bool
    var used: i64 = 0
    for f in fs
        if f.width < 1 or f.lsb < 0 or f.lsb + f.width > width
            return false
        if used & mask(&f) != 0
            return false
        used = used | mask(&f)
    return true

pub const DEVICE_CLASSES: text = "Cpu Simd Gpu Npu Tpu Lpu Photonic Quantum"

# Sandbox v0.1 5.1: the least tier (0 for S0 .. 7) a grant of this class
# needs: Cpu and Simd none beyond S0, any other class S2, direct
# assignment (passthrough) S5, a confidential-compute device S6. -1 for
# an unknown class.
pub fn grant_tier(class: &text, passthrough: bool, confidential: bool) -> i64
    if index_of(&DEVICE_CLASSES, class) < 0
        return -1
    var t: i64 = 0
    if class != "Cpu" and class != "Simd"
        t = 2
    if passthrough
        t = 5
    if confidential
        t = 6
    return t

module os.env

# Arguments and environment (survey M35), pure. A program never reads the
# process environment directly: the host admits one snapshot (argv and
# the variables the grant makes visible) as a logged event, and replay
# reads that event. This module holds what a program does with it:
# entry parsing and lookup with POSIX and Windows rules, pure updates for
# a child's environment, the grant filter and canonical form of a
# snapshot, shell-style expansion as Go's os.Expand defines it, and the
# Windows command line codec (CommandLineToArgvW rules as Rust's std
# parses them, and Rust's quoting for CreateProcessW).

error BadEnv(why: text)

pub struct Var
    key: text
    value: text

pub struct Snapshot
    argv: List[text]
    vars: List[Var]

fn sub(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi and i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

# One "KEY=VALUE" entry. POSIX splits at the first "="; Windows starts the
# search at the second character, so "=C:=C:\\x" has key "=C:" (the
# per-drive current directories). An entry without "=" is a key with an
# empty value.
pub fn parse_entry(e: &text, win: bool) -> Var
    let cs = e.chars()
    var i: usize = if win and cs.len() > 0 then 1 else 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if cs[i] == "="
            return Var(key: sub(&cs, 0, i), value: sub(&cs, i + 1, cs.len()))
        i += 1
    return Var(key: copy(e), value: "")

pub fn parse_environ(es: &[text], win: bool) -> List[Var]
    var o: List[Var] = []
    for e in es
        o.push(parse_entry(&e, win))
    return o

pub fn entry(v: &Var) -> text = v.key + "=" + v.value

fn upper_ascii(t: &text) -> text = t.upper()

fn same_key(a: &text, b: &text, win: bool) -> bool = if win then upper_ascii(a) == upper_ascii(b) else a == b

# The first matching entry wins (glibc getenv, Go's syscall.Getenv,
# GetEnvironmentVariableW on a block). Windows keys compare without case
# (ASCII here; the host supplies the full Windows upper-case table).
pub fn lookup(vs: &[Var], key: &text, win: bool) -> text?
    for v in vs
        if same_key(&v.key, key, win)
            return some(copy(v.value))
    return none

pub fn getenv(vs: &[Var], key: &text, win: bool) -> text = lookup(vs, key, win).or("")

pub fn valid_key(key: &text, win: bool) -> bool
    let cs = key.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0
        return false
    var i: usize = if win then 1 else 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "\u{0}"
            return false
        i += 1
    return cs[0] != "\u{0}"

# Set (replacing every entry of the key, keeping the first one's place)
# and unset; a pure update for building a child's environment.
pub fn setenv(vs: &[Var], key: &text, value: &text, win: bool) -> List[Var] ! BadEnv
    if not valid_key(key, win)
        fail BadEnv(why: "invalid key")
    for c in value.chars()
        if c == "\u{0}"
            fail BadEnv(why: "NUL in value")
    var o: List[Var] = []
    var done = false
    for v in vs
        if same_key(&v.key, key, win)
            if not done
                o.push(Var(key: copy(v.key), value: copy(value)))
                done = true
        else
            o.push(copy(v))
    if not done
        o.push(Var(key: copy(key), value: copy(value)))
    return o

pub fn unsetenv(vs: &[Var], key: &text, win: bool) -> List[Var]
    var o: List[Var] = []
    for v in vs
        if not same_key(&v.key, key, win)
            o.push(copy(v))
    return o

fn key_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# Canonical form of a snapshot for the log: only the granted keys
# (exact names; all keys when `all`), one entry per key (the first), sorted
# by key bytes. Two hosts with the same environment admit the same event.
pub fn snapshot(argv: &[text], es: &[text], granted: &[text], all: bool, win: bool) -> Snapshot
    var vs: List[Var] = []
    for v in parse_environ(es, win)
        var g = all
        for k in granted
            if same_key(&k, &v.key, win)
                g = true
        if not g
            continue
        var dup = false
        for w in vs
            if same_key(&w.key, &v.key, win)
                dup = true
        if not dup
            vs.push(v)
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < vs.len() bound 16777216
        var j = i
        while j > 0 and key_lt(&vs[j].key, &vs[j - 1].key) bound 16777216
            let t = copy(vs[j])
            vs[j] = copy(vs[j - 1])
            vs[j - 1] = t
            j -= 1
        i += 1
    var a: List[text] = []
    for x in argv
        a.push(copy(x))
    return Snapshot(argv: a, vars: vs)

# ---------------- expansion (Go os.Expand) ----------------

fn special(c: &text) -> bool = c == "*" or c == "#" or c == "$" or c == "@" or c == "!" or c == "?" or c == "-" or (c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] >= 48 and c[0] <= 57)

fn alnum(c: &text) -> bool
    if c.len_bytes() != 1
        return false
    let x = c[0]
    return x == 95 or (x >= 48 and x <= 57) or (x >= 97 and x <= 122) or (x >= 65 and x <= 90)

    name: text
    width: i64

fn shell_name(cs: &[text], at: usize) -> Name
    if cs[at] == "{"
        if cs.len() > at + 2 and special(&cs[at + 1]) and cs[at + 2] == "}"
            return Name(name: copy(cs[at + 1]), width: 3)
        var i = at + 1
        while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
            if cs[i] == "}"
                if i == at + 1
                    return Name(name: "", width: 2)
                return Name(name: sub(cs, at + 1, i), width: (i - at + 1) as i64)
            i += 1
        return Name(name: "", width: 1)
    if special(&cs[at])
        return Name(name: copy(cs[at]), width: 1)
    var i = at
    while i < cs.len() and alnum(&cs[i]) bound 16777216
        i += 1
    return Name(name: sub(cs, at, i), width: (i - at) as i64)

# $NAME, ${NAME} and the one-character specials; an unset name expands to
# "". "$" not followed by a name stays; "${" and "${}" are eaten.
# Note: Go's width for "${" counts bytes; names are ASCII so code points
# and bytes agree except inside "${...}" with non-ASCII, where both
# take the text up to "}".
pub fn expand(s: &text, vs: &[Var], win: bool) -> text
    let cs = s.chars()
    var o = ""
    var j: usize = 0
    while j < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if cs[j] == "$" and j + 1 < cs.len()
            let n = shell_name(&cs, j + 1)
            if n.name == "" and n.width > 0
                o = o
            elif n.name == ""
                o = o + "$"
            else
                o = o + getenv(vs, &n.name, win)
            j += n.width as usize + 1
        else
            o = o + cs[j]
            j += 1
    return o

# ---------------- Windows command lines ----------------

fn ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t"

# CommandLineToArgvW / MSVC (2008 and later) rules, as Rust's std parses
# GetCommandLineW: argv[0] has no escapes (quotes toggle); then
# backslashes escape only before a quote (2n -> n and toggle, 2n+1 -> n
# and a literal quote); "" inside quotes is a literal quote. An empty
# command line gives [exe].
pub fn win_parse(line: &text, exe: &text) -> List[text]
    let cs = line.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    var z: usize = 0
    while z < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if cs[z] == "\u{0}"
            n = z
            break
        z += 1
    var out: List[text] = []
    if n == 0
        out.push(copy(exe))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    var q = false
    var cur = ""
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        i += 1
        if c == "\""
            q = not q
        elif ws(&c) and not q
            break
        else
            cur = cur + c
    while i < n and ws(&cs[i]) bound 16777216
        i += 1
    out.push(cur)
    cur = ""
    q = false
    while i < n bound 16777216
        let c = copy(cs[i])
        i += 1
        if ws(&c) and not q
            out.push(cur)
            cur = ""
            while i < n and ws(&cs[i]) bound 16777216
                i += 1
        elif c == "\\"
            var k: usize = 1
            while i < n and cs[i] == "\\" bound 16777216
                k += 1
                i += 1
            if i < n and cs[i] == "\""
                var h: usize = 0
                while h < k / 2 bound 16777216
                    cur = cur + "\\"
                    h += 1
                if k % 2 == 1
                    i += 1
                    cur = cur + "\""
            else
                var h: usize = 0
                while h < k bound 16777216
                    cur = cur + "\\"
                    h += 1
        elif c == "\"" and q
            if i < n and cs[i] == "\""
                cur = cur + "\""
                i += 1
            elif i < n
                q = false
            else
                break
        elif c == "\""
            q = true
        else
            cur = cur + c
    if cur != "" or q
        out.push(cur)
    return out

# One argument quoted for CreateProcessW (Rust's append_arg): quoted when
# it is empty or holds a space or tab (or always); backslashes doubled
# before a quote and before the closing quote.
pub fn win_quote(arg: &text, force: bool) -> text ! BadEnv
    var quote = force or arg == ""
    for c in arg.chars()
        if c == "\u{0}"
            fail BadEnv(why: "NUL in argument")
        if ws(&c)
            quote = true
    var o = if quote then "\"" else ""
    var bs: usize = 0
    for c in arg.chars()
        if c == "\\"
            bs += 1
        else
            if c == "\""
                var h: usize = 0
                while h <= bs bound 16777216
                    o = o + "\\"
                    h += 1
            bs = 0
        o = o + c
    if quote
        var h: usize = 0
        while h < bs bound 16777216
            o = o + "\\"
            h += 1
        o = o + "\""
    return o

# The full command line: the program name always quoted (it cannot hold
# a quote: refused), then each argument.
pub fn win_command_line(prog: &text, args: &[text], force: bool) -> text ! BadEnv
    for c in prog.chars()
        if c == "\"" or c == "\u{0}"
            fail BadEnv(why: "quote or NUL in program name")
    var o = "\"" + prog + "\""
    for a in args
        let x = try win_quote(&a, force)
        o = o + " " + x
    return o

module os.fs

# Descriptor-relative filesystem (survey M38), pure. The program never sees
# an ambient root: every path is resolved beneath a preopened directory
# (WASI style), and the host performs the real operations as logged
# capability effects (cap Fs, grant fs per preopened subtree). This module
# holds two pure parts:
#  - the in-memory filesystem model used for tests and for replay: one
#    preopened root, directories, regular files, open descriptors with a
#    position and access mode. Results and errors follow Linux (openat2
#    with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, mkdirat, unlinkat,
#    renameat, ftruncate, read, write, lseek), named with the
#    wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 error-code cases. A path that would leave the
#    preopen (an absolute path, or ".." at the root) fails with
#    not-permitted (Linux reports EXDEV). Symlinks, hard links, sparse
#    holes and timestamps are not modelled.
#  - the error-code table of wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 and the Linux errno
#    names that map onto it.

error FsErr(code: text)

# wasi:filesystem@0.2.8 types.wit, enum error-code, in declaration order.
pub const ERROR_CODES: text = "access would-block already bad-descriptor busy deadlock quota exist file-too-large illegal-byte-sequence in-progress interrupted invalid io is-directory loop too-many-links message-size name-too-long no-device no-entry no-lock insufficient-memory insufficient-space not-directory not-empty not-recoverable unsupported no-tty no-such-device overflow not-permitted pipe read-only invalid-seek text-file-busy cross-device"

# The POSIX errno each error-code stands for (wasi-libc's mapping, same order).
pub const ERRNOS: text = "EACCES EAGAIN EALREADY EBADF EBUSY EDEADLK EDQUOT EEXIST EFBIG EILSEQ EINPROGRESS EINTR EINVAL EIO EISDIR ELOOP EMLINK EMSGSIZE ENAMETOOLONG ENODEV ENOENT ENOLCK ENOMEM ENOSPC ENOTDIR ENOTEMPTY ENOTRECOVERABLE ENOTSUP ENOTTY ENXIO EOVERFLOW EPERM EPIPE EROFS ESPIPE ETXTBSY EXDEV"

pub fn code_index(c: text) -> i64
    var i: i64 = 0
    for x in ERROR_CODES.split(" ")
        if x == c
            return i
        i += 1
    return -1

pub fn errno_of(c: text) -> text
    let i = code_index(c)
    if i < 0
        return ""
    return copy(ERRNOS.split(" ")[i as usize])

pub fn code_of_errno(e: text) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    let es = ERRNOS.split(" ")
    while i < es.len() bound 64
        if es[i] == e
            return copy(ERROR_CODES.split(" ")[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# ---------------- the model ----------------

pub struct Node
    dir: bool
    data: List[text]
    parent: i64

pub struct Ent
    dir: i64
    name: text
    nd: i64

pub struct Desc
    nd: i64
    pos: i64
    rd: bool
    wr: bool
    app: bool
    live: bool

pub struct Fs
    nodes: List[Node]
    ents: List[Ent]
    descs: List[Desc]

# A fresh filesystem: node 0 is the preopened root directory.
pub fn fs_new() -> Fs = Fs(nodes: [Node(dir: true, data: [], parent: -1)], ents: [], descs: [])

fn bad(c: text) -> FsErr = FsErr(code: c)

fn lookup(fs: &Fs, d: i64, name: &text) -> i64
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d and e.name == name
            return e.nd
    return -1

fn is_empty(fs: &Fs, d: i64) -> bool
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == d
            return false
    return true

# Where a path leads: the directory holding the last component, the last
# component ("." or ".." or a name), the node it names (-1 when absent)
# and whether the path ends in "/".
pub struct Where
    dir: i64
    last: text
    nd: i64
    slash: bool

fn comps(path: &text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    for c in path.split("/")
        if c != ""
            o.push(c)
    return o

fn walk1(fs: &Fs, cur: i64, c: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if c == "."
        return cur
    if c == ".."
        let p = fs.nodes[cur as usize].parent
        if p < 0
            fail bad("not-permitted")
        return p
    let n = lookup(fs, cur, c)
    if n < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    return n

# follow: whether a final "." or ".." is stepped (open, stat, list); the
# calls that create or remove an entry (mkdirat, unlinkat, renameat) look
# only at the parent and refuse a final dot entry themselves.
pub fn resolve(fs: &Fs, path: &text, follow: bool) -> Where ! FsErr
    if path == ""
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if path.startswith("/")
        fail bad("not-permitted")
    let cs = comps(path)
    var cur: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i + 1 < cs.len() bound 4096
        cur = try walk1(fs, cur, &cs[i])
        i += 1
    if not fs.nodes[cur as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    let last = copy(cs[cs.len() - 1])
    var nd: i64 = -1
    if last == "." or last == ".."
        if follow
            nd = try walk1(fs, cur, &last)
    else
        nd = lookup(fs, cur, &last)
    return Where(dir: cur, last: last, nd: nd, slash: path.endswith("/"))

fn named(w: &Where) -> bool = w.last != "." and w.last != ".."

fn add_node(fs: &mut Fs, dir: bool, parent: i64) -> i64
    fs.nodes.push(Node(dir: dir, data: [], parent: parent))
    return fs.nodes.len() as i64 - 1

fn drop_ent(fs: &mut Fs, d: i64, name: &text)
    var o: List[Ent] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if not (e.dir == d and e.name == name)
            o.push(copy(e))
    fs.ents = o

pub fn mkdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w) or w.nd >= 0
        fail bad("exist")
    let n = add_node(fs, true, w.dir)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    return true

# Open flags as text: r (read), w (write), c (create), x (exclusive),
# t (truncate), d (directory), a (append). Returns the descriptor index.
pub fn open_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text, flags: &text) -> i64 ! FsErr
    let rd = flags.contains("r")
    let wr = flags.contains("w")
    let cr = flags.contains("c")
    let ex = flags.contains("x")
    let tr = flags.contains("t")
    let dr = flags.contains("d")
    if cr and dr
        fail bad("invalid")
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if cr and w.slash and named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    var n = w.nd
    if n < 0
        if not cr
            fail bad("no-entry")
        n = add_node(fs, false, w.dir)
        fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: w.dir, name: copy(w.last), nd: n))
    elif cr and ex
        fail bad("exist")
    elif fs.nodes[n as usize].dir
        if wr or cr or tr
            fail bad("is-directory")
    else
        if dr or w.slash
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if tr
            fs.nodes[n as usize].data = []
    fs.descs.push(Desc(nd: n, pos: 0, rd: rd, wr: wr, app: flags.contains("a"), live: true))
    return fs.descs.len() as i64 - 1

fn desc(fs: &Fs, h: i64) -> Desc ! FsErr
    if h < 0 or h as usize >= fs.descs.len() or not fs.descs[h as usize].live
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    return copy(fs.descs[h as usize])

pub fn read(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, n: i64) -> text ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.rd
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    if fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    let data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o = ""
    var p = d.pos
    while p < data.len() as i64 and p < d.pos + n bound 16777216
        o = o + data[p as usize]
        p += 1
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return o

pub fn write(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, s: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr
        fail bad("bad-descriptor")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var p = if d.app then data.len() as i64 else d.pos
    while data.len() as i64 < p bound 16777216
        data.push("\u{0}")
    for c in s.chars()
        if p < data.len() as i64
            data[p as usize] = c
        else
            data.push(c)
        p += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = data
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = p
    return true

pub fn seek(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, pos: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    if pos < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    fs.descs[h as usize].pos = pos
    return true

pub fn truncate(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64, len: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let d = try desc(fs, h)
    if not d.wr or len < 0
        fail bad("invalid")
    var data = copy(fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data)
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < len bound 16777216
        o.push(if i < data.len() as i64 then copy(data[i as usize]) else "\u{0}")
        i += 1
    fs.nodes[d.nd as usize].data = o
    return true

pub fn close(fs: &mut Fs, h: i64) -> bool ! FsErr
    let _d = try desc(fs, h)
    fs.descs[h as usize].live = false
    return true

pub fn unlink_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if not named(&w)
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("is-directory")
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

pub fn rmdir_at(fs: &mut Fs, path: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, false)
    if w.last == "."
        fail bad("invalid")
    if w.last == ".."
        fail bad("not-empty")
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    if not is_empty(fs, w.nd)
        fail bad("not-empty")
    drop_ent(fs, w.dir, &w.last)
    return true

# a is d or a directory above d.
fn above(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> bool
    var x = d
    while x >= 0 bound 4096
        if x == a
            return true
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return false

# The child of a on the way down to d (a strictly above d).
fn child_towards(fs: &Fs, a: i64, d: i64) -> i64
    var x = d
    while fs.nodes[x as usize].parent != a bound 4096
        x = fs.nodes[x as usize].parent
    return x

pub fn rename_at(fs: &mut Fs, src: &text, dst: &text) -> bool ! FsErr
    let o = try resolve(fs, src, false)
    let n = try resolve(fs, dst, false)
    if not named(&o) or not named(&n)
        fail bad("busy")
    if o.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    let isdir = fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].dir
    if not isdir and (o.slash or n.slash)
        fail bad("not-directory")
    # lock_rename's trap: the entry under the common ancestor
    if o.dir != n.dir
        if above(fs, o.dir, n.dir) and child_towards(fs, o.dir, n.dir) == o.nd
            fail bad("invalid")
        if above(fs, n.dir, o.dir) and child_towards(fs, n.dir, o.dir) == n.nd
            fail bad("not-empty")
    if o.nd == n.nd
        return true
    if n.nd >= 0
        let tdir = fs.nodes[n.nd as usize].dir
        if isdir and not tdir
            fail bad("not-directory")
        if not isdir and tdir
            fail bad("is-directory")
        if tdir and not is_empty(fs, n.nd)
            fail bad("not-empty")
        drop_ent(fs, n.dir, &n.last)
    drop_ent(fs, o.dir, &o.last)
    fs.ents.push(Ent(dir: n.dir, name: copy(n.last), nd: o.nd))
    if isdir
        fs.nodes[o.nd as usize].parent = n.dir
    return true

# stat: "d" for a directory, else "f" and the size.
pub fn stat_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> text ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        return "d"
    if w.slash
        fail bad("not-directory")
    return "f" + fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].data.len().tostr()

# UTF-8 byte order (Linux sorts names as bytes).
fn text_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 4096
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# The entry names of a directory, sorted (without "." and "..").
pub fn list_at(fs: &Fs, path: &text) -> List[text] ! FsErr
    let w = try resolve(fs, path, true)
    if w.nd < 0
        fail bad("no-entry")
    if not fs.nodes[w.nd as usize].dir
        fail bad("not-directory")
    var o: List[text] = []
    for e in fs.ents
        if e.dir == w.nd
            var k = o.len()
            o.push(copy(e.name))
            while k > 0 and text_lt(&o[k], &o[k - 1]) bound 4096
                let t = copy(o[k])
                o[k] = copy(o[k - 1])
                o[k - 1] = t
                k -= 1
    return o

# ---------------- scripts ----------------

fn num(s: &text) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in s.chars()
        v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
    return v

fn op1(fs: &mut Fs, a: &List[text]) -> text ! FsErr
    let k = copy(a[0])
    if k == "mkdir"
        let _ = try mkdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "open"
        let h = try open_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "h" + h.tostr()
    if k == "read"
        let s = try read(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "=" + s
    if k == "write"
        let _ = try write(fs, num(&a[1]), &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "seek"
        let _ = try seek(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "trunc"
        let _ = try truncate(fs, num(&a[1]), num(&a[2]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "close"
        let _ = try close(fs, num(&a[1]))
        return "ok"
    if k == "unlink"
        let _ = try unlink_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rmdir"
        let _ = try rmdir_at(fs, &a[1])
        return "ok"
    if k == "rename"
        let _ = try rename_at(fs, &a[1], &a[2])
        return "ok"
    if k == "stat"
        return try stat_at(fs, &a[1])
    if k == "list"
        let l = try list_at(fs, &a[1])
        return ":" + ",".join(l)
    fail bad("invalid")

# Run a script of ";"-separated operations on a fresh filesystem; the
# outcome of each (ok, hN, =data, d, fN, :names or an error-code), joined by ";".
pub fn script(s: text) -> text
    var fs = fs_new()
    var out: List[text] = []
    for line in s.split(";")
        let a = line.split(" ")
        out.push(op1(&mut fs, &a) catch |e| e.code)
    return ";".join(out)

module os.ipc

# Pipes and IPC (survey M41), pure. Channels are opened by name through
# the host (cap Channel, grant ipc per endpoint name); shared memory is
# not offered (it cannot be logged). This module holds:
#  - framing over byte streams: netstrings (D. J. Bernstein) and u32
#    big-endian length prefixes, with streaming decoders that accept
#    chunks split anywhere (as M18 io delivers them);
#  - the Linux pipe buffer: 16 page slots of 4096 bytes, writes of at most
#    PIPE_BUF (4096) bytes are atomic, a short final fragment merges into
#    the last page when it fits, non-blocking writes return a short count
#    or EAGAIN and reads EAGAIN when empty (fs/pipe.c pipe_write and
#    pipe_read);
#  - Unix domain socket addresses (unix(7)): pathname, abstract and
#    unnamed, the 108-byte sun_path limit and the address length the
#    kernel reports;
#  - Windows named pipe names (\\.\pipe\name, \\server\pipe\name);
#  - the grant ipc check by endpoint name.

error BadFrame(why: text)

# ---------------- netstrings ----------------

pub fn netstring(payload: &List[u8]) -> List[u8]
    let h = payload.len().tostr() + ":"
    var o: List[u8] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < h.len_bytes() bound 32
        o.push(h[i])
        i += 1
    for b in payload
        o.push(b)
    o.push(44)
    return o

pub struct NsDec
    buf: List[u8]
    out: List[List[u8]]
    bad: text

pub fn ns_new() -> NsDec = NsDec(buf: [], out: [], bad: "")

fn slice(b: &List[u8], i: usize, j: usize) -> List[u8]
    var o: List[u8] = []
    var k = i
    while k < j bound 16777216
        o.push(b[k])
        k += 1
    return o

# Feed bytes; complete frames are appended to out. A malformed stream
# (a length with a leading zero or no digits, a missing ":" or ",", or a
# length over 999999999) stops the decoder with bad set.
pub fn ns_feed(d: &mut NsDec, chunk: &List[u8])
    if d.bad != ""
        return
    for b in chunk
        d.buf.push(b)
    loop bound 16777216
        var i: usize = 0
        var n: i64 = 0
        while i < d.buf.len() and d.buf[i] >= 48 and d.buf[i] <= 57 bound 16
            if i == 1 and d.buf[0] == 48
                d.bad = "leading zero"
                return
            n = n * 10 + (d.buf[i] as i64 - 48)
            i += 1
            if i > 9
                d.bad = "length too long"
                return
        if i == d.buf.len()
            return
        if i == 0 or d.buf[i] != 58
            d.bad = "expected digits and ':'"
            return
        let end = i + 1 + n as usize
        if d.buf.len() <= end
            return
        if d.buf[end] != 44
            d.bad = "expected ','"
            return
        d.out.push(slice(&d.buf, i + 1, end))
        var rest: List[u8] = []
        var k = end + 1
        while k < d.buf.len() bound 16777216
            rest.push(d.buf[k])
            k += 1
        d.buf = rest

# ---------------- u32 length prefix ----------------

pub fn be32_frame(payload: &List[u8]) -> List[u8]
    let n = payload.len() as i64
    var o: List[u8] = [((n >> 24) & 255) as u8, ((n >> 16) & 255) as u8, ((n >> 8) & 255) as u8, (n & 255) as u8]
    for b in payload
        o.push(b)
    return o

pub struct LpDec
    buf: List[u8]
    frames: List[List[u8]]
    max: i64
    bad: text

pub fn lp_new(max: i64) -> LpDec = LpDec(buf: [], frames: [], max: max, bad: "")

pub fn lp_feed(d: &mut LpDec, chunk: &List[u8])
    if d.bad != ""
        return
    for b in chunk
        d.buf.push(b)
    while d.buf.len() >= 4 bound 16777216
        let n = (d.buf[0] as i64) << 24 | (d.buf[1] as i64) << 16 | (d.buf[2] as i64) << 8 | d.buf[3] as i64
        if n > d.max
            d.bad = "frame too large"
            return
        if (d.buf.len() as i64) < 4 + n
            return
        var f: List[u8] = []
        var rest: List[u8] = []
        var k: usize = 4
        while k < d.buf.len() bound 16777216
            if (k as i64) < 4 + n
                f.push(d.buf[k])
            else
                rest.push(d.buf[k])
            k += 1
        d.frames.push(f)
        d.buf = rest

# ---------------- Linux pipe buffer ----------------

pub const PAGE: i64 = 4096
pub const PIPE_BUF: i64 = 4096
pub const PIPE_SLOTS: i64 = 16

pub struct PBuf
    offset: i64
    len: i64

pub struct Pipe
    bufs: List[PBuf]
    slots: i64

pub fn pipe_new() -> Pipe = Pipe(bufs: [], slots: PIPE_SLOTS)

pub fn pipe_bytes(p: &Pipe) -> i64
    var n: i64 = 0
    for b in p.bufs
        n += b.len
    return n

# A non-blocking write of n bytes: the count written, or -1 for EAGAIN.
pub fn pipe_write(p: &mut Pipe, n: i64) -> i64
    if n == 0
        return 0
    var ret: i64 = 0
    let chars = n % PAGE
    if chars > 0 and p.bufs.len() > 0
        let k = p.bufs.len() - 1
        if p.bufs[k].offset + p.bufs[k].len + chars <= PAGE
            p.bufs[k].len += chars
            ret = chars
            if ret == n
                return ret
    while (p.bufs.len() as i64) < p.slots bound 1024
        let c = if n - ret < PAGE then n - ret else PAGE
        p.bufs.push(PBuf(offset: 0, len: c))
        ret += c
        if ret == n
            return ret
    return if ret == 0 then -1 else ret

# A non-blocking read of up to n bytes: the count read, or -1 for EAGAIN.
pub fn pipe_read(p: &mut Pipe, n: i64) -> i64
    if p.bufs.len() == 0
        return if n == 0 then 0 else -1
    var got: i64 = 0
    while got < n and p.bufs.len() > 0 bound 1024
        let take = if p.bufs[0].len < n - got then p.bufs[0].len else n - got
        p.bufs[0].offset += take
        p.bufs[0].len -= take
        got += take
        if p.bufs[0].len == 0
            var rest: List[PBuf] = []
            var k: usize = 1
            while k < p.bufs.len() bound 1024
                rest.push(copy(p.bufs[k]))
                k += 1
            p.bufs = rest
    return got

# F_SETPIPE_SZ: the capacity rounds up to a power of two pages; it cannot
# drop below the bytes held. Returns the new capacity or -1 (EBUSY).
pub fn pipe_set_size(p: &mut Pipe, bytes: i64) -> i64
    var pages: i64 = 1
    while pages * PAGE < bytes bound 64
        pages = pages * 2
    if (p.bufs.len() as i64) > pages
        return -1
    p.slots = pages
    return pages * PAGE

# ---------------- Unix domain socket addresses ----------------

pub const SUN_PATH: i64 = 108

# The address length getsockname reports after bind(2) with a name of
# name_len bytes: a pathname counts its terminating NUL, an abstract name
# (first byte NUL, counted in name_len) does not; an empty name autobinds
# to an abstract name of a NUL and five hex digits. -1 when the name does
# not fit sun_path (EINVAL). An unbound socket reports UNNAMED_LEN.
pub const UNNAMED_LEN: i64 = 2

pub fn unix_addrlen(name_len: i64, abstract: bool) -> i64
    if name_len == 0
        return 8
    if name_len > SUN_PATH
        return -1
    if abstract
        return 2 + name_len
    return 2 + name_len + 1

# ---------------- Windows named pipes ----------------

# \\.\pipe\name or \\server\pipe\name; the name part is 1 to 256
# characters, any character but the backslash. Returns the name or "".
pub fn win_pipe_name(path: &text) -> text
    let cs = path.chars()
    if cs.len() < 3 or cs[0] != "\\" or cs[1] != "\\"
        return ""
    var i: usize = 2
    while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != "\\" bound 4096
        i += 1
    if i == 2 or i >= cs.len()
        return ""
    let _rest = cs.len() - i - 1
    var head = ""
    var j = i + 1
    while j < cs.len() and j < i + 6 bound 8
        head = head + cs[j]
        j += 1
    if head.lower() != "pipe\\"
        return ""
    var name = ""
    var k = i + 6
    while k < cs.len() bound 4096
        name = name + cs[k]
        k += 1
    let nl = name.chars().len()
    if nl == 0 or nl > 256 or name.contains("\\")
        return ""
    return name

# ---------------- the ipc grant ----------------

# grant ipc: an endpoint is reachable only when the sandbox grant names
# it exactly (deny by default); a grant ending in "/*" covers the names
# directly below that prefix.
pub fn ipc_granted(grants: &List[text], endpoint: &text) -> bool
    for g in grants
        if g == endpoint
            return true
        if g.endswith("/*")
            let gc = g.chars()
            var pre = ""
            var i: usize = 0
            while i + 1 < gc.len() bound 4096
                pre = pre + gc[i]
                i += 1
            if endpoint.startswith(&pre) and endpoint.len_bytes() > pre.len_bytes()
                let ec = endpoint.chars()
                var ok = true
                var k = pre.chars().len()
                while k < ec.len() bound 4096
                    if ec[k] == "/"
                        ok = false
                    k += 1
                if ok
                    return true
    return false

module os.path

# Path algebra (survey M34), pure and lexical: POSIX paths, Windows paths
# and WASI preopen-relative paths. The POSIX and Windows functions follow
# CPython 3.13 posixpath and ntpath exactly (the reference behind Python's
# os.path and pathlib), including POSIX's implementation-defined "//"
# root and Windows drives, UNC shares and \\?\ device paths. Nothing here
# touches a file system: symbolic links, the current directory and case
# folding of the file system are the host's (relpath takes the current
# directory as an argument; Windows case folding is ASCII here, see
# win_normcase). WASI resolution (wasi_resolve) is the lexical part of the
# preview 1 and 2 rule that a path is relative to a granted directory
# descriptor and never leaves it.

error BadPath(why: text)

pub struct Root
    drive: text
    root: text
    tail: text

pub struct Pair
    head: text
    tail: text

fn sub(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i = lo
    while i < hi and i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn cat(cs: &[text]) -> text = sub(cs, 0, cs.len())

fn rstrip_seps(t: &text, win: bool) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var n = cs.len()
    while n > 0 and (cs[n - 1] == "/" or (win and cs[n - 1] == "\\")) bound 16777216
        n -= 1
    return sub(&cs, 0, n)

fn is_sep(c: &text, win: bool) -> bool = c == "/" or (win and c == "\\")

fn split_on(t: &text, sep: text) -> List[text]
    var o: List[text] = []
    var cur = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        if c == sep
            o.push(cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur + c
    o.push(cur)
    return o

fn join_with(ps: &[text], sep: text) -> text
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < ps.len() bound 16777216
        if i > 0
            o = o + sep
        o = o + ps[i]
        i += 1
    return o

fn slashes_to_back(t: &text) -> text
    var o = ""
    for c in t.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "/" then "\\" else c)
    return o

# Splitting the extension (genericpath._splitext): the last dot after the
# last separator, unless every character before it in the name is a dot.
fn splitext_any(p: &text, win: bool) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var s: i64 = -1
    var d: i64 = -1
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        if is_sep(&cs[i], win)
            s = i as i64
        if cs[i] == "."
            d = i as i64
        i += 1
    if d > s
        var k = (s + 1) as usize
        while (k as i64) < d bound 16777216
            if cs[k] != "."
                return Pair(head: sub(&cs, 0, d as usize), tail: sub(&cs, d as usize, cs.len()))
            k += 1
    return Pair(head: copy(p), tail: "")

# ---------------- POSIX ----------------

pub fn posix_splitroot(p: &text) -> Root
    let cs = p.chars()
    if cs.len() == 0 or cs[0] != "/"
        return Root(drive: "", root: "", tail: copy(p))
    if cs.len() < 2 or cs[1] != "/" or (cs.len() > 2 and cs[2] == "/")
        return Root(drive: "", root: "/", tail: sub(&cs, 1, cs.len()))
    return Root(drive: "", root: "//", tail: sub(&cs, 2, cs.len()))

pub fn posix_isabs(p: &text) -> bool = p.startswith("/")

pub fn posix_join(parts: &[text]) -> text
    var path = ""
    var first = true
    for b in parts
        if first
            path = copy(b)
            first = false
        elif b.startswith("/") or path == ""
            path = copy(b)
        elif path.endswith("/")
            path = path + b
        else
            path = path + "/" + b
    return path

pub fn posix_split(p: &text) -> Pair
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    var head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    let tail = sub(&cs, i, cs.len())
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    if head != "" and not all
        head = rstrip_seps(&head, false)
    return Pair(head: head, tail: tail)

pub fn posix_basename(p: &text) -> text = posix_split(p).tail

pub fn posix_dirname(p: &text) -> text
    let cs = p.chars()
    var i = cs.len()
    while i > 0 and cs[i - 1] != "/" bound 16777216
        i -= 1
    let head = sub(&cs, 0, i)
    var all = true
    for c in head.chars()
        if c != "/"
            all = false
    return if head != "" and not all then rstrip_seps(&head, false) else head

pub fn posix_normpath(p: &text) -> text
    if p == ""
        return "."
    let r = posix_splitroot(p)
    let init = copy(r.root)

            let v49 = (if v37.v29 != 0 then ~v37.v29 else 0) | v47
            v46 = (v46 & v49) | v30
        elif v37.v27 == "+"
            v46 = v46 | v30
        else
            v46 = v46 & ~v30
    return v46

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn f8(v12: i64, v38: &text, v44: i64) -> t0 ! x0
    let v45 = try f6(v38)
    let v43 = v12 & v1 == v6
    return t0(v25: (v12 & v1) | f7(v12, v43, v44, &v45), v26: (v12 & v1) | f7(v12, v43, 0, &v45))

pub struct t2
    v50: i64
    v51: i64
    v52: List[i64]

pub const v53: i64 = 4
pub const v54: i64 = 2
pub const v55: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn f9(v37: &t2, v25: i64, v56: i64, v57: i64, v58: i64) -> bool
    var v59 = v25 & 7
    if v37.v50 == v56
        v59 = (v25 >> 6) & 7
    else
        var v60 = v37.v51 == v57
        for v61 in v37.v52
            if v61 == v57
                v60 = true
        if v60
            v59 = (v25 >> 3) & 7
    return v59 & v58 == v58

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------
pub struct t3
    v62: i64
    v63: List[i64]

fn f10(v35: &[text], v16: usize, v64: usize) -> i64
    if v64 <= v16 or v64 - v16 > 15
        return -1
    var v23: i64 = 0
    var v36 = v16
    while v36 < v64 bound 16
        let v20 = v35[v36][0] as i64
        if v35[v36].len_bytes() != 1 or v20 < 48 or v20 > 57
            return -1
        v23 = v23 * 10 + (v20 - 48)
        v36 += 1
    return v23

fn f11(v35: &[text], v16: usize, v64: usize) -> i64
    if v64 <= v16 or v64 - v16 > 12
        return -1
    var v23: i64 = 0
    var v36 = v16
    while v36 < v64 bound 16
        let v20 = v35[v36][0] as i64
        var v41: i64 = -1
        if v20 >= 48 and v20 <= 57
            v41 = v20 - 48
        elif v20 >= 65 and v20 <= 70
            v41 = v20 - 55
        elif v20 >= 97 and v20 <= 102
            v41 = v20 - 87
        if v35[v36].len_bytes() != 1 or v41 < 0
            return -1
        v23 = v23 * 16 + v41
        v36 += 1
    return v23

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn f12(v13: &text) -> t3 ! x0
    let v35 = v13.chars()

    var v36: usize = 4
    var v66 = true
    var v67: i64 = 0
    while v36 <= v35.len() bound 64
        var v68 = v36
        while v68 < v35.len() and v35[v68] != "-" bound 64
            v68 += 1
        var v23: i64 = -1
        if v66 and v68 - v36 > 2 and v35[v36] == "0" and (v35[v36 + 1] == "x" or v35[v36 + 1] == "X")

        else
            v23 = f10(&v35, v36, v68)
        if v23 < 0 or (v66 and v23 >= 281474976710656) or (not v66 and v23 >= 4294967296)
            fail x0(v0: "bad SID")

            v66 = false

        v36 = v68 + 1
    if v65.len() > 15
        fail x0(v0: "too many sub-authorities")
    return t3(v62: v67, v63: v65)

fn f13(v23: i64) -> text
    let v69 = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var v22 = ""
    var v20 = v23
    var v24: i64 = 0
    while v24 < 12 bound 12
        v22 = copy(v69[(v20 & 15) as usize]) + v22
        v20 = v20 >> 4
        v24 += 1
    return v22

pub fn f14(v70: &t3) -> text
    var v22 = "S-1-" + (if v70.v62 < 4294967296 then v70.v62.tostr() else "0x" + f13(v70.v62))
    for v20 in v70.v63
        v22 = v22 + "-" + v20.tostr()
    return v22

# Binary form (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.2): revision, count, 6-byte big-endian
# authority, little-endian 32-bit sub-authorities.
pub fn f15(v70: &t3) -> List[i64]
    var v22: List[i64] = [1, v70.v63.len() as i64]
    var v24: i64 = 5
    while v24 >= 0 bound 6
        v22.push((v70.v62 >> (v24 * 8)) & 255)
        v24 -= 1
    for v20 in v70.v63
        v22.push(v20 & 255)
        v22.push((v20 >> 8) & 255)
        v22.push((v20 >> 16) & 255)
        v22.push((v20 >> 24) & 255)
    return v22

pub fn f16(v71: &[i64]) -> t3 ! x0
    if v71.len() < 8 or v71[0] != 1 or v71[1] > 15 or v71.len() != 8 + 4 * v71[1] as usize
        fail x0(v0: "bad SID bytes")
    var v72: i64 = 0
    for v24 in 2..8
        v72 = v72 * 256 + v71[v24]
    var v63: List[i64] = []
    var v36: usize = 8
    while v36 < v71.len() bound 64
        v63.push(v71[v36] | v71[v36 + 1] << 8 | v71[v36 + 2] << 16 | v71[v36 + 3] << 24)
        v36 += 4
    return t3(v62: v72, v63: v63)

pub struct t4
    v73: bool
    v74: text
    v75: i64

# Discretionary access check (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2, simplified: no owner
# rights, generic mapping, inheritance or object ACEs): with no DACL
# everything is granted; otherwise ACEs are read in order, a deny ACE
# for a token SID that names a still-wanted bit refuses, an allow ACE
# grants its bits, and access is granted once every wanted bit is.
pub fn f17(v76: bool, v77: &[t4], v78: &[text], v58: i64) -> bool
    if not v76
        return true
    var v79 = v58
    for v72 in v77
        var v80 = false
        for v70 in v78
            if v70 == v72.v74
                v80 = true
        if not v80
            continue
        if not v72.v73 and v72.v75 & v79 != 0
            return false
        if v72.v73
            v79 = v79 & ~v72.v75
        if v79 == 0
            return true
    return v79 == 0

# ---------------- Landlock ----------------
pub const v81: i64 = 1
pub const v82: i64 = 2
pub const v83: i64 = 4
pub const v84: i64 = 8
pub const v85: i64 = 16
pub const v86: i64 = 32
pub const v87: i64 = 64
pub const v88: i64 = 128
pub const v89: i64 = 256
pub const v90: i64 = 512
pub const v91: i64 = 1024
pub const v92: i64 = 2048
pub const v93: i64 = 4096
pub const v94: i64 = 8192
pub const v95: i64 = 16384
pub const v96: i64 = 32768
pub const v97: i64 = 1
pub const v98: i64 = 2
pub const v99: i64 = 1
pub const v100: i64 = 2

# Filesystem rights known to a Landlock ABI version (1: EXECUTE to
# MAKE_SYM, 2: REFER, 3: TRUNCATE, 5: IOCTL_DEV; 4 added network rights
# only); a sandbox handles only what the running kernel knows.
pub fn f18(v101: i64) -> i64
    if v101 < 1
        return 0
    var v18: i64 = 8191
    if v101 >= 2
        v18 = v18 | v94
    if v101 >= 3
        v18 = v18 | v95
    if v101 >= 5
        v18 = v18 | v96
    return v18

pub fn f19(v101: i64) -> i64 = if v101 >= 4 then 3 else 0
pub fn f20(v101: i64) -> i64 = if v101 >= 6 then 3 else 0

pub struct t5
    v102: List[text]
    v103: i64

pub struct t6
    v104: i64
    v105: List[t5]

fn f21(v106: &[text], v107: &[text]) -> bool
    if v106.len() > v107.len()
        return false
    var v36: usize = 0
    while v36 < v106.len() bound 16777216
        if v106[v36] != v107[v36]
            return false
        v36 += 1
    return true

# A filesystem access `want` on path p (components from the root): each
# layer must allow it; a layer allows the rights it does not handle, and
# a handled right only if a rule on p or an ancestor grants it.
pub fn f22(v108: &[t6], v107: &[text], v58: i64) -> bool
    for v109 in v108
        let v110 = v58 & v109.v104
        var v111: i64 = 0
        for v18 in v109.v105
            if f21(&v18.v102, v107)
                v111 = v111 | v18.v103
        if v110 & ~v111 != 0
            return false
    return true

# ---------------- Sandbox grant mapping (proposal) ----------------

# fs grant modes as letters "r", "w", "x" (any subset). Proposed rights:
# r: read files and list directories; w: write, truncate, create and
# remove files, directories and symlinks, and rename within (REFER); x:
# execute. Device nodes, sockets, FIFOs and device ioctl are never
# granted by fs; they belong to the device and ipc grants.
pub fn f23(v112: &text) -> i64
    var v18: i64 = 0
    for v37 in v112.chars()
        if v37 == "r"
            v18 = v18 | v83 | v84
        elif v37 == "w"
            v18 = v18 | v82 | v95 | v89 | v88 | v93 | v86 | v85 | v94
        elif v37 == "x"
            v18 = v18 | v81
    return v18

# The POSIX bits an fs grant needs on the files it covers, for reporting
# (owner class: the sandboxed program runs as the file's owner or not at
# all).
pub fn f24(v112: &text) -> i64
    var v12: i64 = 0
    for v37 in v112.chars()
        if v37 == "r"
            v12 = v12 | 256
        elif v37 == "w"
            v12 = v12 | 128
        elif v37 == "x"
            v12 = v12 | 64
    return v12

# The fs grant modes a Landlock right set fully contains.
pub fn f25(v103: i64) -> text
    var v22 = ""
    let v18 = "r"
    let v19 = "w"
    let v113 = f23(&v18)
    let v114 = f23(&v19)
    if v103 & v113 == v113
        v22 = v22 + "r"
    if v103 & v114 == v114
        v22 = v22 + "w"
    if v103 & v81 != 0
        v22 = v22 + "x"
    return v22

module os.perm

# Permission models (survey M36), pure, for reading and reporting: a
# program's authority is exactly its grants (Sandbox v0.1) and it never
# raises privilege, so nothing here changes a permission on a system.
#  - POSIX mode bits: file type and permission bits, the ls -l string
#    (CPython stat.filemode), octal, symbolic modes as POSIX chmod defines
#    them (with GNU coreutils' umask and X rules), and the access check
#    of POSIX.1 section 4.5 for an unprivileged process.
#  - Windows: SIDs (MS-DTYP 2.4.2: string and binary forms) and the
#    discretionary access check over an ordered ACE list (MS-DTYP 2.5.3.2,
#    allow and deny ACEs, no inheritance or object ACEs).
#  - Linux Landlock: the access-right bits of include/uapi/linux/landlock.h,
#    the rights each ABI version knows, and a ruleset check (path-beneath
#    rules, every layer must allow).
#  - The proposed mapping of a Sandbox fs grant (r, w, x on a subtree) to
#    POSIX bits and Landlock rights (spec item: grant names table).

error BadPerm(why: text)

# ---------------- POSIX mode bits ----------------

pub const S_IFMT: i64 = 61440
pub const S_IFSOCK: i64 = 49152
pub const S_IFLNK: i64 = 40960
pub const S_IFREG: i64 = 32768
pub const S_IFBLK: i64 = 24576
pub const S_IFDIR: i64 = 16384
pub const S_IFCHR: i64 = 8192
pub const S_IFIFO: i64 = 4096
pub const S_ISUID: i64 = 2048
pub const S_ISGID: i64 = 1024
pub const S_ISVTX: i64 = 512

fn type_char(m: i64) -> text
    let t = m & S_IFMT
    if t == S_IFREG
        return "-"
    if t == S_IFDIR
        return "d"
    if t == S_IFLNK
        return "l"
    if t == S_IFCHR
        return "c"
    if t == S_IFBLK
        return "b"
    if t == S_IFIFO
        return "p"
    if t == S_IFSOCK
        return "s"
    return "?"

fn trio(m: i64, shift: i64, special: bool, lo: text, up: text) -> text
    let r = if (m >> (shift + 2)) & 1 == 1 then "r" else "-"
    let w = if (m >> (shift + 1)) & 1 == 1 then "w" else "-"
    let x = (m >> shift) & 1 == 1
    let e = if special then (if x then lo else up) else (if x then "x" else "-")
    return r + w + e

# The ls -l mode string, as CPython's stat.filemode writes it.
pub fn filemode(m: i64) -> text
    return type_char(m) + trio(m, 6, m & S_ISUID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 3, m & S_ISGID != 0, "s", "S") + trio(m, 0, m & S_ISVTX != 0, "t", "T")

pub fn octal(m: i64) -> text
    var o = ""
    var v = m & 4095
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 4 bound 4
        o = (v % 8).tostr() + o
        v = v / 8
        k += 1
    return o

pub struct Chmod
    mode: i64
    naive: i64

pub struct Change
    op: text
    flag: i64
    affected: i64
    value: i64
    mentioned: i64

const ORDINARY: i64 = 0
const COPY: i64 = 1
const X_IF_X: i64 = 2

fn octal_run(cs: &[text], i: usize) -> i64
    var v: i64 = 0
    var k = i
    while k < cs.len() and cs[k].len_bytes() == 1 and cs[k][0] as i64 >= 48 and cs[k][0] as i64 <= 55 bound 16777216
        v = v * 8 + (cs[k][0] as i64 - 48)
        if v > 4095
            return -1
        k += 1
    return v

fn is_oct(c: &text) -> bool = c.len_bytes() == 1 and c[0] as i64 >= 48 and c[0] as i64 <= 55

# The mode string compiled as gnulib's mode_compile does: an octal mode,
# or [ugoa]*([-+=]([rwxXst]*|[ugo]|[0-7]+))+ clauses joined by ",".
pub fn mode_compile(spec: &text) -> List[Change] ! BadPerm
    let cs = spec.chars()
    var out: List[Change] = []
    if cs.len() > 0 and is_oct(&cs[0])
        var k: usize = 0
        while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
            k += 1
        let v = octal_run(&cs, 0)
        if v < 0 or k != cs.len()
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        let men = if k < 5 then (v & (S_ISUID | S_ISGID)) | S_ISVTX | 511 else 4095
        out.push(Change(op: "=", flag: ORDINARY, affected: 4095, value: v, mentioned: men))
        return out
    var i: usize = 0
    loop bound 16777216
        var affected: i64 = 0
        loop bound 16777216
            if i >= cs.len()
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            let c = copy(cs[i])
            if c == "u"
                affected = affected | 2496
            elif c == "g"
                affected = affected | 1080
            elif c == "o"
                affected = affected | 519
            elif c == "a"
                affected = affected | 4095
            elif c == "=" or c == "+" or c == "-"
                break
            else
                fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
            i += 1
        while i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "=" or cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-") bound 16777216
            let op = copy(cs[i])
            i += 1
            var value: i64 = 0
            var mentioned: i64 = 0
            var flag = COPY
            let c = if i < cs.len() then copy(cs[i]) else ""
            if is_oct(&c)
                var k = i
                while k < cs.len() and is_oct(&cs[k]) bound 16777216
                    k += 1
                let v = octal_run(&cs, i)
                if v < 0 or affected != 0 or (k < cs.len() and cs[k] != ",")
                    fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
                i = k
                affected = 4095
                mentioned = 4095
                value = v
                flag = ORDINARY
            elif c == "u"
                value = 448
                i += 1
            elif c == "g"
                value = 56
                i += 1
            elif c == "o"
                value = 7
                i += 1
            else
                flag = ORDINARY
                while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
                    let d = copy(cs[i])
                    if d == "r"
                        value = value | 292
                    elif d == "w"
                        value = value | 146
                    elif d == "x"
                        value = value | 73
                    elif d == "X"
                        flag = X_IF_X
                    elif d == "s"
                        value = value | 3072
                    elif d == "t"
                        value = value | 512
                    else
                        break
                    i += 1
            let men = if mentioned != 0 then mentioned else (if affected != 0 then affected & value else value)
            out.push(Change(op: op, flag: flag, affected: affected, value: value, mentioned: men))
        if i >= cs.len()
            return out
        if cs[i] != ","
            fail BadPerm(why: "invalid mode")
        i += 1
    return out

# gnulib mode_adjust: the permission bits after the changes.
pub fn mode_adjust(old: i64, dir: bool, umask: i64, ch: &[Change]) -> i64
    var nm = old & 4095
    for c in ch
        let omit = (if dir then S_ISUID | S_ISGID else 0) & ~c.mentioned
        var value = c.value
        if c.flag == COPY
            value = value & nm
            var spread: i64 = 0
            if value & 292 != 0
                spread = spread | 292
            if value & 146 != 0
                spread = spread | 146
            if value & 73 != 0
                spread = spread | 73
            value = value | spread
        elif c.flag == X_IF_X
            if nm & 73 != 0 or dir
                value = value | 73
        value = value & (if c.affected != 0 then c.affected else ~umask) & ~omit
        if c.op == "="
            let preserved = (if c.affected != 0 then ~c.affected else 0) | omit
            nm = (nm & preserved) | value
        elif c.op == "+"
            nm = nm | value
        else
            nm = nm & ~value
    return nm

# chmod MODE on a file of mode `m` (type and permission bits) under a
# umask, as GNU coreutils chmod applies it (symbolic modes as POSIX
# chmod; with no who, the umask's bits are left; X means x when a
# directory or any x bit is set; for a directory the setuid and setgid
# bits stay unless the mode names them, and an octal mode of fewer than
# five digits names them only when set). `naive` is the result with umask
# 0: GNU reports "new permissions are ..." when a mode given as an option
# ("-w") sets a bit `naive` does not.
pub fn chmod(m: i64, spec: &text, umask: i64) -> Chmod ! BadPerm
    let ch = try mode_compile(spec)
    let dir = m & S_IFMT == S_IFDIR
    return Chmod(mode: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, umask, &ch), naive: (m & S_IFMT) | mode_adjust(m, dir, 0, &ch))

pub struct Cred
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    groups: List[i64]

pub const R_OK: i64 = 4
pub const W_OK: i64 = 2
pub const X_OK: i64 = 1

# POSIX.1 4.5 for a process without appropriate privileges: the owner
# class if the effective uid owns the file, else the group class if the
# effective gid or a supplementary gid is the file's group, else other;
# the requested bits (R_OK|W_OK|X_OK) must all be set in that class.
pub fn may(c: &Cred, mode: i64, owner: i64, grp: i64, want: i64) -> bool
    var cls = mode & 7
    if c.uid == owner
        cls = (mode >> 6) & 7
    else
        var in_group = c.gid == grp
        for g in c.groups
            if g == grp
                in_group = true
        if in_group
            cls = (mode >> 3) & 7
    return cls & want == want

# ---------------- Windows SIDs and ACLs ----------------

pub struct Sid
    authority: i64
    subs: List[i64]

fn digits(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 15
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or x < 48 or x > 57
            return -1
        v = v * 10 + (x - 48)
        i += 1
    return v

fn hexval(cs: &[text], lo: usize, hi: usize) -> i64
    if hi <= lo or hi - lo > 12
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    var i = lo
    while i < hi bound 16
        let x = cs[i][0] as i64
        var d: i64 = -1
        if x >= 48 and x <= 57
            d = x - 48
        elif x >= 65 and x <= 70
            d = x - 55
        elif x >= 97 and x <= 102
            d = x - 87
        if cs[i].len_bytes() != 1 or d < 0
            return -1
        v = v * 16 + d
        i += 1
    return v

# "S-1-<authority>-<sub>..." (MS-DTYP 2.4.2.1): revision 1, the authority
# in decimal below 2^32 and as 0x followed by 12 hex digits otherwise, 0
# to 15 sub-authorities each below 2^32.
pub fn sid_parse(t: &text) -> Sid ! BadPerm
    let cs = t.chars()
    if cs.len() < 5 or not (cs[0] == "S" or cs[0] == "s") or cs[1] != "-" or cs[2] != "1" or cs[3] != "-"
        fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
    var parts: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 4
    var first = true
    var auth: i64 = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 64
        var j = i
        while j < cs.len() and cs[j] != "-" bound 64
            j += 1
        var v: i64 = -1
        if first and j - i > 2 and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X")
            v = hexval(&cs, i + 2, j)
        else
            v = digits(&cs, i, j)
        if v < 0 or (first and v >= 281474976710656) or (not first and v >= 4294967296)
            fail BadPerm(why: "bad SID")
        if first
            auth = v
            first = false
        else
            parts.push(v)
        i = j + 1
    if parts.len() > 15
        fail BadPerm(why: "too many sub-authorities")
    return Sid(authority: auth, subs: parts)

fn hex12(v: i64) -> text
    let h = "0123456789ABCDEF".chars()
    var o = ""
    var x = v
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 12 bound 12
        o = copy(h[(x & 15) as usize]) + o
        x = x >> 4
        k += 1
    return o

pub fn sid_text(s: &Sid) -> text

module os.proc

# Processes (survey M39), pure. Spawning, waiting and killing are host
# capability effects (cap Spawn, Wait, Kill under grant exec, scoped to an
# allow-list of image digests); their results (pid, wait status) are
# admitted to the log, and this module decodes and describes them.
#  - Wait status codec as Linux and glibc define it (WIFEXITED,
#    WEXITSTATUS, WIFSIGNALED, WTERMSIG, WCOREDUMP, WIFSTOPPED, WSTOPSIG,
#    WIFCONTINUED) and Rust's ExitStatus on top of it: code, signal,
#    core_dumped, stopped_signal, continued, success and its Display text.
#  - The spawn spec: Rust's std::process::Command model (program, args
#    with arg0, environment changes, cwd, uid, gid, process group, stdio
#    plan) and both of its Debug forms ({:?} as a shell line, {:#?}).
#  - POSIX shell words as Python's shlex gives them: split (posix mode,
#    comments on), quote and join.
#  - The Spawn request as logged (a canonical line) and the exec grant
#    check by image digest.

error BadProc(why: text)

# ---------------- wait status ----------------

pub fn wifexited(s: i64) -> bool = s & 127 == 0
pub fn wexitstatus(s: i64) -> i64 = (s >> 8) & 255
# glibc: ((signed char) ((s & 0x7f) + 1) >> 1) > 0
pub fn wifsignaled(s: i64) -> bool
    let v = (s & 127) + 1
    let sc = if v >= 128 then v - 256 else v
    return (sc >> 1) > 0
pub fn wtermsig(s: i64) -> i64 = s & 127
pub fn wcoredump(s: i64) -> bool = s & 128 != 0
pub fn wifstopped(s: i64) -> bool = s & 255 == 127
pub fn wstopsig(s: i64) -> i64 = wexitstatus(s)
pub fn wifcontinued(s: i64) -> bool = s == 65535

# The raw status a 32-bit int holds (the low 32 bits, signed).
fn raw32(s: i64) -> i64
    let v = s & 4294967295
    return if v >= 2147483648 then v - 4294967296 else v

pub fn code(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifexited(raw32(s)) then some(wexitstatus(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifsignaled(raw32(s)) then some(wtermsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn core_dumped(s: i64) -> bool = wifsignaled(raw32(s)) and wcoredump(raw32(s))
pub fn stopped_signal(s: i64) -> i64? = if wifstopped(raw32(s)) then some(wstopsig(raw32(s))) else none
pub fn continued(s: i64) -> bool = wifcontinued(raw32(s))
# ExitStatus::success: exit_ok, i.e. the raw status is zero.
pub fn success(s: i64) -> bool = raw32(s) == 0

# Rust's signal_string for Linux x86_64, aarch64, arm and x86.
const RUST_SIGNALS: text = "HUP INT QUIT ILL TRAP ABRT BUS FPE KILL USR1 SEGV USR2 PIPE ALRM TERM STKFLT CHLD CONT STOP TSTP TTIN TTOU URG XCPU XFSZ VTALRM PROF WINCH IO PWR SYS"

pub fn signal_string(n: i64) -> text
    if n < 1 or n > 31
        return ""
    return " (SIG" + RUST_SIGNALS.split(" ")[(n - 1) as usize] + ")"

fn hex(v: i64) -> text
    let d = "0123456789abcdef".chars()
    if v == 0
        return "0"
    var x = v
    var o = ""
    while x > 0 bound 64
        o = d[(x % 16) as usize] + o
        x = x / 16
    return o

# Display for ExitStatus.
pub fn status_text(s: i64) -> text
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return "exit status: " + wexitstatus(r).tostr()
    if wifsignaled(r)
        let n = wtermsig(r)
        return "signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n) + (if wcoredump(r) then " (core dumped)" else "")
    if wifstopped(r)
        let n = wstopsig(r)
        return "stopped (not terminated) by signal: " + n.tostr() + signal_string(n)
    if wifcontinued(r)
        return "continued (WIFCONTINUED)"
    # {:#x} of an i32 prints its two's complement bits
    let u = if r < 0 then r + 4294967296 else r
    return "unrecognised wait status: " + r.tostr() + " 0x" + hex(u)

# The status a POSIX shell reports in $? for a wait status (128 + signal).
pub fn shell_status(s: i64) -> i64
    let r = raw32(s)
    if wifexited(r)
        return wexitstatus(r)
    if wifsignaled(r)
        return 128 + wtermsig(r)
    if wifstopped(r)
        return 128 + wstopsig(r)
    return -1

# ---------------- Rust str Debug ----------------

fn cp_of(c: &text) -> i64
    let b = c[0] as i64
    if b < 128
        return b
    if b < 224
        return (b & 31) << 6 | (c[1] as i64 & 63)
    if b < 240
        return (b & 15) << 12 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[2] as i64 & 63)
    return (b & 7) << 18 | (c[1] as i64 & 63) << 12 | (c[2] as i64 & 63) << 6 | (c[3] as i64 & 63)

# char::escape_debug as str's Debug uses it, for the characters a spawn
# spec carries in practice: the C0 and C1 controls, DEL and the soft
# hyphen are not printable and print as \u{..}; other characters print as
# themselves (NBSP is escaped as Rust does; grapheme extenders and the rest of Unicode's non-printable
# set are outside this model).
pub fn debug_str(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 0
            o = o + "\\0"
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32 or (v >= 127 and v <= 160) or v == 173
            o = o + "\\u{" + hex(v) + "}"
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# CStr's Debug (program, arg0 and cwd are C strings in the Command): ASCII
# as u8::escape_ascii writes it (\t \r \n \' \" \\, \xNN for other
# bytes outside 0x20..0x7e), other characters as debug_str.
pub fn debug_c(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v >= 128
            let d = debug_str(&c)
            let dc = d.chars()
            var k: usize = 1
            while k + 1 < dc.len() bound 64
                o = o + dc[k]
                k += 1
        elif v == 9
            o = o + "\\t"
        elif v == 10
            o = o + "\\n"
        elif v == 13
            o = o + "\\r"
        elif v == 39 or v == 34 or v == 92
            o = o + "\\" + c
        elif v < 32 or v == 127
            o = o + "\\x" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "") + hex(v)
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

# ---------------- Command ----------------

# Rust's os2c: a string with an interior NUL cannot become a C string, and
# the Command keeps this marker instead (spawning then fails).
pub const WITH_NUL: text = "<string-with-nul>"
fn os2c(s: &text) -> text = if s.contains("\u{0}") then WITH_NUL else copy(s)

pub struct EnvVar
    key: text
    set: bool
    val: text

pub struct Cmd
    program: text
    args: List[text]
    clear: bool
    vars: List[EnvVar]
    has_cwd: bool
    cwd: text
    uid: i64
    gid: i64
    pgroup: i64
    stdin: text
    stdout: text
    stderr: text

pub fn cmd_new(program: &text) -> Cmd = Cmd(program: os2c(program), args: [os2c(program)], clear: false, vars: [], has_cwd: false, cwd: "", uid: -1, gid: -1, pgroup: -1, stdin: "", stdout: "", stderr: "")

pub fn arg(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
    c.args.push(os2c(a))

pub fn arg0(c: &mut Cmd, a: &text)
    c.args[0] = os2c(a)

fn bytes_lt(a: &text, b: &text) -> bool
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < a.len_bytes() and i < b.len_bytes() bound 16777216
        if a[i] != b[i]
            return a[i] < b[i]
        i += 1
    return a.len_bytes() < b.len_bytes()

# CommandEnv keeps a BTreeMap from key to Option<value>.
fn put(c: &mut Cmd, v: EnvVar)
    var o: List[EnvVar] = []
    var placed = false
    for x in c.vars
        if x.key == v.key
            continue
        if not placed and bytes_lt(&v.key, &x.key)
            o.push(copy(v))
            placed = true
        o.push(copy(x))
    if not placed
        o.push(copy(v))
    c.vars = o

pub fn env(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text, v: &text)
    put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: true, val: copy(v)))

# With the environment cleared a removal only forgets the key.
pub fn env_remove(c: &mut Cmd, k: &text)
    if c.clear
        var o: List[EnvVar] = []
        for x in c.vars
            if x.key != k
                o.push(copy(x))
        c.vars = o
    else
        put(c, EnvVar(key: copy(k), set: false, val: ""))

pub fn env_clear(c: &mut Cmd)
    c.clear = true
    c.vars = []

pub fn current_dir(c: &mut Cmd, d: &text)
    c.has_cwd = true
    c.cwd = os2c(d)

# Stdio plans: "inherit", "null" or "piped".
pub fn set_stdio(c: &mut Cmd, which: &text, plan: &text) -> bool ! BadProc
    let v = if plan == "inherit" then "Inherit" else (if plan == "null" then "Null" else (if plan == "piped" then "MakePipe" else ""))
    if v == ""
        fail BadProc(why: "unknown stdio plan")
    if which == "stdin"
        c.stdin = v
    elif which == "stdout"
        c.stdout = v
    elif which == "stderr"
        c.stderr = v
    else
        fail BadProc(why: "unknown stream")
    return true

pub fn env_unchanged(c: &Cmd) -> bool = not c.clear and c.vars.len() == 0

# {:?}: a shell line.
pub fn debug(c: &Cmd) -> text
    var o = ""
    if c.has_cwd
        o = o + "cd " + debug_c(&c.cwd) + " && "
    if c.clear
        o = o + "env -i "
    else
        var any = false
        for v in c.vars
            if not v.set
                if not any
                    o = o + "env "
                    any = true
                o = o + "-u " + v.key + " "
    for v in c.vars
        if v.set
            o = o + v.key + "=" + debug_str(&v.val) + " "
    if c.program != c.args[0]
        o = o + "[" + debug_c(&c.program) + "] "
    o = o + debug_c(&c.args[0])
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < c.args.len() bound 16777216
        o = o + " " + debug_str(&c.args[i])
        i += 1
    return o

fn some_block(ind: text, v: text) -> text = "Some(\n" + ind + "    " + v + ",\n" + ind + ")"

# {:#?}: Rust's pretty Debug of the Command struct (Linux field set).
pub fn debug_pretty(c: &Cmd) -> text
    var o = "Command {\n    program: " + debug_c(&c.program) + ",\n    args: [\n"
    for a in c.args
        o = o + "        " + debug_c(&a) + ",\n"
    o = o + "    ],\n"
    if not env_unchanged(c)
        o = o + "    env: CommandEnv {\n        clear: " + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\n        vars: {"
        if c.vars.len() == 0
            o = o + "},\n"
        else
            o = o + "\n"
            for v in c.vars
                o = o + "            " + debug_str(&v.key) + ": " + (if v.set then some_block("            ", debug_str(&v.val)) else "None") + ",\n"
            o = o + "        },\n"
        o = o + "    },\n"
    if c.has_cwd
        o = o + "    cwd: " + some_block("    ", debug_c(&c.cwd)) + ",\n"
    if c.uid >= 0
        o = o + "    uid: " + some_block("    ", c.uid.tostr()) + ",\n"
    if c.gid >= 0
        o = o + "    gid: " + some_block("    ", c.gid.tostr()) + ",\n"
    if c.stdin != ""
        o = o + "    stdin: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stdin)) + ",\n"
    if c.stdout != ""
        o = o + "    stdout: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stdout)) + ",\n"
    if c.stderr != ""
        o = o + "    stderr: " + some_block("    ", copy(c.stderr)) + ",\n"
    if c.pgroup >= 0
        o = o + "    pgroup: " + some_block("    ", c.pgroup.tostr()) + ",\n"
    return o + "    create_pidfd: false,\n}"

# ---------------- POSIX shell words (Python shlex) ----------------

fn is_ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\r" or c == "\n"

# shlex.split(s, comments=True): posix mode, whitespace_split; "#" starts
# a comment to the end of the line; quotes ' and "; escape \ (inside
# double quotes it escapes only " and \).
pub fn shlex_split(s: &text) -> List[text] ! BadProc
    let cs = s.chars()
    var out: List[text] = []
    var tok = ""
    var st = " "
    var esc_from = ""
    var i: usize = 0
    while i <= cs.len() bound 16777216
        let eof = i == cs.len()
        let c = if eof then "" else copy(cs[i])
        i += 1
        if st == " " or st == "a"
            if eof
                break
            if is_ws(&c)
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "#"
                while i < cs.len() and cs[i] != "\n" bound 16777216
                    i += 1
                if i < cs.len()
                    i += 1
                if st == "a"
                    out.push(tok)
                    tok = ""
                    st = " "
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "a"
                st = "\\"
            elif c == "'" or c == "\""
                st = c
            else
                tok = tok + c
                st = "a"
        elif st == "'"
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "'"
                st = "a"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        elif st == "\""
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No closing quotation")
            if c == "\""
                st = "a"
            elif c == "\\"
                esc_from = "\""
                st = "\\"
            else
                tok = tok + c
        else
            if eof
                fail BadProc(why: "No escaped character")
            if esc_from == "\"" and c != "\"" and c != "\\"
                tok = tok + "\\"
            tok = tok + c
            st = esc_from
    if st == "a"
        out.push(tok)
    return out

fn safe_char(c: &text) -> bool
    if c.len_bytes() != 1
        return false
    let v = c[0] as i64
    return (v >= 48 and v <= 57) or (v >= 65 and v <= 90) or (v >= 97 and v <= 122) or "@%_-+=:,./".contains(c)

# shlex.quote
pub fn shlex_quote(s: &text) -> text
    if s == ""
        return "''"
    var safe = true
    for c in s.chars()
        if not safe_char(&c)
            safe = false
    if safe
        return copy(s)
    var o = "'"
    for c in s.chars()
        o = o + (if c == "'" then "'\"'\"'" else c)
    return o + "'"

pub fn shlex_join(ws: &List[text]) -> text
    var o: List[text] = []
    for w in ws
        o.push(shlex_quote(&w))
    return " ".join(o)

# ---------------- Spawn request and the exec grant ----------------

fn jstr(s: &text) -> text
    var o = "\""
    for c in s.chars()
        let v = cp_of(&c)
        if v == 34
            o = o + "\\\""
        elif v == 92
            o = o + "\\\\"
        elif v < 32
            o = o + "\\u00" + (if v < 16 then "0" else "1") + "0123456789abcdef".chars()[(v % 16) as usize]
        else
            o = o + c
    return o + "\""

fn plan_json(x: &text) -> text = if x == "Null" then "\"null\"" else (if x == "MakePipe" then "\"piped\"" else "\"inherit\"")

# The Spawn effect as logged: a canonical JSON line (keys sorted, as JCS
# orders ASCII keys) naming the image digest, argv, the environment
# changes, cwd and the stdio plan.
pub fn spawn_request(c: &Cmd, digest: &text) -> text
    var argv: List[text] = []
    for a in c.args
        argv.push(jstr(&a))
    var ev: List[text] = []
    for v in c.vars
        ev.push("[" + jstr(&v.key) + "," + (if v.set then jstr(&v.val) else "null") + "]")
    return "{\"argv\":[" + ",".join(argv) + "],\"clear\":" + (if c.clear then "true" else "false") + ",\"cwd\":" + (if c.has_cwd then jstr(&c.cwd) else "null") + ",\"env\":[" + ",".join(ev) + "],\"image\":" + jstr(digest) + ",\"stdio\":[" + plan_json(&c.stdin) + "," + plan_json(&c.stdout) + "," + plan_json(&c.stderr) + "]}"

# grant exec: the image digest must be on the allow-list (deny by default).
pub fn exec_granted(allow: &List[text], digest: &text) -> bool
    for a in allow
        if a == digest
            return true
    return false

# in a Form: the host takes it (blocked, then dequeued as signalfd or
# sigtimedwait does) and admits it as an event Signal(kind) at the next
# tick boundary. Sending one is cap Kill under grant exec.

#    (x86, ARM and most others), Alpha/SPARC, MIPS and PA-RISC (signal(7))
#    and on Darwin (xnu bsd/sys/signal.h), its default action and the
#    standard that defines it.
#  - glibc's strsignal text and bash's kill -l names on Linux.
#  - Windows console control events and their nearest signal.
#  - The pending-signal model the host uses to order admissions, as Linux

#    while pending is dropped, the first value kept); a real-time signal
#    (34 to 64) queues every send; setting a disposition that ignores a

#    sending SIGCONT discards pending stop signals and a stop signal
