module os.signal

# Signals (survey M40), pure. A signal never runs an asynchronous handler
# in a Form: the host takes it (blocked, then dequeued as signalfd or
# sigtimedwait does) and admits it as an event Signal(kind) at the next
# tick boundary. Sending one is cap Kill under grant exec.
#  - The cross-OS table: each signal name with its number on Linux
#    (x86, ARM and most others), Alpha/SPARC, MIPS and PA-RISC (signal(7))
#    and on Darwin (xnu bsd/sys/signal.h), its default action and the
#    standard that defines it.
#  - glibc's strsignal text and bash's kill -l names on Linux.
#  - Windows console control events and their nearest signal.
#  - The pending-signal model the host uses to order admissions, as Linux
#    keeps it: a standard signal is pending at most once (a second send
#    while pending is dropped, the first value kept); a real-time signal
#    (34 to 64) queues every send; setting a disposition that ignores a
#    signal (SIG_IGN, or SIG_DFL for CONT, CHLD, WINCH, URG) discards its
#    pending sends, yet a send to a blocked, ignored signal stays pending;
#    sending SIGCONT discards pending stop signals and a stop signal
#    discards a pending SIGCONT; dequeuing takes the synchronous signals
#    (SEGV, BUS, ILL, TRAP, FPE, SYS) first, then the lowest number, and
#    real-time instances in the order sent.

error BadSignal(why: text)

# name linux alpha/sparc mips parisc darwin action standard ("-" absent;
# alpha/sparc "29/-" lists Alpha then SPARC).
const TABLE: text = "SIGABRT 6 6 6 6 6 Core P1990|SIGALRM 14 14 14 14 14 Term P1990|SIGBUS 7 10 10 10 10 Core P2001|SIGCHLD 17 20 18 18 20 Ign P2001|SIGCLD - - 18 - - Ign -|SIGCONT 18 19 25 26 19 Cont P1990|SIGEMT - 7 7 - 7 Term -|SIGFPE 8 8 8 8 8 Core P1990|SIGHUP 1 1 1 1 1 Term P1990|SIGILL 4 4 4 4 4 Core P1990|SIGINFO - 29/- - - 29 - -|SIGINT 2 2 2 2 2 Term P1990|SIGIO 29 23 22 22 23 Term -|SIGIOT 6 6 6 6 6 Core -|SIGKILL 9 9 9 9 9 Term P1990|SIGLOST - -/29 - - - Term -|SIGPIPE 13 13 13 13 13 Term P1990|SIGPOLL 29 23 22 22 - Term P2001|SIGPROF 27 27 29 21 27 Term P2001|SIGPWR 30 29/- 19 19 - Term -|SIGQUIT 3 3 3 3 3 Core P1990|SIGSEGV 11 11 11 11 11 Core P1990|SIGSTKFLT 16 - - 7 - Term -|SIGSTOP 19 17 23 24 17 Stop P1990|SIGTSTP 20 18 24 25 18 Stop P1990|SIGSYS 31 12 12 31 12 Core P2001|SIGTERM 15 15 15 15 15 Term P1990|SIGTRAP 5 5 5 5 5 Core P2001|SIGTTIN 21 21 26 27 21 Stop P1990|SIGTTOU 22 22 27 28 22 Stop P1990|SIGUNUSED 31 - - 31 - Core -|SIGURG 23 16 21 29 16 Ign P2001|SIGUSR1 10 30 16 16 30 Term P1990|SIGUSR2 12 31 17 17 31 Term P1990|SIGVTALRM 26 26 28 20 26 Term P2001|SIGXCPU 24 24 30 12 24 Core P2001|SIGXFSZ 25 25 31 30 25 Core P2001|SIGWINCH 28 28 20 23 28 Ign P2024"

pub struct SigRow
    name: text
    linux: text
    alpha_sparc: text
    mips: text
    parisc: text
    darwin: text
    action: text
    standard: text

pub fn rows() -> List[SigRow]
    var o: List[SigRow] = []
    for r in TABLE.split("|")
        let f = r.split(" ")
        o.push(SigRow(name: copy(f[0]), linux: copy(f[1]), alpha_sparc: copy(f[2]), mips: copy(f[3]), parisc: copy(f[4]), darwin: copy(f[5]), action: copy(f[6]), standard: copy(f[7])))
    return o

fn num(s: &text) -> i64
    if s == "" or s == "-"
        return -1
    var v: i64 = 0
    for c in s.chars()
        v = v * 10 + (c[0] as i64 - 48)
    return v

fn row(name: &text) -> SigRow ! BadSignal
    for r in rows()
        if r.name == name
            return r
    fail BadSignal(why: "unknown signal")

# Numbers by target: "linux", "darwin", "alpha", "sparc", "mips", "parisc"; -1 when absent.
pub fn number(name: &text, target: &text) -> i64 ! BadSignal
    let r = try row(name)
    if target == "linux"
        return num(&r.linux)
    if target == "darwin"
        return num(&r.darwin)
    if target == "mips"
        return num(&r.mips)
    if target == "parisc"
        return num(&r.parisc)
    if target == "alpha" or target == "sparc"
        let p = r.alpha_sparc.split("/")
        if p.len() == 1
            return num(&p[0])
        let k: usize = if target == "alpha" then 0 else 1
        return num(&p[k])
    fail BadSignal(why: "unknown target")

# The default action of signal(7): Term, Core, Ign, Stop or Cont ("-" for SIGINFO, a synonym).
pub fn action(name: &text) -> text ! BadSignal
    let r = try row(name)
    return copy(r.action)

pub fn standard(name: &text) -> text ! BadSignal
    let r = try row(name)
    return copy(r.standard)

# The preferred name of a number on a target (the synonyms of signal(7),
# SIGIOT, SIGPOLL, SIGCLD, SIGUNUSED and on Linux SIGINFO, are not preferred); "" when there is none.
const SYNONYMS: text = "SIGIOT SIGPOLL SIGCLD SIGUNUSED SIGINFO"

pub fn name_of(n: i64, target: &text) -> text
    let syn = SYNONYMS.split(" ")
    for r in rows()
        if syn.contains(&r.name) and not (target == "darwin" and r.name == "SIGINFO")
            continue
        let v = number(&r.name, target) catch -1
        if v == n
            return copy(r.name)
    return ""

# Linux x86-64 with glibc: SIGRTMIN is 34 (32 and 33 are taken by the C library), SIGRTMAX 64.
pub const RTMIN: i64 = 34
pub const RTMAX: i64 = 64

# bash's kill -l name of a Linux signal number (without "SIG").
# 0 is the shell's EXIT trap; "" for 32, 33 and numbers out of range.
pub fn kill_l(n: i64) -> text
    if n == 0
        return "EXIT"
    if n >= RTMIN and n <= RTMAX
        if n == RTMIN
            return "RTMIN"
        if n == RTMAX
            return "RTMAX"
        if n - RTMIN <= 15
            return "RTMIN+" + (n - RTMIN).tostr()
        return "RTMAX-" + (RTMAX - n).tostr()
    let lx = "linux"
    let s = name_of(n, &lx)
    if s == ""
        return ""
    let cs = s.chars()
    var o = ""
    var i: usize = 3
    while i < cs.len() bound 64
        o = o + cs[i]
        i += 1
    return o

const GLIBC_TEXT: text = "Hangup|Interrupt|Quit|Illegal instruction|Trace/breakpoint trap|Aborted|Bus error|Floating point exception|Killed|User defined signal 1|Segmentation fault|User defined signal 2|Broken pipe|Alarm clock|Terminated|Stack fault|Child exited|Continued|Stopped (signal)|Stopped|Stopped (tty input)|Stopped (tty output)|Urgent I/O condition|CPU time limit exceeded|File size limit exceeded|Virtual timer expired|Profiling timer expired|Window changed|I/O possible|Power failure|Bad system call"

# glibc strsignal on Linux.
pub fn strsignal(n: i64) -> text
    if n >= 1 and n <= 31
        return copy(GLIBC_TEXT.split("|")[(n - 1) as usize])
    if n >= RTMIN and n <= RTMAX
        return "Real-time signal " + (n - RTMIN).tostr()
    return "Unknown signal " + n.tostr()

# Windows console control events (wincon.h) and the C runtime signal a
# console program sees for them (SIGINT for Ctrl+C, SIGBREAK = 21 for the
# others); "" for an unknown event.
pub fn console_event(code: i64) -> text
    if code == 0
        return "CTRL_C_EVENT"
    if code == 1
        return "CTRL_BREAK_EVENT"
    if code == 2
        return "CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT"
    if code == 5
        return "CTRL_LOGOFF_EVENT"
    if code == 6
        return "CTRL_SHUTDOWN_EVENT"
    return ""

pub fn console_signal(code: i64) -> i64
    if code == 0
        return 2
    if code == 1 or code == 2 or code == 5 or code == 6
        return 21
    return -1

# ---------------- pending signals (Linux) ----------------

pub struct Queued
    sig: i64
    val: i64

pub struct Pending
    std: List[bool]
    stdval: List[i64]
    rt: List[Queued]
    ignored: List[bool]

pub fn pending_new() -> Pending
    var b: List[bool] = []
    var v: List[i64] = []
    var k: i64 = 0
    while k < 65 bound 65
        b.push(false)
        v.push(0)
        k += 1
    return Pending(std: copy(b), stdval: v, rt: [], ignored: b)

fn is_rt(n: i64) -> bool = n >= 32

fn flush(p: &mut Pending, n: i64)
    p.std[n as usize] = false
    var o: List[Queued] = []
    for q in p.rt
        if q.sig != n
            o.push(copy(q))
    p.rt = o

fn kernel_ignore(n: i64) -> bool = n == 18 or n == 17 or n == 28 or n == 23

fn valid(n: i64) -> bool = n >= 1 and n <= 64

# sigaction: "ign", "dfl" or "catch". An ignoring disposition discards
# the pending sends of that signal.
pub fn set_disposition(p: &mut Pending, n: i64, how: &text) -> bool ! BadSignal
    if not valid(n) or n == 9 or n == 19
        fail BadSignal(why: "invalid signal")
    let ign = how == "ign" or (how == "dfl" and kernel_ignore(n))
    p.ignored[n as usize] = ign
    if ign
        flush(p, n)
    return true

fn is_stop(n: i64) -> bool = n == 19 or n == 20 or n == 21 or n == 22

# A send while every signal is blocked (the host's way of receiving them).
pub fn sig_send(p: &mut Pending, n: i64, val: i64) -> bool ! BadSignal
    if not valid(n)
        fail BadSignal(why: "invalid signal")
    if is_stop(n)
        flush(p, 18)
    elif n == 18
        flush(p, 19)
        flush(p, 20)
        flush(p, 21)
        flush(p, 22)
    if is_rt(n)
        p.rt.push(Queued(sig: n, val: val))
    elif not p.std[n as usize]
        p.std[n as usize] = true
        p.stdval[n as usize] = val
    return true

fn sync_sig(n: i64) -> bool = n == 11 or n == 7 or n == 4 or n == 5 or n == 8 or n == 31

fn has_rt(p: &Pending, n: i64) -> bool
    for q in p.rt
        if q.sig == n
            return true
    return false

# Dequeue the next pending signal among `set` (sigtimedwait, signalfd);
# none when no signal of the set is pending.
pub fn dequeue(p: &mut Pending, set: &List[i64]) -> Queued?
    var best: i64 = -1
    var bsync = false
    for n in set
        if not valid(n)
            continue
        let pend = if is_rt(n) then has_rt(p, n) else p.std[n as usize]
        if not pend
            continue
        let s = sync_sig(n)
        if best < 0 or (s and not bsync) or (s == bsync and n < best)
            best = n
            bsync = s
    if best < 0
        return none
    if not is_rt(best)
        p.std[best as usize] = false
        return some(Queued(sig: best, val: p.stdval[best as usize]))
    var o: List[Queued] = []
    var got = Queued(sig: -1, val: 0)
    for q in p.rt
        if got.sig < 0 and q.sig == best
            got = copy(q)
        else
            o.push(copy(q))
    p.rt = o
    return some(got)

# Every pending signal in admission order (all dequeued): the Signal
# events the host admits at a tick boundary.
pub fn drain(p: &mut Pending) -> List[Queued]
    var all: List[i64] = []
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k <= 64 bound 64
        all.push(k)
        k += 1
    var o: List[Queued] = []
    loop bound 1048576
        match dequeue(p, &all)
            some(q) -> o.push(q)
            none -> break
    return o

module os.svc
# Services (survey M44), pure: the supervision decisions a host makes for a
# service unit, as systemd makes them (src/shared/exit-status.c,
# src/basic/signal-util.c, src/core/service.c at systemd main, Oct 2026):
#  - exit status names (SUCCESS, TEMPFAIL, NAMESPACE, ...) and their class
#    (libc, systemd, LSB, BSD), and the exit status a word names;
#  - signal names as systemd reads them: numbers, HUP or SIGHUP,
#    RTMIN+n and RTMAX-n (Linux numbering: SIGRTMIN 34, SIGRTMAX 64);
#  - SuccessExitStatus=, RestartPreventExitStatus= and
#    RestartForceExitStatus= sets, with systemd's number syntax (decimal,
#    0x hex, C octal, 0o and 0b prefixes);
#  - the result of a main process exit (clean, exit-code, signal,
#    core-dump) and the Restart= decision with its reason;
#  - launchd's KeepAlive decision (launchd.plist(5): a bool, or a dict of
#    SuccessfulExit and Crashed conditions) and the Windows service
#    control manager's failure actions (sc failure / sc failureflag),
#    both recorded live (vectors/os/svc/launchd_keepalive.tsv on macOS
#    27.0.1, vectors/os/svc/scm_failure_actions.tsv on Windows build
#    26200).
# Codes and statuses are those of waitid(2): code "exited" with the exit
# status, "killed" or "dumped" with the signal number.

error BadSvc(why: text)

const EINVAL: i64 = -22
const ERANGE: i64 = -34
const SIGRTMIN: i64 = 34
const SIGRTMAX: i64 = 64
const NSIG: i64 = 65

const EXIT_CODES: List[i64] = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 200, 201, 202, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207, 208, 209, 210, 211, 212, 213, 214, 215, 216, 217, 218, 219, 220, 221, 222, 224, 225, 226, 227, 228, 229, 230, 231, 232, 233, 235, 236, 237, 238, 239, 240, 241, 242, 243, 244, 245, 246, 255]
const EXIT_NAMES: List[text] = ["SUCCESS", "FAILURE", "INVALIDARGUMENT", "NOTIMPLEMENTED", "NOPERMISSION", "NOTINSTALLED", "NOTCONFIGURED", "NOTRUNNING", "USAGE", "DATAERR", "NOINPUT", "NOUSER", "NOHOST", "UNAVAILABLE", "SOFTWARE", "OSERR", "OSFILE", "CANTCREAT", "IOERR", "TEMPFAIL", "PROTOCOL", "NOPERM", "CONFIG", "CHDIR", "NICE", "FDS", "EXEC", "MEMORY", "LIMITS", "OOM_ADJUST", "SIGNAL_MASK", "STDIN", "STDOUT", "CHROOT", "IOPRIO", "TIMERSLACK", "SECUREBITS", "SETSCHEDULER", "CPUAFFINITY", "GROUP", "USER", "CAPABILITIES", "CGROUP", "SETSID", "CONFIRM", "STDERR", "PAM", "NETWORK", "NAMESPACE", "NO_NEW_PRIVILEGES", "SECCOMP", "SELINUX_CONTEXT", "PERSONALITY", "APPARMOR", "ADDRESS_FAMILIES", "RUNTIME_DIRECTORY", "CHOWN", "SMACK_PROCESS_LABEL", "KEYRING", "STATE_DIRECTORY", "CACHE_DIRECTORY", "LOGS_DIRECTORY", "CONFIGURATION_DIRECTORY", "NUMA_POLICY", "CREDENTIALS", "BPF", "KSM", "MEMORY_THP", "EXCEPTION"]
const EXIT_CLASSES: List[text] = ["libc", "libc", "LSB", "LSB", "LSB", "LSB", "LSB", "LSB", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "BSD", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd", "systemd"]
const SIGNAMES: List[text] = ["", "HUP", "INT", "QUIT", "ILL", "TRAP", "ABRT", "BUS", "FPE", "KILL", "USR1", "SEGV", "USR2", "PIPE", "ALRM", "TERM", "STKFLT", "CHLD", "CONT", "STOP", "TSTP", "TTIN", "TTOU", "URG", "XCPU", "XFSZ", "VTALRM", "PROF", "WINCH", "IO", "PWR", "SYS"]

# ---------------- numbers as systemd reads them ----------------

fn ws(c: &text) -> bool = c == " " or c == "\t" or c == "\n" or c == "\r"
# isspace() of the C locale, which strtoul skips on its own
fn cspace(c: &text) -> bool = ws(c) or c == "\u{b}" or c == "\u{c}"

fn digit_val(c: &text) -> i64
    if c.len_bytes() != 1
        return 99
    let b = c[0] as i64
    if b >= 48 and b <= 57
        return b - 48
    if b >= 97 and b <= 122
        return b - 87
    if b >= 65 and b <= 90
        return b - 55
    return 99

pub struct Num
    err: i64
    val: i64
    neg: bool

# strtoul()/strtol() after systemd's mangle_base(): leading WHITESPACE is
# dropped, "0b"/"0B" and "0o"/"0O" select base 2 and 8, otherwise C's
# base 0 rules (0x hex, a leading 0 octal). The whole text must be a
# number; values past 2^40 are reported as out of range (every caller
# needs them below 2^31).
fn c_num(s: &text) -> Num
    let cs = s.chars()
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < cs.len() and ws(&cs[i]) bound 16777216
        i += 1
    var base: i64 = 0
    if i + 1 < cs.len() and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "b" or cs[i + 1] == "B")
        base = 2
        i += 2
    else
        if i + 1 < cs.len() and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "o" or cs[i + 1] == "O")
            base = 8
            i += 2
    while i < cs.len() and cspace(&cs[i]) bound 16777216
        i += 1
    var neg = false
    if i < cs.len() and (cs[i] == "+" or cs[i] == "-")
        neg = cs[i] == "-"
        i += 1
    # glibc 2.38+ (C23, as systemd is built): 0x before hex digits in
    # base 0, 0b before binary digits in base 0 and base 2
    let pre_x = i + 2 < cs.len() and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "x" or cs[i + 1] == "X") and digit_val(&cs[i + 2]) < 16
    let pre_b = i + 2 < cs.len() and cs[i] == "0" and (cs[i + 1] == "b" or cs[i + 1] == "B") and digit_val(&cs[i + 2]) < 2
    if base == 0 and pre_x
        base = 16
        i += 2
    if (base == 0 or base == 2) and pre_b
        base = 2
        i += 2
    if base == 0
        base = if i < cs.len() and cs[i] == "0" then 8 else 10
    var v: i64 = 0
    var n: i64 = 0
    var big = false
    while i < cs.len() and digit_val(&cs[i]) < base bound 16777216
        v = v * base + digit_val(&cs[i])
        if v > 1099511627776
            big = true
            v = 1099511627776
        n += 1
        i += 1
    if big
        return Num(err: ERANGE, val: 0, neg: neg)
    if n == 0 or i < cs.len()
        return Num(err: EINVAL, val: 0, neg: neg)
    return Num(err: 0, val: v, neg: neg)

# safe_atou8: 0 to 255, negative numbers out of range.
fn atou8(s: &text) -> i64
    let r = c_num(s)
    if r.err < 0
        return r.err
    if r.neg and r.val != 0
        return ERANGE
    if r.val > 255
        return ERANGE
    return r.val

# safe_atoi: the signed value, or an error.
fn atoi(s: &text) -> Num
    let r = c_num(s)
    if r.err < 0
        return r
    if r.val > 2147483648 or (r.val == 2147483648 and not r.neg)
        return Num(err: ERANGE, val: 0, neg: false)
    return Num(err: 0, val: if r.neg then 0 - r.val else r.val, neg: r.neg)

# ---------------- exit statuses and signals ----------------

# The name systemd gives an exit status ("" if none).
pub fn exit_status_name(code: i64) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < EXIT_CODES.len() bound 1024
        if EXIT_CODES[i] == code
            return copy(EXIT_NAMES[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# libc, systemd, LSB or BSD ("" if the status has no name).
pub fn exit_status_class(code: i64) -> text
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < EXIT_CODES.len() bound 1024
        if EXIT_CODES[i] == code
            return copy(EXIT_CLASSES[i])
        i += 1
    return ""

# exit_status_from_string: a name, or a number 0 to 255; a negative errno
# (-22 malformed, -34 out of range) otherwise.
pub fn exit_status_from_string(s: &text) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < EXIT_NAMES.len() bound 1024
        if EXIT_NAMES[i] == s
            return EXIT_CODES[i]
        i += 1
    return atou8(s)

fn rt_offset(p: &text, lo: i64, hi: i64, base: i64) -> i64
    let r = atoi(p)
    if r.err < 0
        return r.err
    if r.val < lo or r.val > hi
        return ERANGE
    return r.val + base

# signal_from_string: a number 1 to 64, a name with or without SIG,
# RTMIN, RTMIN+n, RTMAX, RTMAX-n; a negative errno otherwise.
pub fn signal_from_string(s: &text) -> i64
    let n = atoi(s)
    if n.err == 0
        return if n.val > 0 and n.val < NSIG then n.val else ERANGE
    let t = if s.startswith("SIG") then drop_front(s, 3) else copy(s)
    var i: usize = 1
    while i < SIGNAMES.len() bound 64
        if SIGNAMES[i] == t
            return i as i64
        i += 1
    if t.startswith("RTMIN")
        let p = drop_front(&t, 5)
        if p == ""
            return SIGRTMIN
        if not p.startswith("+")
            return EINVAL
        return rt_offset(&p, 0, SIGRTMAX - SIGRTMIN, SIGRTMIN)
    if t.startswith("RTMAX")
        let p = drop_front(&t, 5)
        if p == ""
            return SIGRTMAX
        if not p.startswith("-")
            return EINVAL
        return rt_offset(&p, SIGRTMIN - SIGRTMAX, 0, SIGRTMAX)
    return EINVAL

fn drop_front(t: &text, n: i64) -> text
    let cs = t.chars()
    var o: List[text] = []
    var i = n as usize
    while i < cs.len() bound 16777216
        o.push(copy(cs[i]))
        i += 1
    return "".join(o)

# The name of a signal (HUP, RTMIN+3), or its number.
pub fn signal_name(n: i64) -> text
    if n > 0 and n < 32
        return copy(SIGNAMES[n as usize])
    if n >= SIGRTMIN and n <= SIGRTMAX
        return "RTMIN+" + (n - SIGRTMIN).tostr()
    return n.tostr()

# ---------------- status sets ----------------

# Exit statuses and signals, each ascending without duplicates.
pub struct StatusSet
    status: List[i64]
    signal: List[i64]

fn add_sorted(xs: &List[i64], v: i64) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var done = false
    for x in xs
        if not done and v <= x
            if v < x
                o.push(v)
            done = true
        o.push(x)
    if not done
        o.push(v)
    return o

fn has(xs: &List[i64], v: i64) -> bool
    for x in xs
        if x == v
            return true
    return false

# A SuccessExitStatus=-style value: words separated by whitespace, each an
# exit status (name or number) or else a signal; words that are neither
# are skipped (systemd logs and ignores them). Quotes and backslashes are
# refused (systemd's word splitter would unquote them).
pub fn status_set_parse(v: &text) -> StatusSet ! BadSvc
    if v.contains("\"") or v.contains("'") or v.contains("\\")
        fail BadSvc(why: "quoted words are not supported")
    var st: List[i64] = []
    var sg: List[i64] = []
    var cur: List[text] = []
    var words: List[text] = []
    for c in v.chars()
        if ws(&c)
            if cur.len() > 0
                words.push("".join(cur))
                cur = []
        else
            cur.push(c)
    if cur.len() > 0
        words.push("".join(cur))
    for w in words
        let e = exit_status_from_string(&w)
        if e >= 0
            st = add_sorted(&st, e)
        else
            let g = signal_from_string(&w)
            if g >= 0
                sg = add_sorted(&sg, g)
    return StatusSet(status: st, signal: sg)

fn set_test(x: &StatusSet, code: &text, status: i64) -> bool
    if code == "exited" and has(&x.status, status)
        return true
    return (code == "killed" or code == "dumped") and has(&x.signal, status)

# is_clean_exit: a daemon (a main process not of Type=oneshot) may also
# die of SIGHUP, SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGPIPE. `success` holds
# SuccessExitStatus= (systemd's own helper processes pass none: use_set
# false).
pub fn is_clean_exit(code: &text, status: i64, daemon: bool, success: &StatusSet, use_set: bool) -> bool
    if code == "exited"
        return status == 0 or (use_set and has(&success.status, status))
    if code == "killed"
        return (daemon and (status == 1 or status == 2 or status == 15 or status == 13)) or (use_set and has(&success.signal, status))
    return false

# The result of a main process exit (service_sigchld_event).
pub fn exit_result(stype: &text, code: &text, status: i64, success: &StatusSet) -> text
    let daemon = stype != "oneshot"
    if is_clean_exit(code, status, daemon, success, true)
        return "success"
    if code == "exited"
        return "exit-code"
    if code == "killed"
        return "signal"
    return "core-dump"

# ---------------- Restart= ----------------

pub struct Restart
    yes: bool
    reason: text

pub struct Policy
    rst: text
    stype: text
    prevent: StatusSet
    force: StatusSet

# service_shall_restart: Restart= is one of no, on-success, on-failure,
# on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort, always; result one of success,
# resources, protocol, timeout, exit-code, signal, core-dump, watchdog,
# start-limit-hit, oom-kill, condition; code/status the main process's
# exit; manual_stop when the stop was asked for.
pub fn shall_restart(p: &Policy, result: &text, code: &text, status: i64, manual_stop: bool) -> Restart
    if manual_stop
        return Restart(yes: false, reason: "manual stop")
    if set_test(&p.prevent, code, status)
        return Restart(yes: false, reason: "prevented by exit status")
    if set_test(&p.force, code, status)
        if p.stype == "oneshot" and result == "success"
            return Restart(yes: false, reason: "service type and exit status")
        return Restart(yes: true, reason: "forced by exit status")
    let r = p.rst
    let ok = result == "success"
    let skip = result == "condition"
    var y = false
    if r == "always"
        y = not skip
    if r == "on-success"
        y = ok
    if r == "on-failure"
        y = not ok and not skip
    if r == "on-abnormal"
        y = not ok and not skip and result != "exit-code"
    if r == "on-watchdog"
        y = result == "watchdog"
    if r == "on-abort"
        y = result == "signal" or result == "core-dump"
    return Restart(yes: y, reason: "restart setting")

# ---------------- launchd ----------------

# KeepAlive: form "none" (key absent), "bool" (value) or "dict" with
# SuccessfulExit and Crashed each "", "true" or "false".
pub struct KeepAlive
    form: text
    value: bool
    successful: text
    crashed: text

# Darwin signals launchd counts as a crash: SIGILL, SIGTRAP, SIGABRT,
# SIGFPE, SIGBUS, SIGSEGV, SIGSYS.
pub fn darwin_crash_signal(sig: i64) -> bool = sig == 4 or sig == 5 or sig == 6 or sig == 8 or sig == 10 or sig == 11 or sig == 12

# Whether launchd starts the job again after it ended: exited with
# `status`, or (exited false) killed by Darwin signal `status`. A dict
# keeps the job alive when any of its conditions holds: SuccessfulExit
# true/false on an exit 0 / anything else, Crashed true/false on a crash
# signal / anything else.
pub fn launchd_relaunch(k: &KeepAlive, exited: bool, status: i64) -> bool
    if k.form == "bool"
        return k.value
    if k.form != "dict"
        return false
    let ok = exited and status == 0
    let crash = not exited and darwin_crash_signal(status)
    if k.successful == "true" and ok
        return true
    if k.successful == "false" and not ok
        return true
    if k.crashed == "true" and crash
        return true
    if k.crashed == "false" and not crash
        return true
    return false

# ---------------- Windows service control manager ----------------

# The failure actions of `sc failure ... actions= a/d/a/d...` as their
# kinds ("restart", "none", "run", "reboot"), and `sc failureflag` (on:
# a stop with a non-zero exit code counts as a failure too).
pub struct ScmPolicy
    actions: List[text]
    nonzero_is_failure: bool

# Whether the SCM treats the end of the service process as a failure:
# it ended without reporting SERVICE_STOPPED (crashed), or, with the
# failure flag, reported SERVICE_STOPPED with a non-zero exit code.
pub fn scm_failure(p: &ScmPolicy, crashed: bool, exit_code: i64) -> bool = crashed or (p.nonzero_is_failure and exit_code != 0)

# The action for the n-th failure since the reset period began (n from
# 1); the last action repeats; "none" when there are none.
pub fn scm_action(p: &ScmPolicy, n: i64) -> text
    if p.actions.len() == 0
        return "none"
    let i = if n > p.actions.len() as i64 then p.actions.len() - 1 else (n - 1) as usize
    return copy(p.actions[i])

# How many times the service runs when every run ends the same way,
# capped at `cap` (a policy that keeps restarting reaches it).
pub fn scm_runs(p: &ScmPolicy, crashed: bool, exit_code: i64, cap: i64) -> i64
    var runs: i64 = 1
    while runs < cap bound 1024
        if not scm_failure(p, crashed, exit_code)
            return runs
        if scm_action(p, runs) != "restart"
            return runs
        runs += 1
    return runs

module rand.det

# Deterministic random streams (survey M12). A generator is the RFC 8439

# handling an event that carries it. `from_seed` is for seeds that are
# already part of the program or its log (test vectors, replays, a value
# split from another generator). Not for keys: this is reference code and
# not constant time; key material comes straight from logged Random bytes.
#
# Stream: key = the 32 seed bytes; nonce = stream id (bytes 0..7, little
# endian) followed by 4 zero bytes; block counter starts at 0. Blocks past
# 2^32 carry into the third nonce word, so for counters below 2^32 the
# output is exactly the RFC 8439 keystream. Words are taken in order and
# serialise little endian. Bytes are List[i64] with values 0..255; words
# are i64 masked to 32 bits.
const v0: i64 = 4294967295

# Cap[Entropy] in the event that delivers the Random bytes.

error x1(v3: i64, v4: i64)

pub struct t1
    v5: List[i64]
    v6: i64
    v7: i64
    v8: List[i64]
    v9: i64

fn f1(v12: &[i64], v13: usize) -> i64 = v12[v13] | (v12[v13 + 1] << 8) | (v12[v13 + 2] << 16) | (v12[v13 + 3] << 24)

    v14[v16] = (v14[v16] + v14[v17]) & v0
    v14[v12] = f0(v14[v12] ^ v14[v16], 12)
    v14[v15] = (v14[v15] + v14[v12]) & v0
    v14[v17] = f0(v14[v17] ^ v14[v15], 8)

# The ChaCha20 block function of RFC 8439 2.3 on words: 8 key words, the
# 32-bit counter, 3 nonce words; 16 output words.

        v20.push(v5[v13])
    v20.push(v18 & v0)
    for v13 in 0..3
        v20.push(v19[v13])

        f2(&mut v10, 1, 5, 9, 13)
        f2(&mut v10, 2, 6, 10, 14)
        f2(&mut v10, 3, 7, 11, 15)
        f2(&mut v10, 0, 5, 10, 15)
        f2(&mut v10, 1, 6, 11, 12)
        f2(&mut v10, 2, 7, 8, 13)
        f2(&mut v10, 3, 4, 9, 14)

        v23.push((v14 >> 8) & 255)
        v23.push((v14 >> 16) & 255)
        v23.push((v14 >> 24) & 255)

    let v25 = f4(v19)
    let v22 = f3(&v24, v18, &v25)
    return f5(&v22)

    var v21: List[i64] = []
    var v27: List[i64] = []
    var v28 = v18
    var v13: usize = 0

        if v13 % 64 == 0
            v27 = f6(v5, v28, v19)
            v28 += 1
        v21.push(v10 ^ v27[v13 % 64])
        v13 += 1

# with the capability that came with them.
pub fn f9(_v30: Cap[t0], v29: &[i64], v6: i64) -> t1 ! x0 = f8(v29, v6)

pub fn f10(v29: &[i64], v6: i64) -> t1 ! x0 = f8(v29, v6)

    v31.v8 = f3(&v31.v5, v31.v7 & v0, &v19)
    v31.v7 += 1
    v31.v9 = 0

# The next 32-bit word of the stream, 0 .. 2^32 - 1.
pub fn f12(v31: &mut t1) -> i64
    if v31.v9 >= 16
        f11(v31)
    let v14 = v31.v8[v31.v9 as usize]
    v31.v9 += 1
    return v14

pub fn f13(v31: &mut t1, v32: i64) -> i64
    if v32 <= 0
        return 0
    if v32 <= 32
        return f12(v31) >> (32 - v32)
    let v4 = f12(v31) >> (64 - v32)
    let v3 = f12(v31)
    return (v4 << 32) | v3

    var v14 = v10

        v11 += 1
    return v11

pub fn f15(v31: &mut t1, v11: i64) -> i64 ! x1

        fail x1(v3: 0, v4: v11)
    let v32 = f14(v11 - 1)
    var v14 = f13(v31, v32)
    while v14 >= v11 bound 256
        v14 = f13(v31, v32)
    return v14

pub fn f16(v31: &mut t1, v3: i64, v4: i64) -> i64 ! x1
    if v4 < v3 or v4 - v3 >= 4611686018427387904
        fail x1(v3: v3, v4: v4)
    let v14 = try f15(v31, v4 - v3 + 1)
    return v3 + v14

# the keystream bytes, little endian).
pub fn f17(v31: &mut t1, v11: i64) -> List[i64]
    var v23: List[i64] = []
    var v22: i64 = 0
    for v13 in 0..v11

            v22 = f12(v31)
        v23.push((v22 >> (8 * (v13 % 4))) & 255)
    return v23

pub fn f18(v31: &mut t1, v33: &mut List[i64])
    var v13 = v33.v2() as i64 - 1

        let v34 = f15(v31, v13 + 1) catch 0
        let v35 = v33[v13 as usize]
        v33[v13 as usize] = v33[v34 as usize]
        v33[v34 as usize] = v35
        v13 -= 1

# stream id. The parent advances by 8 words.
pub fn f19(v31: &mut t1, v6: i64) -> t1 ! x0
    let v29 = f17(v31, 32)
    return f8(&v29, v6)

module rand.det

# Deterministic random streams (survey M12). A generator is the RFC 8439
# ChaCha20 keystream under a 32-byte seed, so a run replays bit for bit
# from its seed. The library draws no entropy: fresh seed bytes enter a
# program as a logged host result, and `from_entropy` takes them only
# together with a `Cap[Entropy]` (5.16), which a program holds only while
# handling an event that carries it. `from_seed` is for seeds that are
# already part of the program or its log (test vectors, replays, a value
# split from another generator). Not for keys: this is reference code and
# not constant time; key material comes straight from logged Random bytes.
#
# Stream: key = the 32 seed bytes; nonce = stream id (bytes 0..7, little
# endian) followed by 4 zero bytes; block counter starts at 0. Blocks past
# 2^32 carry into the third nonce word, so for counters below 2^32 the
# output is exactly the RFC 8439 keystream. Words are taken in order and
# serialise little endian. Bytes are List[i64] with values 0..255; words
# are i64 masked to 32 bits.

const M32: i64 = 4294967295

# The authority to seed from fresh entropy. A host grants it by putting a
# Cap[Entropy] in the event that delivers the Random bytes.
pub struct Entropy
    source: text

error BadSeed(len: i64)
error BadRange(lo: i64, hi: i64)

pub struct Rng
    key: List[i64]
    stream: i64
    block: i64
    buf: List[i64]
    pos: i64

fn rotl32(x: i64, n: i64) -> i64 = ((x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))) & M32

fn le32(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64 = b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8) | (b[i + 2] << 16) | (b[i + 3] << 24)

pub fn quarter(v: &mut List[i64], a: usize, b: usize, c: usize, d: usize)
    v[a] = (v[a] + v[b]) & M32
    v[d] = rotl32(v[d] ^ v[a], 16)
    v[c] = (v[c] + v[d]) & M32
    v[b] = rotl32(v[b] ^ v[c], 12)
    v[a] = (v[a] + v[b]) & M32
    v[d] = rotl32(v[d] ^ v[a], 8)
    v[c] = (v[c] + v[d]) & M32
    v[b] = rotl32(v[b] ^ v[c], 7)

# The ChaCha20 block function of RFC 8439 2.3 on words: 8 key words, the
# 32-bit counter, 3 nonce words; 16 output words.
pub fn block_words(key: &[i64], counter: i64, nonce: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var s: List[i64] = [1634760805, 857760878, 2036477234, 1797285236]
    for i in 0..8
        s.push(key[i])
    s.push(counter & M32)
    for i in 0..3
        s.push(nonce[i])
    var x = copy(s)
    for _ in 0..10
        quarter(&mut x, 0, 4, 8, 12)
        quarter(&mut x, 1, 5, 9, 13)
        quarter(&mut x, 2, 6, 10, 14)
        quarter(&mut x, 3, 7, 11, 15)
        quarter(&mut x, 0, 5, 10, 15)
        quarter(&mut x, 1, 6, 11, 12)
        quarter(&mut x, 2, 7, 8, 13)
        quarter(&mut x, 3, 4, 9, 14)
    var out: List[i64] = []
    for i in 0..16
        out.push((x[i] + s[i]) & M32)
    return out

fn words_le(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var w: List[i64] = []
    for i in 0..(b.len() / 4)
        w.push(le32(b, 4 * i))
    return w

fn bytes_le(w: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for v in w
        o.push(v & 255)
        o.push((v >> 8) & 255)
        o.push((v >> 16) & 255)
        o.push((v >> 24) & 255)
    return o

# RFC 8439 2.3 on bytes: 32-byte key, counter, 12-byte nonce; 64 bytes.
pub fn chacha20_block(key: &[i64], counter: i64, nonce: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    let kw = words_le(key)
    let nw = words_le(nonce)
    let w = block_words(&kw, counter, &nw)
    return bytes_le(&w)

# RFC 8439 2.4: XOR data with the keystream from the initial counter.
pub fn chacha20(key: &[i64], counter: i64, nonce: &[i64], data: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var out: List[i64] = []
    var ks: List[i64] = []
    var ctr = counter
    var i: usize = 0
    for x in data
        if i % 64 == 0
            ks = chacha20_block(key, ctr, nonce)
            ctr += 1
        out.push(x ^ ks[i % 64])
        i += 1
    return out

fn make(seed: &[i64], stream: i64) -> Rng ! BadSeed
    if seed.len() != 32 or stream < 0
        fail BadSeed(len: seed.len() as i64)
    for b in seed
        if b < 0 or b > 255
            fail BadSeed(len: seed.len() as i64)
    return Rng(key: words_le(seed), stream: stream, block: 0, buf: [], pos: 16)

# A generator from fresh entropy: 32 logged Random bytes, admitted only
# with the capability that came with them.
pub fn from_entropy(_c: Cap[Entropy], seed: &[i64], stream: i64) -> Rng ! BadSeed = make(seed, stream)

# A generator from a seed already in the program or its log.
pub fn from_seed(seed: &[i64], stream: i64) -> Rng ! BadSeed = make(seed, stream)

fn refill(r: &mut Rng)
    let nonce = [r.stream & M32, r.stream >> 32, r.block >> 32]
    r.buf = block_words(&r.key, r.block & M32, &nonce)
    r.block += 1
    r.pos = 0

# The next 32-bit word of the stream, 0 .. 2^32 - 1.
pub fn next_u32(r: &mut Rng) -> i64
    if r.pos >= 16
        refill(r)
    let v = r.buf[r.pos as usize]
    r.pos += 1
    return v

# k uniform bits, 0 <= k <= 62 (one word for k <= 32, else two, high first).
pub fn bits(r: &mut Rng, k: i64) -> i64
    if k <= 0
        return 0
    if k <= 32
        return next_u32(r) >> (32 - k)
    let hi = next_u32(r) >> (64 - k)
    let lo = next_u32(r)
    return (hi << 32) | lo

fn bitlen(x: i64) -> i64
    var n: i64 = 0
    var v = x
    while v > 0 bound 64
        v = v >> 1
        n += 1
    return n

# Uniform in 0 .. n - 1 for 1 <= n <= 2^62, by masked rejection (no
# modulo bias). n = 1 draws nothing.
pub fn below(r: &mut Rng, n: i64) -> i64 ! BadRange
    if n < 1 or n > 4611686018427387904

    if hi < lo or hi - lo >= 4611686018427387904

# the keystream bytes, little endian).

        xs[j as usize] = t
        i -= 1

# stream id. The parent advances by 8 words.
pub fn split(r: &mut Rng, stream: i64) -> Rng ! BadSeed
    let seed = bytes(r, 32)
    return make(&seed, stream)

module text.utf8

# UTF-8 (survey M9, first part): validation, decoding to code points,
# lossy decoding with U+FFFD, encoding, and code-point / UTF-16 views of
# text. Well-formedness is Unicode Table 3-7 (no overlongs, no surrogates,
# nothing above U+10FFFF). Lossy decoding replaces each maximal subpart of
# an ill-formed sequence with one U+FFFD (Unicode 3.9, "Best Practices for
# U+FFFD Substitution"; the WHATWG Encoding Standard behaviour).
# Bytes are List[i64] 0..255 (core.bytes). Normalization, grapheme
# clusters and case folding need a pinned UCD and building text from code
# points; see vectors/SOURCE.md (needs spec).

pub const REPLACEMENT: i64 = 65533

# Allowed range of the second byte after lead byte x, as [lo, hi, len];
# len 0 marks a byte that cannot start a sequence.
fn lead_info(x: i64) -> List[i64]
    if x < 128
        return [0, 0, 1]
    if x >= 194 and x <= 223
        return [128, 191, 2]
    if x == 224
        return [160, 191, 3]
    if x == 237
        return [128, 159, 3]
    if x >= 225 and x <= 239
        return [128, 191, 3]
    if x == 240
        return [144, 191, 4]
    if x >= 241 and x <= 243
        return [128, 191, 4]
    if x == 244
        return [128, 143, 4]
    return [0, 0, 0]

# Length of the well-formed sequence at i, or minus the length of the
# maximal subpart to replace (at least 1) when ill-formed.
pub fn utf8_seq_at(b: &[i64], i: usize) -> i64
    let li = lead_info(b[i])
    let n = li[2]
    if n == 1
        return 1
    if n == 0
        return -1
    var k: i64 = 1
    while k < n bound 4
        let j = i + (k as usize)
        if j >= b.len()
            return 0 - k
        let x = b[j]
        let lo = if k == 1 then li[0] else 128
        let hi = if k == 1 then li[1] else 191
        if x < lo or x > hi
            return 0 - k
        k += 1
    return n

fn cp_at(b: &[i64], i: usize, n: i64) -> i64
    if n == 1
        return b[i]
    if n == 2
        return ((b[i] & 31) << 6) | (b[i + 1] & 63)
    if n == 3
        return ((b[i] & 15) << 12) | ((b[i + 1] & 63) << 6) | (b[i + 2] & 63)
    return ((b[i] & 7) << 18) | ((b[i + 1] & 63) << 12) | ((b[i + 2] & 63) << 6) | (b[i + 3] & 63)

# Byte offset of the first ill-formed sequence, or -1 when well-formed.
pub fn utf8_first_error(b: &[i64]) -> i64
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < b.len() bound 67108864
        let n = utf8_seq_at(b, i)
        if n <= 0
            return i as i64
        i += n as usize
    return -1

pub fn utf8_valid(b: &[i64]) -> bool = utf8_first_error(b) < 0

error BadUtf8(at: i64)

pub fn utf8_decode(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64] ! BadUtf8
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < b.len() bound 67108864
        let n = utf8_seq_at(b, i)
        if n <= 0
            fail BadUtf8(at: i as i64)
        o.push(cp_at(b, i, n))
        i += n as usize
    return o

pub fn utf8_decode_lossy(b: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < b.len() bound 67108864
        let n = utf8_seq_at(b, i)
        if n > 0
            o.push(cp_at(b, i, n))
            i += n as usize
        else
            o.push(REPLACEMENT)
            i += (0 - n) as usize
    return o

pub fn is_scalar(cp: i64) -> bool = cp >= 0 and cp <= 1114111 and (cp < 55296 or cp > 57343)

pub fn utf8_encode_cp(o: &mut List[i64], cp: i64)
    let _ok = 1 / (if is_scalar(cp) then 1 else 0)
    if cp < 128
        o.push(cp)
    elif cp < 2048
        o.push(192 | (cp >> 6))
        o.push(128 | (cp & 63))
    elif cp < 65536
        o.push(224 | (cp >> 12))
        o.push(128 | ((cp >> 6) & 63))
        o.push(128 | (cp & 63))
    else
        o.push(240 | (cp >> 18))
        o.push(128 | ((cp >> 12) & 63))
        o.push(128 | ((cp >> 6) & 63))
        o.push(128 | (cp & 63))

# Encode Unicode scalar values; a surrogate or value out of range traps.
pub fn utf8_encode(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        utf8_encode_cp(&mut o, c)
    return o

pub fn text_bytes(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        o.push(t[i] as i64)
        i += 1
    return o

# Code points of a text (text is always well-formed UTF-8).
pub fn codepoints(t: &text) -> List[i64]
    let b = text_bytes(t)
    return utf8_decode_lossy(&b)

pub fn cp_count(t: &text) -> i64
    var n: i64 = 0
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < t.len_bytes() bound 67108864
        let x = t[i] as i64
        if x < 128 or x >= 192
            n += 1
        i += 1
    return n

pub fn utf16_of_cps(cps: &[i64]) -> List[i64]
    var o: List[i64] = []
    for c in cps
        if c >= 65536
            o.push(55296 + ((c - 65536) >> 10))
            o.push(56320 + ((c - 65536) & 1023))
        else
            o.push(c)
    return o

error BadUtf16(at: i64)

# UTF-16 code units to code points; unpaired surrogates fail.
pub fn utf16_decode(u: &[i64]) -> List[i64] ! BadUtf16
    var o: List[i64] = []
    var i: usize = 0
    while i < u.len() bound 67108864
        let x = u[i]
        if x >= 55296 and x <= 56319
            if i + 1 >= u.len() or u[i + 1] < 56320 or u[i + 1] > 57343
                fail BadUtf16(at: i as i64)
            o.push(65536 + ((x - 55296) << 10) + (u[i + 1] - 56320))
            i += 2
        elif x >= 56320 and x <= 57343
            fail BadUtf16(at: i as i64)
        else
            o.push(x)
            i += 1
    return o

module time

# Time as a logged input (survey M10). There is no clock here: an instant
# is a number a program received in an event (a Tick, a host.WallTime
# result), and every function is pure arithmetic on it, so replay is exact.
# Instant: i64 nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the POSIX
# timescale (no leap seconds; 23:59:60 is refused on parse). Duration: i64
# nanoseconds. Range: about years 1678..2261 for instants; day-level civil
# functions work on any i64 day count that fits. Overflow traps (checked
# integers). Civil dates are proleptic Gregorian, from Howard Hinnant's
# "chrono-Compatible Low-Level Date Algorithms" (days_from_civil,
# civil_from_days, weekday_from_days). Time zones need tz data as a logged
# or pinned input (see vectors/SOURCE.md); only fixed UTC offsets here.
pub const v0: i64 = 1
pub const v1: i64 = 1000
pub const v2: i64 = 1000000
pub const v3: i64 = 1000000000
pub const v4: i64 = 60000000000
pub const v5: i64 = 3600000000000
pub const v6: i64 = 86400000000000

pub struct t0
    v7: i64
    v8: i64
    v9: i64

# floor division and modulo for possibly negative a, b > 0
pub fn f0(v10: i64, v11: i64) -> i64 = if v10 >= 0 then v10 / v11 else 0 - ((0 - v10 - 1) / v11) - 1

pub fn f1(v10: i64, v11: i64) -> i64 = v10 - f0(v10, v11) * v11

# Days since 1970-01-01 of a proleptic Gregorian date (Hinnant).
pub fn f2(v12: i64, v8: i64, v9: i64) -> i64
    let v7 = if v8 <= 2 then v12 - 1 else v12
    let v13 = f0(v7, 400)
    let v14 = v7 - v13 * 400
    let v15 = if v8 > 2 then v8 - 3 else v8 + 9
    let v16 = (153 * v15 + 2) / 5 + v9 - 1
    let v17 = v14 * 365 + v14 / 4 - v14 / 100 + v16
    return v13 * 146097 + v17 - 719468

pub fn f3(v18: i64) -> t0
    let v19 = v18 + 719468
    let v13 = f0(v19, 146097)
    let v17 = v19 - v13 * 146097
    let v14 = (v17 - v17 / 1460 + v17 / 36524 - v17 / 146096) / 365
    let v16 = v17 - (365 * v14 + v14 / 4 - v14 / 100)
    let v15 = (5 * v16 + 2) / 153
    let v9 = v16 - (153 * v15 + 2) / 5 + 1
    let v8 = if v15 < 10 then v15 + 3 else v15 - 9
    let v7 = v14 + v13 * 400 + (if v8 <= 2 then 1 else 0)
    return t0(v7: v7, v8: v8, v9: v9)

# 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday
pub fn f4(v19: i64) -> i64 = if v19 >= -4 then (v19 + 4) % 7 else (v19 + 5) % 7 + 6

pub fn f5(v7: i64) -> bool = f1(v7, 4) == 0 and (f1(v7, 100) != 0 or f1(v7, 400) == 0)

pub fn f6(v7: i64, v8: i64) -> i64
    if v8 == 2
        return if f5(v7) then 29 else 28
    if v8 == 4 or v8 == 6 or v8 == 9 or v8 == 11
        return 30
    return 31

pub fn f7(v7: i64, v8: i64, v9: i64) -> bool = v8 >= 1 and v8 <= 12 and v9 >= 1 and v9 <= f6(v7, v8)

# Day of year, 1-based.
pub fn f8(v7: i64, v8: i64, v9: i64) -> i64 = f2(v7, v8, v9) - f2(v7, 1, 1) + 1

# Add calendar months; the day is clamped to the end of the target month
# (2024-01-31 + 1 month = 2024-02-29).
pub fn f9(v20: &t0, v21: i64) -> t0
    let v22 = v20.v7 * 12 + (v20.v8 - 1) + v21
    let v7 = f0(v22, 12)
    let v8 = f1(v22, 12) + 1
    let v23 = f6(v7, v8)
    return t0(v7: v7, v8: v8, v9: if v20.v9 > v23 then v23 else v20.v9)

# ISO 8601 week date: [iso_year, week 1..53, weekday 1 = Monday .. 7].
pub fn f10(v7: i64, v8: i64, v9: i64) -> List[i64]
    let v19 = f2(v7, v8, v9)
    let v24 = f1(f4(v19) + 6, 7) + 1
    let v25 = v19 + 4 - v24
    let v26 = f3(v25).v7
    let v27 = (v25 - f2(v26, 1, 1)) / 7 + 1
    return [v26, v27, v24]

# ---------------- instants and durations ----------------
pub fn f11(v7: i64, v28: i64, v9: i64, v29: i64, v30: i64, v31: i64, v32: i64) -> i64 = f2(v7, v28, v9) * v6 + v29 * v5 + v30 * v4 + v31 * v3 + v32

pub fn f12(v22: i64) -> i64 = f0(v22, v6)

pub fn f13(v22: i64) -> i64 = f1(v22, v6)

pub fn f14(v29: i64, v8: i64, v31: i64, v32: i64) -> i64 = v29 * v5 + v8 * v4 + v31 * v3 + v32

# Truncate an instant to a multiple of unit (floor, also before 1970).
pub fn f15(v22: i64, v33: i64) -> i64 = f0(v22, v33) * v33

fn f16(v34: i64, v27: i64) -> text
    var v31 = v34.tostr()
    while (v31.len_bytes() as i64) < v27 bound 20
        v31 = "0" + v31
    return v31

fn f17(v7: i64) -> text
    if v7 < 0
        return "-" + f16(0 - v7, 4)
    return f16(v7, 4)

# RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 text with a fixed offset in minutes (0 prints "Z");
# fraction digits: 0, 3, 6 or 9 (truncated, not rounded).
pub fn f18(v22: i64, v35: i64, v36: i64) -> text
    let v37 = v22 + v35 * v4
    let v20 = f3(f12(v37))
    let v38 = f13(v37)
    let v29 = v38 / v5
    let v30 = (v38 / v4) % 60
    let v31 = (v38 / v3) % 60
    var v39 = f17(v20.v7) + "-" + f16(v20.v8, 2) + "-" + f16(v20.v9, 2) + "T" + f16(v29, 2) + ":" + f16(v30, 2) + ":" + f16(v31, 2)
    if v36 > 0
        var v40 = v38 % v3
        var v41: i64 = 9
        while v41 > v36 bound 9
            v40 = v40 / 10
            v41 -= 1
        v39 = v39 + "." + f16(v40, v36)
    if v35 == 0
        return v39 + "Z"
    let v10 = if v35 < 0 then 0 - v35 else v35
    return v39 + (if v35 < 0 then "-" else "+") + f16(v10 / 60, 2) + ":" + f16(v10 % 60, 2)

error x0(v42: i64)

fn f19(v31: &text, v42: usize, v21: usize) -> i64 ! x0
    if v42 + v21 > v31.len_bytes()
        fail x0(v42: v42 as i64)
    var v34: i64 = 0
    for v41 in 0..v21
        let v20 = (v31[v42 + v41] as i64) - 48
        if v20 < 0 or v20 > 9
            fail x0(v42: (v42 + v41) as i64)
        v34 = v34 * 10 + v20
    return v34

fn f20(v31: &text, v42: usize, v20: i64) -> bool ! x0
    if v42 >= v31.len_bytes() or (v31[v42] as i64) != v20
        fail x0(v42: v42 as i64)
    return true

# Parse RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.6): YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.frac](Z|+HH:MM|-HH:MM),
# 'T'/'t' and 'Z'/'z' accepted; at most 9 fraction digits; second 60
# (leap second) is refused because instants are POSIX time.
pub fn f21(v31: &text) -> i64 ! x0
    let v7 = try f19(v31, 0, 4)
    let _ = try f20(v31, 4, 45)
    let v28 = try f19(v31, 5, 2)
    let _ = try f20(v31, 7, 45)
    let v9 = try f19(v31, 8, 2)
    if not f7(v7, v28, v9)
        fail x0(v42: 5)
    if v31.len_bytes() < 11 or ((v31[10] as i64) != 84 and (v31[10] as i64) != 116)
        fail x0(v42: 10)
    let v29 = try f19(v31, 11, 2)
    let _ = try f20(v31, 13, 58)
    let v30 = try f19(v31, 14, 2)
    let _ = try f20(v31, 16, 58)
    let v43 = try f19(v31, 17, 2)
    if v29 > 23 or v30 > 59 or v43 > 59
        fail x0(v42: 11)

module time

# Time as a logged input (survey M10). There is no clock here: an instant
# is a number a program received in an event (a Tick, a host.WallTime
# result), and every function is pure arithmetic on it, so replay is exact.
# Instant: i64 nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the POSIX
# timescale (no leap seconds; 23:59:60 is refused on parse). Duration: i64
# nanoseconds. Range: about years 1678..2261 for instants; day-level civil
# functions work on any i64 day count that fits. Overflow traps (checked
# integers). Civil dates are proleptic Gregorian, from Howard Hinnant's
# "chrono-Compatible Low-Level Date Algorithms" (days_from_civil,
# civil_from_days, weekday_from_days). Time zones need tz data as a logged
# or pinned input (see vectors/SOURCE.md); only fixed UTC offsets here.

pub const NS: i64 = 1
pub const US: i64 = 1000
pub const MS: i64 = 1000000
pub const SEC: i64 = 1000000000
pub const MINUTE: i64 = 60000000000
pub const HOUR: i64 = 3600000000000
pub const DAY: i64 = 86400000000000

pub struct Civil
    y: i64
    m: i64
    d: i64

# floor division and modulo for possibly negative a, b > 0
pub fn fdiv(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = if a >= 0 then a / b else 0 - ((0 - a - 1) / b) - 1

pub fn fmod(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a - fdiv(a, b) * b

# Days since 1970-01-01 of a proleptic Gregorian date (Hinnant).
pub fn days_from_civil(y0: i64, m: i64, d: i64) -> i64
    let y = if m <= 2 then y0 - 1 else y0
    let era = fdiv(y, 400)
    let yoe = y - era * 400
    let mp = if m > 2 then m - 3 else m + 9
    let doy = (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + d - 1
    let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy
    return era * 146097 + doe - 719468

pub fn civil_from_days(z0: i64) -> Civil
    let z = z0 + 719468
    let era = fdiv(z, 146097)
    let doe = z - era * 146097
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100)
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153
    let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1
    let m = if mp < 10 then mp + 3 else mp - 9
    let y = yoe + era * 400 + (if m <= 2 then 1 else 0)
    return Civil(y: y, m: m, d: d)

# 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday
pub fn weekday_from_days(z: i64) -> i64 = if z >= -4 then (z + 4) % 7 else (z + 5) % 7 + 6

pub fn is_leap(y: i64) -> bool = fmod(y, 4) == 0 and (fmod(y, 100) != 0 or fmod(y, 400) == 0)

pub fn days_in_month(y: i64, m: i64) -> i64
    if m == 2
        return if is_leap(y) then 29 else 28
    if m == 4 or m == 6 or m == 9 or m == 11
        return 30
    return 31

pub fn valid_civil(y: i64, m: i64, d: i64) -> bool = m >= 1 and m <= 12 and d >= 1 and d <= days_in_month(y, m)

# Day of year, 1-based.
pub fn ordinal_day(y: i64, m: i64, d: i64) -> i64 = days_from_civil(y, m, d) - days_from_civil(y, 1, 1) + 1

# Add calendar months; the day is clamped to the end of the target month
# (2024-01-31 + 1 month = 2024-02-29).
pub fn add_months(c: &Civil, n: i64) -> Civil
    let t = c.y * 12 + (c.m - 1) + n
    let y = fdiv(t, 12)
    let m = fmod(t, 12) + 1
    let dim = days_in_month(y, m)
    return Civil(y: y, m: m, d: if c.d > dim then dim else c.d)

# ISO 8601 week date: [iso_year, week 1..53, weekday 1 = Monday .. 7].
pub fn iso_week(y: i64, m: i64, d: i64) -> List[i64]
    let z = days_from_civil(y, m, d)
    let wd = fmod(weekday_from_days(z) + 6, 7) + 1
    let th = z + 4 - wd
    let ty = civil_from_days(th).y
    let w = (th - days_from_civil(ty, 1, 1)) / 7 + 1
    return [ty, w, wd]

# ---------------- instants and durations ----------------

pub fn instant_of(y: i64, mo: i64, d: i64, h: i64, mi: i64, s: i64, ns: i64) -> i64 = days_from_civil(y, mo, d) * DAY + h * HOUR + mi * MINUTE + s * SEC + ns

pub fn days_of(t: i64) -> i64 = fdiv(t, DAY)

pub fn ns_of_day(t: i64) -> i64 = fmod(t, DAY)

pub fn dur_of(h: i64, m: i64, s: i64, ns: i64) -> i64 = h * HOUR + m * MINUTE + s * SEC + ns

# Truncate an instant to a multiple of unit (floor, also before 1970).
pub fn floor_to(t: i64, unit: i64) -> i64 = fdiv(t, unit) * unit

fn pad(v: i64, w: i64) -> text
    var s = v.tostr()
    while (s.len_bytes() as i64) < w bound 20
        s = "0" + s
    return s

fn year_text(y: i64) -> text
    if y < 0
        return "-" + pad(0 - y, 4)
    return pad(y, 4)

# RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 text with a fixed offset in minutes (0 prints "Z");
# fraction digits: 0, 3, 6 or 9 (truncated, not rounded).
pub fn format_rfc3339(t: i64, offset_min: i64, frac: i64) -> text
    let lt = t + offset_min * MINUTE
    let c = civil_from_days(days_of(lt))
    let nd = ns_of_day(lt)
    let h = nd / HOUR
    let mi = (nd / MINUTE) % 60
    let s = (nd / SEC) % 60
    var out = year_text(c.y) + "-" + pad(c.m, 2) + "-" + pad(c.d, 2) + "T" + pad(h, 2) + ":" + pad(mi, 2) + ":" + pad(s, 2)
    if frac > 0
        var f = nd % SEC
        var k: i64 = 9
        while k > frac bound 9
            f = f / 10
            k -= 1
        out = out + "." + pad(f, frac)
    if offset_min == 0
        return out + "Z"
    let a = if offset_min < 0 then 0 - offset_min else offset_min
    return out + (if offset_min < 0 then "-" else "+") + pad(a / 60, 2) + ":" + pad(a % 60, 2)

error BadTime(at: i64)

fn digits(s: &text, at: usize, n: usize) -> i64 ! BadTime
    if at + n > s.len_bytes()
        fail BadTime(at: at as i64)
    var v: i64 = 0
    for k in 0..n
        let c = (s[at + k] as i64) - 48
        if c < 0 or c > 9
            fail BadTime(at: (at + k) as i64)
        v = v * 10 + c
    return v

fn expect(s: &text, at: usize, c: i64) -> bool ! BadTime
    if at >= s.len_bytes() or (s[at] as i64) != c
        fail BadTime(at: at as i64)
    return true

# Parse RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.6): YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.frac](Z|+HH:MM|-HH:MM),
# 'T'/'t' and 'Z'/'z' accepted; at most 9 fraction digits; second 60
# (leap second) is refused because instants are POSIX time.
pub fn parse_rfc3339(s: &text) -> i64 ! BadTime
    let y = try digits(s, 0, 4)
    let _ = try expect(s, 4, 45)
    let mo = try digits(s, 5, 2)
    let _ = try expect(s, 7, 45)
    let d = try digits(s, 8, 2)
    if not valid_civil(y, mo, d)
        fail BadTime(at: 5)
    if s.len_bytes() < 11 or ((s[10] as i64) != 84 and (s[10] as i64) != 116)
        fail BadTime(at: 10)
    let h = try digits(s, 11, 2)
    let _ = try expect(s, 13, 58)
    let mi = try digits(s, 14, 2)
    let _ = try expect(s, 16, 58)
    let sec = try digits(s, 17, 2)
    if h > 23 or mi > 59 or sec > 59
        fail BadTime(at: 11)
    var i: usize = 19
    var ns: i64 = 0
    if i < s.len_bytes() and (s[i] as i64) == 46
        i += 1
        var k: i64 = 0
        while i < s.len_bytes() and (s[i] as i64) >= 48 and (s[i] as i64) <= 57 bound 32
            if k >= 9
                fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
            ns = ns * 10 + (s[i] as i64) - 48
            k += 1
            i += 1
        if k == 0
            fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
        while k < 9 bound 9
            ns = ns * 10
            k += 1
    if i >= s.len_bytes()
        fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
    let z = s[i] as i64
    var off: i64 = 0
    if z == 90 or z == 122
        i += 1
    elif z == 43 or z == 45
        let oh = try digits(s, i + 1, 2)
        let _ = try expect(s, i + 3, 58)
        let om = try digits(s, i + 4, 2)
        if oh > 23 or om > 59
            fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
        off = oh * 60 + om
        if z == 45
            off = 0 - off
        i += 6
    else
        fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
    if i != s.len_bytes()
        fail BadTime(at: i as i64)
    return instant_of(y, mo, d, h, mi, sec, ns) - off * MINUTE

# A tree of expressions and statements: eval and run call each other on
# components; run also passes its environment on unchanged.
kind E
    Num(v: i64)
    Add(a: Box[E], b: Box[E])
    Blk(s: Box[S])

kind S
    Ret(e: Box[E])
    Seq(x: Box[E], rest: Box[S])

fn eval(e: &E, k: i64) -> i64
    match e
        Num(v: v) -> return v + k
        Add(a: a, b: b) -> return eval(a, k) + eval(b, k)
        Blk(s: s) -> return run(s, k)

fn run(s: &S, k: i64) -> i64
    match s
        Ret(e: e) -> return eval(e, k)

kind N
    Z
    S(p: Box[N])

fn ack(m: &N, n: &N) -> i64
    match m
        Z -> return 1
        S(p: q)

                S(p: r) -> return ack(q, n) + ack(m, r)

fn two(a: &N, b: &N) -> i64
    match a
        Z -> return 0
        S(p: x)
            match b
                Z -> return two(x, b)
                S(p: y) -> return 1 + two(a, y) + two(x, b)

    let two_ = S(p: Box(S(p: Box(Z))))

module media

intent "media capture and playback: each Tick reads one frame from the open track; D logs only (track, seq, digest) and the frame's Tick, the frame bytes stay a blob addressed by digest; every captured frame is played back to the sink by digest"
    example Open(source: "pattern:2"), MediaOpenDone(req: 1, status: "delivered", data: some(1), err: "") -> track == 1

struct MediaOpen
    req: u64
    source: text

struct MediaRead
    req: u64
    id: u64

struct MediaPlay
    req: u64
    track: text
    digest: text

event Open(source: text)
event Tick(n: u64)
event MediaOpenDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event MediaReadDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)
event MediaPlayDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)

state Call
    next: u64 = 0
    track: u64 = 0
    tick: u64 = 0
    ended: bool = false
    frames: List[text] = []
    played: u64 = 0
    bytes: u64 = 0
    errors: u64 = 0

step Call on Open(source: s)
    next += 1
    emit MediaOpen(req: next, source: s)

step Call on MediaOpenDone(req: _r, status: st, data: d, err: _e)
    if st == "delivered"
        track = d.or(0)
    else
        errors += 1

step Call on Tick(n: n)
    tick = n
    if track > 0 and not ended
        next += 1
        emit MediaRead(req: next, id: track)

# a frame: "track/seq/digest@tick"; the bytes are never in state or D
step Call on MediaReadDone(req: _r, status: st, data: d, err: e)
    if st == "delivered"
        let f = d.or("").split(":")
        frames.push(track.tostr() + "/" + copy(f[0]) + "/" + copy(f[1]) + "@" + tick.tostr())
        next += 1
        emit MediaPlay(req: next, track: "loopback", digest: copy(f[1]))
    else
        if e == "eof"
            ended = true
        else
            errors += 1

step Call on MediaPlayDone(req: _r, status: st, data: d, err: _e)
    if st == "delivered"
        played += 1
        bytes += d.or(0)
    else
        errors += 1

module netecho

intent "TCP, random bytes and blobs as effects: each request has one logged result"
    example Listen(addr: "127.0.0.1:1"), NetListenDone(req: 1, status: "failed", data: none, err: "x") -> errors == 1

struct NetListen
    req: u64
    addr: text

struct NetConnect
    req: u64
    addr: text

struct NetAccept
    req: u64
    id: u64

struct NetSend
    req: u64
    id: u64
    data: text

struct NetRecv
    req: u64
    id: u64
    max: u64

struct NetClose
    req: u64
    id: u64

struct Random
    req: u64
    n: u64

struct BlobPut
    req: u64
    data: text

struct BlobGet
    req: u64
    digest: text

event Listen(addr: text)
event Connect(addr: text)
event Accept(id: u64)
event Send(id: u64, data: text)
event Recv(id: u64)
event Close(id: u64)
event Roll(n: u64)
event Put(data: text)
event Get(digest: text)
event NetListenDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event NetConnectDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event NetAcceptDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event NetSendDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event NetRecvDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)
event NetCloseDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event RandomDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)
event BlobPutDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)
event BlobGetDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)

state Net
    next: u64 = 0
    last: u64 = 0
    got: text = ""
    rand: text = ""
    digest: text = ""
    blob: text = ""
    errors: u64 = 0

step Net on Listen(addr: a)
    next += 1
    emit NetListen(req: next, addr: a)

step Net on Connect(addr: a)
    next += 1
    emit NetConnect(req: next, addr: a)

step Net on Accept(id: i)
    next += 1
    emit NetAccept(req: next, id: i)

step Net on Send(id: i, data: d)
    next += 1
    emit NetSend(req: next, id: i, data: d)

step Net on Recv(id: i)
    next += 1
    emit NetRecv(req: next, id: i, max: 4096)

step Net on Close(id: i)
    next += 1
    emit NetClose(req: next, id: i)

step Net on Roll(n: n)
    next += 1
    emit Random(req: next, n: n)

step Net on Put(data: d)
    next += 1
    emit BlobPut(req: next, data: d)

step Net on Get(digest: d)
    next += 1
    emit BlobGet(req: next, digest: d)

step Net on NetListenDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        last = d.or(0)
    else
        errors += 1

step Net on NetConnectDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        last = d.or(0)
    else
        errors += 1

step Net on NetAcceptDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        last = d.or(0)

step Net on NetSendDone(req: _r, status: s, data: _d, err: _e)
    if s != "delivered"
        errors += 1

step Net on NetRecvDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        got = got + d.or("")

step Net on NetCloseDone(req: _r, status: s, data: _d, err: _e)
    if s != "delivered"
        errors += 1

step Net on RandomDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: d, err: _e)
    rand = d.or("")

step Net on BlobPutDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: d, err: _e)
    digest = d.or("")

step Net on BlobGetDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        blob = d.or("")
    else
        errors += 1

module ptyecho

intent "a PTY session as effects: open, write, read until the echo arrives, close"
    example Start, PtyOpenDone(req: 1, status: "failed", data: none, err: "x") -> errors == 1

struct PtyOpen
    req: u64
    argv: List[text]
    rows: u64
    cols: u64

struct PtyWrite
    req: u64
    id: u64
    data: text

struct PtyRead
    req: u64
    id: u64
    max: u64

struct PtyClose
    req: u64
    id: u64

event Start
event Send(data: text)
event Poll
event Stop
event PtyOpenDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event PtyWriteDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)
event PtyReadDone(req: u64, status: text, data: text?, err: text)
event PtyCloseDone(req: u64, status: text, data: u64?, err: text)

state Term
    next: u64 = 0
    id: u64 = 0
    screen: text = ""
    errors: u64 = 0
    closed: bool = false

step Term on Start
    next += 1
    emit PtyOpen(req: next, argv: ["/bin/cat"], rows: 24, cols: 80)

step Term on Send(data: d)
    next += 1
    emit PtyWrite(req: next, id: id, data: d)

step Term on Poll
    next += 1
    emit PtyRead(req: next, id: id, max: 4096)

step Term on Stop
    next += 1
    emit PtyClose(req: next, id: id)

step Term on PtyOpenDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        id = d.or(0)
    else
        errors += 1

step Term on PtyWriteDone(req: _r, status: s, data: _d, err: _e)
    if s != "delivered"
        errors += 1

step Term on PtyReadDone(req: _r, status: s, data: d, err: _e)
    if s == "delivered"
        screen = screen + d.or("")
    else
        errors += 1

step Term on PtyCloseDone(req: _r, status: _s, data: _d, err: _e)
    closed = true

# Recursion on integers, which no constructor measure covers, admitted by
# a declared bound on the number of active calls (6.7).
fn gcd(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64 bound 100
    if b == 0
        return a
    return gcd(b, a % b)

fn collatz(n: u64) -> u64 bound 1000
    if n <= 1
        return 0
    if n % 2 == 0
        return 1 + collatz(n / 2)
    return 1 + collatz(3 * n + 1)

fn down(n: i64) -> i64 bound 5
    if n <= 0
        return 0
    return 1 + down(n - 1)

fn deep() -> i64
    return down(5)

check gcd(1071, 462) == 21
check collatz(27) == 111
check down(4) == 4
